institution: Taideyliopiston Sibelius-Akatemia / Sibelius Academy, University of the Arts Helsinki (Uniarts Helsinki)
programme: Music Technology, master (Musiikkiteknologia) — specialisation path RECORDING ARTS
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Master of Music (MMus), musiikin maisteri
accreditation: State university (Taideyliopisto / University of the Arts Helsinki), Sibelius Academy is its music faculty
tuition: EUR 0 IF STUDYING IN FINNISH OR SWEDISH. EUR 28,000 per academic year if studying in English, for students starting 1 August 2026 or later. THIS IS THE FINNISH-LANGUAGE LOOPHOLE THE BRIEF ASKED ABOUT AND IT IS REAL. Uniarts states VERBATIM: "Tuition fees at Uniarts Helsinki are applicable to bachelor and master students who study in English and who are not citizens of EU, EEA, or Switzerland" and "If a student’s language of studies changes to Finnish or Swedish, they will no longer have to pay annual tuition fees." Finnish national law only permits fees for vieraskielinen (foreign-language) degree education; Finnish- and Swedish-taught degrees are free of charge regardless of nationality. Music Technology is one of the very few Sibelius Academy programmes that formally offers Finnish, Swedish AND English as tuition languages, so the exemption is genuinely reachable here rather than theoretical.
otherFees: EUR 100 application fee for applicants from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland. Language test must be completed by the stated date if proficiency is not evidenced by prior studies.
totalCost: If admitted in Finnish/Swedish: EUR 0 tuition + EUR 100 application + Helsinki living costs (Finnish residence-permit maintenance requirement approx. EUR 800/month, UNVERIFIED 2027 figure) — roughly EUR 24,000 over 2.5 years, all living costs. If admitted in English: add EUR 70,000 tuition over 2.5 years with NO scholarship available.
scholarshipDetail: VERBATIM: "The university does not grant any scholarships to cover the tuition fee for students starting in August 2026 or later" and "Uniarts Helsinki does not grant scholarships for living expenses." The ONLY way to make this affordable is the Finnish/Swedish language exemption.
entry: VERBATIM: applicants need "at least one of the following: A lower university degree in music (Bachelor), a university of applied sciences degree in music, a foreign degree or qualification in music", or a non-music degree with supplementary music studies. Programme-specific clause VERBATIM: "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media is also applicable if you also have a sufficient amount of music studies."
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CONDITIONALLY, AND THIS IS THE BEST NON-MUSIC CLAUSE FOUND IN THE WHOLE REGION. QUOTE: "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media is also applicable if you also have a sufficient amount of music studies." A BSc Software Engineering is a higher education degree in the field of technology. The binding condition is "a sufficient amount of music studies", which is not quantified on the page (UNVERIFIED how many ECTS of music study count). This clause exists specifically because Music Technology expects engineers — it is a designed door for exactly this candidate profile, provided he accumulates formal music studies before applying.
portfolio: EXACT advance assignments: (1) Portfolio of MAXIMUM 3 WORKS, total length 10 MINUTES OR LESS, audio in MP3 or video in MP4 format. (2) Video self-presentation, 3 minutes or less. (3) Project description forms (PDF). (4) Motivation letter, max 2 A4 pages. (5) CV (PDF). (6) Final project plan, max 2 A4 pages. (7) Preliminary study plan (max 150 ECTS credits). Advance assignments are weighted 100%.
audition: THERE IS A PERFORMANCE AUDITION — this is the decisive distinction for this candidate and it counts AGAINST him. The remote examination has two parts: (1) "Instrument or voice audition (7-10 minutes) - any tradition welcome" weighted 40%; (2) "Interview (up to 25 minutes)" discussing portfolio, audition, background and plans, weighted 60%. So a live instrumental or vocal performance of 7-10 minutes IS required, although any musical tradition is accepted. NO ear-training or music-theory test is mentioned in the documentation. GOOD NEWS: the examination is REMOTE — no travel to Helsinki needed.
deadline: *** NO INTAKE IN 2027 *** VERBATIM from the programme page: "No admission in 2027. Next possible time to apply will be announced later." The programme admits every other year. The 2026 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE) ran: applications 7-21 January 2026 (by 15:00 EET); supporting documents and advance assignments 28 January 2026 (15:00 EET); language test completed by 2 March 2026; entrance exams 31 March - 1 April 2026 (REMOTE); results 10 April 2026; study place acceptance by 9 July 2026. Next master-only intake most likely 2028 — UNVERIFIED.
opens: 7 January 2026 for the 2026 cycle — PRIOR CYCLE. No 2027 cycle.
duration: 2.5 years (150 ECTS equivalent). Admits new students on ALTERNATING years — either a 5.5-year bachelor+master cohort or a 2.5-year master-only cohort.
languageReq: Must demonstrate proficiency in Finnish, Swedish OR English by the application deadline, through prior studies or a standardised test. To get the fee exemption the language of studies must be Finnish or Swedish — which means real Finnish (or Swedish) proficiency, realistically B2/C1, achieved before applying. UNVERIFIED exact required level.
englishTest: Accepted as one of the three qualifying languages; exact test/score UNVERIFIED. Note: choosing English triggers the EUR 28,000/yr fee.
study: Three specialisation paths. (1) RECORDING ARTS — the in-scope one: students develop expertise in "music producer and sound engineer" roles, covering recording, editing and mixing techniques for both popular AND classical music, plus live sound reinforcement and audio technology. (2) Film and Game Music — music production for film, game and visual media, music design, sound design, composing and arranging for virtual instruments. (3) Creative Electronic Music Practices — electroacoustic, live electronics, sonic arts, sound installation, generative music (OUT OF SCOPE per brief). Students participate in recording Sibelius Academy concerts and in contemporary-music, multimedia and electroacoustic concert production.

institution: Technische Universität Ilmenau — Institut für Medientechnik, Fakultät Elektrotechnik und Informationstechnik
programme: M.Sc. Medieningenieurwissenschaften (formerly/also listed as Medientechnologie / Media Technology)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
scholarship: DAAD; Deutschlandstipendium
qualification: Master of Science — full second-cycle degree, 120 credit points
accreditation: Public technical university of the Free State of Thuringia.
tuition: NO TUITION FEES. Verbatim: 'There are no tuition fees at TU Ilmenau, only a semester fee of approximately 250 euros (plus a one-time 20 euros for the student ID card at enrollment).' Thuringia has not introduced non-EU tuition. A Tunisian pays €0 tuition and about €500/year in semester contributions. FIGURE SOURCE: a secondary aggregator rather than a TU Ilmenau fee page read directly — the €250 figure is UNVERIFIED in detail, though tuition-free status in Thuringia is certain.
otherFees: Semester fee ~€250 per semester; one-off €20 student ID card. uni-assist processing fee (typically €75 for the first application). German blocked account for the visa.
totalCost: Tuition €0. Semester fees ~€500/yr. Ilmenau is a small Thuringian town with very low living costs — budget roughly €9,000–11,000/yr (UNVERIFIED). Two-year total roughly €19,000–23,000. WITH FH JOANNEUM GRAZ, THIS IS THE CHEAPEST ROUTE IN THE TERRITORY.
scholarshipDetail: Not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED.
entry: 'A Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in the same or a similar field is required. Subject-specific suitability is evaluated based on application materials (transcripts from previous studies).' The programme is NC-FREE — verbatim, 'the program is NC-free (no numerus clausus/no restricted admission based on grades)'. Non-EU/EEA applicants apply through uni-assist.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music background is required or wanted. The entry test is subject affinity judged from the transcript: 'a Bachelor's degree ... in the same or a similar field'. A BSc Software Engineering is a strong candidate for 'similar field' against a media-ENGINEERING master — signal processing, programming and mathematics are the shared core. The residual risk is that the admissions office reads 'similar field' narrowly against media technology specifically; that judgement is made on the transcript and is UNVERIFIED for his exact degree.
portfolio: NONE. No portfolio, no tracks, no work samples — admission is decided on transcripts. This is a significant advantage for a candidate with nothing recorded yet.
audition: NO AUDITION, NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM, NO PRODUCTION TEST, NO INTERVIEW published. Admission is NC-free and decided on documents. This is the most frictionless gate in Germany.
deadline: UNVERIFIED. TU Ilmenau publishes 'application periods' and routes non-EU/EEA applicants through uni-assist; specific dates were not on the pages read. German winter-semester master deadlines for international applicants are commonly 15 July or earlier via uni-assist, and uni-assist itself needs weeks of lead time. VERIFY DIRECTLY.
duration: 4 semesters, 120 credit points (the older Medientechnologie master was 3 semesters / 90 CP — check which curriculum applies for 2027). Start dates: 1 April or 1 October.
languageReq: German OR English, certificate required in whichever is the language of instruction chosen. Exact level UNVERIFIED — this is the single most important thing to verify about this entry.
englishTest: UNVERIFIED — required if the English route is taken, but no accepted tests or scores were published on the pages read.
study: Structure verbatim: 'core media technology modules (17%) with engineering courses from related fields (34-42%), a research or media project (13-21%), soft skills (4%), and a master's thesis (25%)'. Named courses in the media-technology offer include AUDIO AND RECORDING STUDIO TECHNOLOGY, Audio/Video Signal Processing, Fundamentals of Electroacoustics, Fundamentals of Media Technology, Fundamentals of Video Technology and Computer Animation. Practical work runs in the 'Ilmenau Interactive Immersive Technologies Center (I3TC)'. Ilmenau's media-technology institute has a long-standing audio research reputation (it sits in the orbit of Fraunhofer IDMT, the Ilmenau audio institute behind much German audio-coding work). FIT VERDICT: this is Toningenieur/audio-engineering territory — recording-studio technology, electroacoustics, signal processing. It is in field, but it trains engineers rather than record producers.

institution: FH JOANNEUM Gesellschaft mbH — Institute of Design & Communication (in collaboration with KUG, University of …
programme: MA Interaction, Media and Sound Design — study track SOUND DESIGN
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Master of Arts in Arts and Design (MA) — a FULL SECOND-CYCLE FH DEGREE, NOT a Universitätslehrgang. This distinction matters: it is an ordentliches Masterstudium at a Fachhochschule, so it is a real second-cycle qualification and does not require a completed master to enter.
accreditation: Austrian Fachhochschule, accredited by the AQ Austria board; the Styrian government is the majority shareholder of FH JOANNEUM. Inter-university programme run 'in collaboration with the Graz University of Music and Performing Arts' (KUG).
tuition: €727 PER SEMESTER = €1,454 PER YEAR for a Tunisian, and it must be PREPAID. Verbatim: 'Third Country Nationals: A cost contribution of 727 euros per semester applies, which must be prepaid to FH JOANNEUM for the first two semesters (1,454 euros total) before the study place confirmation.' Compare the EU rate on the programme page: '€ 363,36 per semester' — so a third-country national pays exactly DOUBLE the EU rate. NOTE THE CASH-FLOW TRAP: €1,454 is due up front, before your place is confirmed.
otherFees: ÖH student-union contribution, currently €20.70 per semester. Cost of the English certificate (TOEFL/IELTS/telc/Cambridge/PTE). Austrian residence-permit fees and proof-of-funds requirement.
totalCost: Tuition €1,454/yr + ÖH ~€41/yr = ~€1,495/yr. Graz living costs are the lowest of any city in this search — budget roughly €10,000–12,000/yr (UNVERIFIED). Two-year total including living: roughly €23,000–27,000. THIS IS THE CHEAPEST VIABLE OPTION IN THE WHOLE TERRITORY.
scholarshipDetail: Not published on the admissions pages. Austrian options a Tunisian could pursue separately include the OeAD Ernst Mach Grant and the Austrian Development Cooperation scholarships, neither of which was verified for this programme. UNVERIFIED.
entry: Verbatim: 'If you want to apply for this Master's degree programme you need to have a relevant Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification.' Then, verbatim and in detail: 'Graduates of technical, artistic, humanities, social sciences, economics, natural sciences and interdisciplinary programmes at universities, technical universities or art universities with a Bachelor's, Master's or Diplom degree will be admitted if: 80 ECTS credits from their previous studies largely correspond to the core subject areas of the Bachelor's programme in Information Design at FH JOANNEUM or a comparable relevant degree programme, AND at least one of the following eligibility criteria is met: Relevant professional experience spanning a period of at least two years; Assessment of professional aptitude based on the submitted portfolio; Relevant further training or study modules with a workload equivalent of at least 30 ECTS. The degree must be from a recognised institution of postsecondary education in Austria or abroad. In ambiguous cases, the head of degree programme will decide whether the candidate meets the admission requirements.' Documents: signed letter of application (in English), signed CV (in English), degree certificate, transcript of records, university-entrance qualification, English proof, passport copy, and the portfolio PDF.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — TECHNICAL GRADUATES ARE NAMED FIRST. Quoted verbatim: 'Graduates of TECHNICAL, artistic, humanities, social sciences, economics, natural sciences and interdisciplinary programmes ... will be admitted if ...'. And separately: 'Students from relatively distant (non-design-related) study programs may be given the opportunity to participate in the admissions examination if they demonstrate appropriate talent and prior performance. The study program management of FH JOANNEUM decides on equivalence after a complete application is submitted and may require additional workshops, exercises, and courses.' TWO REAL HURDLES FOR HIM: (1) the 80-ECTS correspondence with the Information Design bachelor's core areas — a software-engineering BSc will match on the technical/media-technology side but not on the design side, and the programme head decides; (2) of the three supplementary criteria he currently meets NONE cleanly — he has no two years of relevant professional experience and no 30 ECTS of further training, so he must rely on 'Assessment of professional aptitude based on the submitted portfolio'. THE PORTFOLIO IS THEREFORE HIS ONLY QUALIFYING LIMB, and it must carry the whole argument.
portfolio: EXACT AND DEMANDING. Verbatim guidelines: 'Only online portfolios are accepted. The portfolio should comprise approximately 10 TO 20 REPRESENTATIVE WORK PIECES. The selection and form of the work samples is totally up to the applicant, but should correspond to the applicant's range of interests and competencies. All media formats are allowed – e.g. graphics, illustrations, photos, texts, videos, animations, apps, AUDIO PRODUCTIONS, web sites, media installations, project documentations, and the like. All descriptive texts must be written in German or English. THE ONLINE PORTFOLIO HAS TO BE ACCESSIBLE IN THE PERIOD FROM THE APPLICATION DEADLINE UNTIL THE END OF OCTOBER.' Submitted as a web link, plus 'a PDF including the web-link to your online portfolio in the first line of the first page; a list of all the work pieces with correct attribution of the authorship. In case of teamwork the applicant's responsibilities have to be clearly outlined; screenshots of all pages of the online portfolio (also screenshots of videos, animations or interactive applications).' 10–20 pieces is a LOT for someone with no portfolio today — but note apps and project documentation count, so his software work is admissible material alongside audio.
audition: NO AUDITION, NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM — A PORTFOLIO REVIEW PLUS AN ONLINE INTERVIEW. Verbatim: 'The admissions process consists of: a complete application, an assessment of the online portfolio by the admissions committee, an online interview with the admissions committee and an assessment of previous qualifications and practical professional experience. The form of the application will also be taken into consideration.' On the interview, verbatim: 'All candidates are invited to an interview. You are given the opportunity to demonstrate both your knowledge in the field of sound design and your motivation, suitability and talent for the chosen course of study and a subsequent career in this field. The admissions interview will either be held via video call. At the beginning of the online interview the applicant must confirm that no unauthorised aids are used and no one else is present to help. The applicant must also present official photo identification. The interview will be conducted by key staff from the Institute of Design & Communication. It will last around 20 minutes.' No performance, no aural test, no set production task — and it is CONDUCTED BY VIDEO CALL, so no Schengen visa is needed to be selected.
deadline: MULTIPLE ROUNDS PER YEAR — the most forgiving calendar found anywhere. PRIOR CYCLE OBSERVED (for the 28.09.2026 start): application until 01.02.2026 with interviews 23–27.02.2026; until 24.03.2026 with interviews 20–24.04.2026; until 27.04.2026 with interviews 11–15.05.2026; until 26.05.2026 with interviews 29.06–03.07.2026; until 29.06.2026 with interview 16.07.2026. Five separate windows. For a September 2027 start expect the same rolling pattern from about February 2027 to late June 2027; FH JOANNEUM notes 'The dates on this page will be updated on an ongoing basis.' International applicants are directed to a separate deadline page — those specific international deadlines are UNVERIFIED and may be earlier, so apply in the FIRST round.
opens: Rolling; the first round closed 1 February in the 2026 cycle. Note the portfolio must stay online from the application deadline until the end of October.
duration: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, 'Work-friendly' mode (berufsbegleitend). Attendance is light: 'One day per week is lesson-free. The average attendance during the first three semesters is 19 hours per week. During the fourth semester, students write a master's thesis, which means that during this time the average attendance is three hours per week.' CAUTION FOR A STUDENT VISA: a part-time/work-friendly programme can complicate an Austrian student residence permit, which normally expects full-time study — verify with the Austrian embassy.
languageReq: English only, B2 CEFR. No German requirement whatsoever for admission or study. (German would still be needed for daily life and for any part-time work in Graz.)
englishTest: SPECIFIC SCORES PUBLISHED, verbatim: 'Proof of proficiency in English must be provided in the form of a TOEFL Certificate (min. 87 points), a TELC Certificate (B2), a Cambridge Certificate (First Certificate in English, FCE), an IELTS Certificate (5.0), a PTE Academic Certificate (Pearson Test of English; min. 59 points), an Austrian secondary school leaving certificate or another equivalent school certificate.' IELTS 5.0 IS AN UNUSUALLY LOW BAR — his working English clears it comfortably.
study: Verbatim: 'Storytelling with sound forms the core of this inter-university programme ... Students of the Sound Design study track ... develop knowledge of sound design, media preparation and technical processing. The master's programme covers topics relevant to musicians, sound designers, digital artists and the creative industry, including sound design, immersive audio, product sound design, sonification and sonic interaction design. Students design sounds for films, computer games, audio logos and podcasts, bring data to life through sound, optimise the sound of products and explore immersive sound.' FIT CAVEAT: this is Audiodesign in the media sense — film, games, podcasts, audio logos, product sound, sonification. It is NOT record production, and it will not teach him to mix and master songs. It IS in the brief's field list (Audiodesign) and it is by far the most accessible door; but it is a different career from making records. Projects run 'under real world conditions' with media-industry and festival partners, and 'virtually all project results are published'.

institution: Fachhochschule Salzburg (Salzburg University of Applied Sciences)
programme: MultiMediaArt (Master), specialisation AUDIO
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: Cheap (about EUR 780/yr), English-taught, no audition, and the deadline structure fits a September 2027 start — but admission is not on portfolio alone: they demand 'proof of ECTS credits in the core subject areas required for the Master's programme', and a software-engineering transcript has none of them. He must email study@fh-salzburg.ac.at with his transcript BEFORE investing in the application and get a written answer on whether his credits count. If they say no, this is dead.
correction: DUPLICATE of index 8 — same programme, same URL. Apply once. Same corrections apply.
qualification: Master of Arts in Arts and Design (MA)
tuition: €363.36 per semester tuition + €26.20 ÖH fee (published for the programme). Applicants without EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship or degree must additionally pay a TUITION FEE DEPOSIT, which is credited against the first semester's tuition and ÖH fee or refunded if you do not enrol; the deposit amount is set in a separate guideline (amount UNVERIFIED).
scholarshipDetail: None found on the pages read.
entry: A relevant university degree (bachelor or diploma) from a domestic or foreign higher-education institution; English B2; AND documented minimum ECTS in three core subject areas: 35 ECTS in "creative-artistic design practice" (graphic/media design, film, TV, audio, music, game design…), 10 ECTS in "basic sciences" (media theory, media informatics, media technology, aesthetics…), and 5 ECTS in "economics and working methods in the field of media" (project management, media economics, marketing, media law…). Proof is a completed form plus transcripts. Non-Austrian documents may need notarisation/legalisation.
acceptsNonMusic: Check — the degree field is flexible but the ECTS gate is the real obstacle. "Media Technology and Media Informatics" (internet technologies, digital media, media technology and design) is explicitly on the published list of relevant disciplines, so a software-engineering BSc can count as a "relevant" degree. However he must document 35 ECTS of creative-artistic design practice (audio/music/media design courses), which a pure SE curriculum will usually not contain. The published exemption from full ECTS proof applies only to the Producing department, not Audio.
portfolio: For Audio (as for Film and Communication Design) a PORTFOLIO is mandatory, uploaded in the application portal under "Upload application project" as a ZIP file containing a PDF: "Present at least three of your best creative works from the last few years. Describe in your portfolio the role you played in the projects shown." All third-party material and any soundtrack used must be credited — undeclared external material or copied ideas means exclusion from the admission procedure. Also required: CV in English, choice-of-department form, proof-of-academic-level form with transcripts, passport copy, English B2 proof, bachelor certificate (may be submitted by 31 October).
audition: No performance audition. A ~15-minute interview with the department head and lecturers about your motivation, previous projects, professional experience and any master-project ideas; you may show further creative work (audio snippets, streaming links, screenshots). "Personal interview or, if travel to Salzburg is not possible, via video conference via MS Teams" — remote is explicitly allowed.
deadline: General applications 30 October 2025 – 1 July 2026; FINAL deadline 1 April 2026 for applicants who hold neither EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship nor an entrance qualification/degree from those countries — this earlier non-EU deadline is the one that binds a Tunisian applicant. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (expect roughly Oct 2026 opening, ~1 April 2027 non-EU cut-off).
opens: 30 October 2025 for the 2026/27 winter-semester intake — PRIOR CYCLE
duration: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time
study: You pick ONE of four departments — Audio, Film, Communication Design or Producing — and build advanced skills in conceiving, designing, implementing and managing cross-media projects (feature films, documentaries, games, VR, interactive installations). The Audio department covers music production & recording, composition, sound synthesis & sound design, mix & mastering, interactive audio, soundtracks & audio post-production, and sound & performance, with cross-department collaboration on film soundtracks, game audio and multimedia installations. Head of Audio: DI (FH) Martin Löcker.
recommendation: The strongest English-taught, low-fee, studio-equipped music-production/sound-design master in Austria, and the admission is humane: three works in a PDF plus a 15-minute interview that can be done over Teams. The obstacle is arithmetic, not artistic — the 35 ECTS creative-practice requirement. He should email study@fh-salzburg.ac.at with his transcript now and, if short, spend 2026/27 collecting creditable audio/media coursework or consider the Producing department as a fallback.

institution: IAD – Institut des Arts de Diffusion
programme: Master en Son — three separate 60-credit sound masters: Son Studio, Son Sono, and Cinéma Son (the first two presented o…
costDisputed: cost band 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is also WRONG
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: An in-person jury audition in Belgium between mid-August and mid-September is a hard gate he cannot pass with no portfolio and no audio experience, and it falls barely three weeks before term — impossible to combine with a Tunisian student-visa timeline. He would also pay the full €4,175 non-EEA supplement on top of €1,194 minerval with no scholarship route, because Tunisia is not on the LDC exemption list. Nothing here is funded and everything here is gated on artistic evidence he does not have.
correction: The record says gate = 'Portfolio only'. WRONG — IAD explicitly auditions shortlisted candidates before a jury. The record's cost band 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr' is also WRONG for a Tunisian: the €1,194 minerval is only the EEA rate; a non-EEA student pays an additional €4,175/yr droit d'inscription spécifique, giving ≈€5,369/yr.
qualification: Master (2nd cycle) in sound for audiovisual media
tuition: NOW VERIFIED, correcting the previous entry. IAD publishes for 2026-2027: standard minerval €1,194 per academic year (covering student card, basic technical and artistic materials, software licences and IT services), plus a mandatory €4,175 annual supplementary contribution for non-EU students = c. €5,369/year. Payment: minimum €50 deposit by 31 October, balance by 31 January; the non-EU contribution is due by 31 January. IAD notes these 2026-2027 amounts are provisional pending final parliamentary approval by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation.
scholarshipDetail: None found that he can realistically use — and this is a correction in the negative direction. The €4,175 supplement is waived for several categories IAD lists explicitly: 'ressortissants d'un pays membre de la liste LDC (ONU, pays les moins avancés)', long-term residents of Belgium, recognised refugees or holders of subsidiary protection, holders of a Wallonie-Bruxelles International scholarship, and students with qualifying EU-citizen parents. Tunisia is not an LDC, so only the WBI route applies. CRITICAL: IAD does NOT appear on the official list of MASTER IN – WBI grant host institutions (which does include ARTS², La Cambre, INSAS and other arts schools), so the main WBI master's scholarship is not available here. No IAD-internal scholarship for non-EU students was found.
entry: Confirmed verbatim, and it is the most degree-agnostic wording in this whole slice: 'La plupart des masters 60 ou 120 organisés à l'IAD sont ouverts aux étudiants titulaires d'un bachelier' — most 60- or 120-credit masters at IAD are open to holders of a bachelor's degree. The only stated exception is the teaching master (Section 5), which requires an existing master. Application is by email to admissions-masters@iad-arts.be with: identity photo, CV, motivation letter, secondary-education diploma, the relevant degree, ID copy, birth certificate, prior academic records, and the portfolio. Candidates selected on file and works are then auditioned by a jury.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes on paper — the strongest published position in this slice. IAD's wording is degree-agnostic ('La plupart des masters 60 ou 120 organisés à l'IAD sont ouverts aux étudiants titulaires d'un bachelier') and imposes no requirement for a music, sound or arts bachelor. The real gate is the portfolio, which must prove technical and artistic ability in the chosen orientation, and the assumed technical baseline is that of IAD's own 180-ECTS sound bachelor.
portfolio: Confirmed verbatim: 'un book de travaux aboutis qui prouvent vos aptitudes techniques et artistiques' — a portfolio of COMPLETED works proving technical and artistic aptitude, specific to the chosen orientation. Submitted alongside identity photo, CV, motivation letter, diplomas, ID and birth certificate. Number of works, durations and formats: UNVERIFIED — not published.
audition: Two-stage with a mandatory IN-PERSON jury at Louvain-la-Neuve. Candidates are first selected on the basis of their file and works; those shortlisted are then auditioned by a jury. For the 2026-2027 intake the admission commissions ran in person from 24 August to 11 September 2026, with dates communicated individually by email. Requires travel to Belgium at the very end of the summer.
deadline: Applications 4 May – 14 August 2026; in-person admission juries 24 August – 11 September 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a September 2027 start expect roughly 4 May – 14 August 2027 with juries late August to mid-September 2027. Non-EU supplementary contribution must be paid by 31 January.
opens: 4 May for the 2026-2027 intake (applications by email to admissions-masters@iad-arts.be). Application deposit for first-year masters is free.
duration: 60 crédits each — confirmed verbatim on the IAD sound faculty page — following a 180-ECTS professional bachelor in sound. A 3+1 structure.
study: IAD's sound training covers the full sound-engineer profession: studio and live recording, mixing, editing, mastering, event sound reinforcement (sonorisation) and sound design, training 'sound engineers who master sound recording tools and techniques in radio, television and multimedia, as well as editors and sound mixers who master editing and sound mixing tools'. The master combines artistic and technical coursework with workshops, an in-depth internship more advanced than at bachelor level, a final work evaluated by a jury of industry professionals, and a written thesis. Students collaborate with IAD's multimedia, theatre and directing programmes on real productions. The three orientations split the field: Son Studio is closest to music recording and mixing, Son Sono covers live sound, Cinéma Son covers film sound.
recommendation: Confirmed as a serious, very practical French-language route into professional audio, with the most welcoming admission wording anywhere in this slice — most IAD masters are open to any bachelor's holder, so his software-engineering BSc is not automatically disqualifying, and Son Studio is the orientation closest to music recording and mixing. Cost is now confirmed at a modest c. €5,369/yr and there is no English-test barrier. But verification made the funding picture worse rather than better: IAD is absent from the MASTER IN – WBI host-institution list, so the €10,020 grant that makes ARTS² so attractive simply cannot be used here, and no IAD-internal scholarship exists. That makes IAD a self-pay option. Add the in-person jury in Louvain-la-Neuve in late August/early September and a 60-credit master built on top of IAD's own three-year sound bachelor — meaning the assumed technical baseline is high and his portfolio must genuinely prove it — and this ranks below both ARTS² Musiques appliquées and KASK for him. Strong programme, weak funding fit.

institution: KASK & Conservatorium, School of Arts Gent (HOGENT and Howest)

On mismatched degrees generally: 'If you wish to begin a master's program, but do not have the appropriate underlying bachelor's degree, you may, in some cases, follow a bridging program. In such cases, it is best to contact your study program supervisor.' Software engineering is neither performing nor composing music nor an artistic discipline, so a bridging (schakel) programme is the probable path, not direct master entry. Master Mind 2027-2028 call: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (the 2026-2027 call launched January 2026 with institution deadlines between 1 February and 1 April 2026).

Year 1 (60 ECTS): Producing & artistic research 31 ECTS; Projects master 1, 3 ECTS; Masterseminaries 8 ECTS; Thesis 1, 3 ECTS; Professional skills 3 ECTS; Minor/Specialisation/Electives 12 ECTS. Year 2 (60 ECTS): Master project Producing 33 ECTS; Projects master 2, 3 ECTS; Thesis 2, 6 ECTS; Arts in Practice 6 ECTS; Minor/Specialisation/Electives 12 ECTS. So 64 of 120 credits sit in producing and the producing capstone. recommendation: Still the strongest overall bet in this slice, and verification strengthened rather than weakened it: 64 of 120 credits are literally producing and a producing capstone; stage-one admission is dossier-only so his portfolio does the work before any travel; the non-EEA fee of €8,800.20 is confirmed and the school's own scholarship is confirmed to be sized to erase it, including for bridging students. Three things kill it for him, and the first is fatal on its own. accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL. No NVAO accreditation, no ECTS, no university validation, no CROHO registration. 'Niet-bekostigd' private institution. Institution-level CRKBO registration is a VAT-exemption/quality register for short vocational training and is NOT higher-education accreditation — it gives this certificate no legal standing as a Dutch qualification and no academic transfer value whatsoever.
tuition: VERIFIED on the official 2026/2027 fee page: STANDARD €699 (= €100 registration + €599 tuition). XF, including 3 months' facility access: €1,099 (= €100 registration + €999 tuition). No EU/non-EU differential published.
otherFees: MAJOR CORRECTION — the registration fee on this course is €100, NOT €500, and it is ALREADY INCLUDED in the €699 / €1,099 headline prices. Earlier records warned the €500 fee 'applies to all programmes' and 'would nearly double the cost' — that is WRONG. The €500 registration figure applies to SAE's longer diploma and certificate programmes; the DJ Certificate carries a €100 registration, already baked into the quoted totals. Nothing further is charged. No materials, exam or insurance fee published.
totalCost: Tuition all-in: €699 standard or €1,099 XF — no hidden registration fee to add. Plus return flights Tunis–Amsterdam (roughly €200–€450) and one month's Amsterdam accommodation (roughly €1,200–€2,200), plus living costs and Schengen visa fee (approx. €90) and insurance. REALISTIC TOTAL: €2,300–€4,000. This is by an order of magnitude the cheapest way for him to physically set foot in the Dutch music-education world.
scholarshipDetail: NONE. No scholarship, bursary or fee waiver of any kind. Not eligible for any Dutch student finance.
entry: VERIFIED — open entry. The course page states plainly that no prior experience is required and that 'Motivation and determination are more important than prior knowledge.' No prior qualification, age gate or prerequisite is published for this course.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — unambiguously. Quoted from the official course page: 'No prior experience required'; 'Motivation and determination are more important than prior knowledge.' A software-engineering bachelor with no music training is explicitly within scope. This is the least restrictive entry requirement in the entire slice.
portfolio: NONE. No portfolio, demo, mix or showreel required. Verified absent.
audition: None. No audition, interview or entrance test.
deadline: No published hard deadline — rolling until the cohort fills. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: only September 2026 and January 2027 starts are published; a September 2027 intake is plausible given the twice-yearly pattern but is NOT yet announced.
opens: Rolling — registration open now via saeamsterdam.com/registration. No fixed opening date.
duration: 1 month. A '1 month + 3 months facility access' (XF) variant is also offered. No ECTS.
englishTest: NO English test required and NO IELTS score published for a one-month certificate. SAE's informal baseline is intermediate conversational English. He would not need IELTS for this. UNVERIFIED in writing — confirm with admissions.
study: VERIFIED published content: beat matching; EQ technique; audio format knowledge (mp3, wav, flac, aiff); mixing with cues; set preparation; B2B (back-to-back) session technique; and promotion/self-marketing strategy. Delivered as hands-on training on decks led by working industry professionals, with personalised feedback. Stated career pathways: DJ, remix artist, live performer.
recommendation: THE ONE DUTCH OPTION HE COULD ACTUALLY ATTEND IN PERSON — and now verified to be cheaper than previously recorded, since the feared €500 registration fee does not apply (it is €100, already included). At €699–€1,099 tuition it is a rounding error next to the €19,000–€21,000 Abbey Road programmes, and it demands nothing he does not already have: no portfolio, no IELTS, no music background. TREAT IT AS A SCOUTING TRIP, NOT AN EDUCATION. For roughly €2,300–€4,000 all-in he gets a month of hands-on DJ training in the dance-music capital, can visit SAE and Abbey Road Institute in person and judge them himself, can start the 4–8 track portfolio that every serious programme will demand, and can build contacts — all while keeping his September 2027 accredited-master application on track elsewhere (Spain, Italy, Portugal, or a Dutch PUBLIC conservatory such as Codarts or the Conservatorium van Amsterdam, which unlike SAE and Abbey Road ARE NVAO-accredited and CAN sponsor a student residence permit). CHOOSE THE XF TIER (€1,099) if he goes — three months of facility access for €400 more is the best-value line item in this entire slice, provided his visa covers the stay. BEFORE BOOKING: confirm in writing (1) that a September 2027 intake will run, (2) that registration is €100 and nothing further is due, and (3) get an enrolment letter for the visa application before paying anything non-refundable.

institution: Point Blank Music School (Ibiza campus)
programme: 1-Week and 2-Week DJ/Producer courses (Ibiza) — NOT A MASTER, short intensive course
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's
qualification: A course completion certificate. NOT a master, NOT a postgraduate qualification, no ECTS, no university validation, no Spanish accreditation of any kind.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL in Spain. Point Blank's UK degree programmes are validated in the UK, but the IBIZA offering is short summer courses only, carrying no Spanish academic status whatsoever.
tuition: £1,195 (1 week) or £1,695 (2 weeks). A 20% early-booking discount has been offered in prior cycles.
otherFees: A £200 deposit is required for both the one-week and two-week courses (applied against the total). Flights, accommodation and Ibiza living costs are NOT included and Ibiza is one of the most expensive places in Spain in summer. A Schengen visa application fee would also apply for a Tunisian national.
totalCost: £1,195–£1,695 tuition, plus flights from Tunis, plus Ibiza summer accommodation (which can easily exceed the tuition), plus a Schengen visa. Realistically £3,000–£5,000 for two weeks. High cost per hour, but a genuine credential-free entry point to the Ibiza scene.
scholarshipDetail: None published for the Ibiza short courses.
entry: None for Level 1. Level 2 requires having mastered the basics.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — completely open, no prerequisites for Level 1.
portfolio: None.
audition: None.
deadline: No academic deadline; booking-based. An 'IBIZAEARLY' promotional code giving 20% off Ibiza courses was advertised with an end date of 30 November — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm whether an equivalent code runs for summer 2027.
opens: Rolling bookings for the summer season.
duration: 1 week or 2 weeks. No ECTS.
englishTest: No IELTS required, though the course is taught in English.
study: 26 hours of tuition per week, combining classroom instruction with DJ experiences playing out at venues. Level 1 covers production and DJing fundamentals on Pioneer DJ equipment and Ableton Live; Level 2 is for those who have already mastered the basics. Classes run roughly 10:00–15:00 Monday to Friday including a lunch hour.
recommendation: EXPLICITLY FLAGGED AS NOT A MASTER — a one or two-week intensive. But it deserves a place on his radar for a reason none of the accredited programmes offer: guaranteed performance slots at real Ibiza venues plus a professional media pack, which is exactly the kind of asset that builds a DJ's actual career. My candid verdict: it is not a route to Spain and not a qualification, but as a two-week, roughly £1,700 investment in portfolio, footage and contacts before applying to a real master's programme, it would do more for his stated ambition than several of the five-figure 'másteres' on this list. Treat it as career marketing, not education.

institution: Point Blank Music School (Ibiza campus, operated by pointblank Limited, a company registered in England)
programme: 1-Week and 2-Week DJ/Producer courses, and 1-Week DJ Skills (Ibiza) — NOT A MASTER, short intensive summer courses
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: NO ACADEMIC QUALIFICATION. The Ibiza course pages name no certificate, no diploma, no ECTS and no validating body — they list only duration, timetable, fees and start date. Whatever completion document is issued (if any) has no Spanish academic status. NOT a master, NOT a postgraduate award. Point Blank's genuine degrees and Certificates of Higher Education are UK-validated products delivered in London / Online, and are a separate offering from the Ibiza summer courses.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL in Spain — verified by absence. Nothing on the Ibiza course pages, the Ibiza location page or the Ibiza terms and conditions claims Spanish accreditation, ECTS, university validation or recognition by any Spanish authority. These are commercial short courses. Point Blank's UK degree provision does not extend any status to the Ibiza campus.
tuition: CORRECTED — the draft said '£1,195 (1 week)'. The verified published price is £1,145 for every one-week course (DJ/Producer Level 1, DJ/Producer Level 2 and DJ Skills), and £1,695 for both two-week courses. Prices as published for the 2026 season; 2027 pricing is not yet posted, so treat these as indicative. A 20% early-booking code has been offered in each of the last two cycles, which would bring two weeks to roughly £1,356.
otherFees: CORRECTED — the deposit is NOT £200 for both. Verified: one-week courses take a £100 registration fee plus a £1,045 balance; two-week courses take a £200 registration fee plus a £1,495 balance. THE DEPOSIT IS NON-REFUNDABLE IN ALL CIRCUMSTANCES, including visa refusal. Not included and not published: flights from Tunis, accommodation (partner-hotel discounts are offered but the rates are not published), Ibiza living costs in peak summer, travel to the venues (students 'are asked to make their own way to the venues'), and a Schengen short-stay visa application fee for a Tunisian national. No insurance or materials fee is charged.
totalCost: Two weeks: £1,695 tuition (or roughly £1,356 with a 20% early-bird code), plus flights Tunis-Ibiza, plus peak-summer Ibiza accommodation which can easily exceed the tuition, plus a Schengen visa fee and the documentation burden that comes with it. Realistically £3,000-£5,000 all-in for two weeks. Very high cost per contact hour, but the only credential-free route into the Ibiza scene on this list.
scholarshipDetail: NONE. No scholarship, bursary or financial aid of any kind is published for the Ibiza short courses.
entry: None published for Level 1 — no qualification, no audition, no portfolio. Level 2 requires 'those of you who have already mastered the basics (or who have graduated from the Ibiza DJ/Producer Course - Level 1 or similar)'. Under-18s need parent/guardian permission per the terms and conditions.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — completely open. Nothing on the Level 1 pages states any academic or musical prerequisite; the course is explicitly 'designed to give beginners a fantastic start in the world of production and DJing'. A BSc Software Engineering is irrelevant either way.
portfolio: None.
audition: None.
deadline: No academic deadline — booking-based, with places sold until full. Payment deadline is contractual: full payment must be received at least FOURTEEN (14) DAYS before the course starts. On discounts: an 'IBIZAEARLY' code for 20% off was extended to 30 November 2025, and an 'IBIZA26' code for 20% off ran until 25 May 2026. BOTH PRIOR CYCLE — but the pattern is consistent, so expect an equivalent 20% early-bird code for summer 2027, likely announced in late 2026. Booking early on a code is the single biggest saving available here.
opens: Rolling bookings for the summer season; no academic application cycle.
duration: 1 week or 2 weeks. NO ECTS. Five distinct products verified: 1 Week DJ/Producer Level 1, 1 Week DJ/Producer Level 2, 2 Week DJ/Producer Level 1, 2 Week DJ/Producer Level 2, and a standalone 1 Week DJ Skills course.
englishTest: No IELTS or any English test required. The course is 'taught in English by professional DJ/Producers'. Booking is commercial, not an academic admission.
study: VERIFIED from the course pages. Level 1 (beginners, supported by Pioneer DJ): production fundamentals — making beats with drums, basslines and chords; recording audio into Ableton Live; editing with effects such as compression and reverb; mixing your tracks; plus DJ skills — tempo and cueing, beatmatching, EQing and effects, creative mixing, looping and set preparation. Level 2 is 'designed for those of you who have already mastered the basics (or who have graduated from the Ibiza DJ/Producer Course - Level 1 or similar)' and covers beat matching, looping, harmonic mixing, effects, plus sound design, sidechaining, synthesis, warping, slicing, mixing and mastering. 26 hours of tuition per week, comprising classroom time plus the DJ experiences playing out at venues. Timetable Monday to Friday roughly 10:00-15:00 including a lunch hour (listed as TBC).
recommendation: EXPLICITLY NOT A MASTER — one or two weeks, no ECTS, no certificate named, no Spanish accreditation, and it cannot bring him to Spain on a student permit. Three corrections he must not miss: the one-week price is £1,145 not £1,195; the deposit is £100 for one week and £200 for two, and it is NON-REFUNDABLE EVEN IF HIS VISA IS REFUSED; and the performance slots are advertised as potential opportunities subject to venue availability, not the guaranteed bookings the marketing implies. There is also no instalment plan — the terms and conditions rule instalments out and demand full payment 14 days before the start. That said, my candid verdict stands: as a roughly £1,700 two-week investment (nearer £1,350 on the recurring 20% early-bird code) in real Ibiza contacts, a free professional media pack of 10 press shots and 2 Instagram reels, and 50% off Ableton Live, it would do more for his stated ambition of becoming a working DJ than several of the five-figure 'másteres' elsewhere on this list. Treat it as career marketing bought with a Schengen tourist-style visa, taken in a summer BEFORE the September 2027 intake, and never as a qualification or a route to residency. CONDITIONAL strictly on that framing — if he is tempted to substitute it for an accredited programme, the answer is AVOID.

institution: Hochschule für Musik Basel FHNW — Institut Jazz (Jazzcampus)
programme: MA Musikalische Performance — Studienrichtung Producing/Performance Jazz (Schwerpunkt Realisation)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
scholarship: FHNW / HSM Basel Stipendien (page exists under Quicklinks: 'Studiengebühren & Finanzierung', 'Stipendien'); Swiss Gover…
qualification: Master of Arts FHNW in Musikalischer Performance, Studienrichtung Producing/Performance Jazz — full second-cycle degree, 120 ECTS
accreditation: Public Fachhochschule (FHNW). Governed by the 'Rahmenordnung für die Studiengänge der FHNW' of 2 Feb 2015 (as at 21 June 2021) and the 'Studien- und Prüfungsordnung der Hochschule für Musik Basel FHNW' of 1 December 2024, plus the binding 'Studienrichtungsreglement MA Musikalische Performance, Studienrichtung Jazz Producing/Performance'.
tuition: CHF 1,250 PER SEMESTER = CHF 2,500 PER YEAR for a Tunisian. FHNW publishes an explicit three-tier rate, quoted verbatim from the Steckbrief: 'Semestergebühr 750 CHF (CH) | 1000 CHF (EU/EFTA-Länder) | 1250 CHF (Nicht-EU/Nicht-EFTA)'. This is the clearest example of a Swiss school charging third-country nationals a higher rate — a Tunisian pays CHF 250/semester more than an EU student and CHF 500/semester more than a Swiss. Still only about CHF 2,500/year in absolute terms.
otherFees: Anmeldegebühr CHF 200 (application fee, stated on the Steckbrief). Compulsory Swiss health insurance. Instrument/equipment costs at own expense.
totalCost: Tuition CHF 2,500/yr + CHF 200 one-off application fee. Basel living costs approx CHF 20,000–24,000/yr (UNVERIFIED — not read from an FHNW page). Two-year total including living: roughly CHF 45,000–53,000.
scholarshipDetail: The programme page carries Quicklinks to 'Studiengebühren & Finanzierung' and 'Stipendien' but the substance of those pages was NOT read here — the amounts, eligibility for third-country nationals and deadlines are UNVERIFIED. Swiss cantonal scholarships are generally closed to students who move to Switzerland purely to study, so the realistic funding route is the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship or Tunisian sources. FUNDING FOR THIS PROGRAMME: UNVERIFIED.
entry: Verbatim from the programme page: 'Zum Masterstudium in Musikalischer Performance Jazz (Producing/Performance) zugelassen wird, wer über ein abgeschlossenes Bachelorstudium in Musik (Profil Jazz) oder eine äquivalente Vorbildung verfügt, die Aufnahmeprüfung bestanden und einen Studienplatz erhalten hat (Anzahl beschränkt).' Documents required with the application per Studienrichtungsreglement §4(4): 'a. Lebenslauf, b. Motivationsschreiben, c. Maturzeugnis, d. Passfoto (für Studierendenausweis)' — note it asks for the school-leaving certificate, plus the subject dossiers described below. Places are capped and awarded by rank: §5(1) 'werden die vorhandenen Studienplätze ... in einem rangorientierten Verfahren entsprechend ihrer Gesamtbewertung der Eignungsabklärung ... vergeben.' §4(5): 'Bei Nichtbestehen der Prüfung im Hauptfach ist die Eignungsabklärung insgesamt nicht bestanden.' The aptitude assessment may be repeated once.
acceptsNonMusic: THE MOST OPEN WORDING FOUND IN SWITZERLAND. Quoted verbatim from the programme page's target-group paragraph: 'Diese Studienrichtung richtet sich an fortgeschrittene Instrumentalist:innen, Sänger:innen, Komponist:innen oder Produzent:innen mit einem Bachelorabschluss in Musik, einem gleichwertigen Studienabschluss oder gleichwertiger Berufserfahrung.' Two things matter here: (a) 'Produzent:innen' are named as a target group in their own right, and (b) the qualifying route is a music bachelor OR an equivalent degree OR EQUIVALENT PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE — the regulation's own phrasing is 'oder eine äquivalente Vorbildung'. A BSc Software Engineering is not by itself an äquivalente Vorbildung for a jazz master, so the realistic route is the professional-experience limb. HE HAS NONE TODAY. This is the single thing that would most change his odds: between now and February 2027 he needs credited production/mix work he can name. There is no ear-training exam and no compulsory instrument audition on the Realisation track.
portfolio: Schwerpunkt Realisation, first round, verbatim: 'Produktions-Dossier — Es ist ein Soundfile einer selbständig produzierten Aufnahme/Mischung (Studioproduktion) und/oder einer Film-/Video-Vertonung oder eines Remixes/Sounddesigns mit einer kurzen Erläuterung der Produktionsweise (PDF) einzureichen.' So: ONE sound file of an independently produced recording/mix (studio production) and/or film-video scoring and/or a remix/sound design, PLUS a short PDF explaining how it was produced. No track count beyond one, no stated length limit, no stated file format beyond 'Soundfile' — UNVERIFIED whether wav or mp3 is preferred. Also required in round one: a Motivationsschreiben ('Im Motivationsschreiben soll die bisherige musikalische und anderweitige Vorbildung tabellarisch beschrieben werden. Daneben soll die Motivation für sowie die Erwartungen an ein Masterstudium ... dargelegt werden') and a MASTER PROJECT PLAN sketching artistic-research interests. YOU MUST ALSO SUBMIT A KOMBINATIONSFACH DOSSIER: verbatim, 'Mit dem Schwerpunktfach Realisation (Produktion) ist Performance (Instrument/Stimme) oder Komposition als Kombinationsfach wählbar.' If Komposition is chosen: 'Es sind drei Kompositionen aus dem aktuellen kompositorischen Schaffen ... einzureichen.' If Performance is chosen: an audiovisual recording of 'mindestens drei Stücken' solo and/or with ensemble. CHOOSING KOMPOSITION AS THE COMBINATION SUBJECT AVOIDS HAVING TO PLAY AN INSTRUMENT ON CAMERA. Deadline for uploads: 'laden Sie die geforderten Unterlagen sowohl für das Schwerpunkt- als auch für das Kombinationsfach bis zum 15. Februar hoch.'
audition: TWO ROUNDS, AND THE DECISIVE PART IS A PORTFOLIO HEARING, NOT AN AUDITION. Round 1 is pure dossier: 'Vorselektion — Anhand des eingereichten Dossiers inkl. Motivationsschreiben und Master Project Plan entscheidet eine Kommission über die Zulassung zur zweiten Runde.' Round 2 for Schwerpunkt Realisation consists of: (a) 'Hearing Realisation (Dauer: 20 Minuten)' — a 20-minute hearing of your productions; the school publishes the duration but no further content detail, so the internal format is UNVERIFIED; (b) the Kombinationsfach element, and this is only conditional — verbatim: 'Auf Verlangen der Prüfungskommission Vorspiel (bei Kombinationsfach Performance; es sind zwei bis drei Stücke vorzubereiten) oder Präsentation (bei Kombinationsfach Komposition; kurze Präsentation/Vorspiel von ein bis zwei eigenen Kompositionsarbeiten)' — i.e. ONLY IF THE COMMISSION ASKS; (c) 'Gespräch mit der Kommission zum Master Project Plan (Dauer: 10 Minuten). In den präsentierten Produktionen soll ein Bezug zum im Master Project Plan dargelegten künstlerischen Interesse gemacht werden.' NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM ANYWHERE. NO COMPULSORY PERFORMANCE AUDITION on the Realisation track. AND ROUND 2 CAN BE DONE ONLINE: verbatim, 'Die zweite Runde (Präsentation/Audition) ... findet in der Regel in Präsenz (vor Ort) statt. Auf Antrag kann die Audition online absolviert werden. Die Zuteilung ins Online-Verfahren erfolgt nach Genehmigung des Antrags, der mit Einreichen des Dossiers verbindlich gestellt werden muss.' A Tunisian can therefore complete the whole selection without a Schengen visa. Reglement §4(2)-(3): 'Der praktische Prüfungsteil besteht aus einer ersten Runde «per Video» und einer zweiten Runde in Form eines Live-Vorspiels ... Das Vorspiel vor Ort findet in April statt.' §4(6): 'Die Ergebnisse werden im Mai per E-Mail bekannt gegeben.'
deadline: 15 FEBRUARY. Verbatim: 'Das Anmeldewindow ist vom 15. Dezember bis zum 15. Februar geöffnet' (page: 'Das Anmeldefenster ist vom 15. Dezember bis zum 15. Februar geöffnet'). NOT a prior cycle — the page already advertises the start date 13.9.2027, so for the September 2027 intake the window is 15 December 2026 – 15 February 2027, live round in April 2027, results by e-mail in May 2027.
opens: 15 December (i.e. 15 December 2026 for the September 2027 intake).
duration: 4 semesters, full-time, on-campus (Präsenz), 120 ECTS. NEXT START PUBLISHED AS 13 SEPTEMBER 2027 — exactly his target intake.
languageReq: 'Gute Grundkenntnisse in Englisch' — good basic English, evaluated during the admission procedure. NO GERMAN REQUIREMENT PUBLISHED. Conditional admission possible if language is short but the artistic assessment convinces.
englishTest: No test score named. Verbatim: 'Diese werden im Verlauf des Zulassungsverfahrens evaluiert' — English is assessed in-process, not by certificate. UNVERIFIED whether an IELTS/TOEFL is ever accepted or required.
study: The Hauptfach is a combination of three areas — Instrument/Gesang (Performance), Komposition and REALISATION (Produktion). Verbatim: 'Im Profil «allrounder» wird einer dieser drei Bereiche zum Schwerpunkt gewählt, die beiden übrigen ergänzen diesen als Kombinationsfächer I+II.' Choosing Realisation as the Schwerpunkt makes this a production degree. Programme aims verbatim: 'Fundierte musikalische, technische und kulturelle Kenntnisse ermöglichen ein rasches Erfassen von Aufbau und Ablauf einer kompletten Produktion im Studio und bei Live-Projekten sowie die überzeugende Umsetzung eigener Ideen auf dem Instrument und in einem technologisch komplexen Umfeld.' Highlights listed: 'flexibler und projektorientierter Aufbau des Studiums mit individuellen Schwerpunkten in Performance, Komposition und Produktion'; 'Arbeit in hervorragend ausgestatteten Studios'; 'Coaching durch erfahrene, renommierte Dozierende'. Artistic Research module. Final assessment verbatim: 'Beim Abschluss präsentieren die Studierenden ein Portfolio aus Kompositionen und/oder professionellen Produktionen und/oder eine Live-Performance.' Named teaching staff for Realisation: Daniel Dettwiler (Basel recording/mixing/mastering engineer) and Prof. Patrik Zosso (programme director). Idiom is jazz and 'verwandte Musikrichtungen' — not pop/hip-hop record production, which is a genuine fit caveat.

institution: Istanbul Technical University (İTÜ) — Dr. Erol Üçer Center for Advanced Studies in Music (MIAM)
programme: Music (M.A.) — Sound Engineering and Design (SED) concentration area
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: Admissions rules that could have been written for him: no subject requirement, no GRE/ALES, no IELTS, fully English-taught, portfolio plus interview, and an April-to-June window that fits a September 2027 start. The unresolved thing is money — the 'Full funding' on his list is unsupported by any ITU page, and the international tuition figure is unpublished, so the only credible full ride is Türkiye Bursları, a separate national competition with an earlier deadline he would have to plan for independently.
correction: DUPLICATE of indices 7 and 22 — same MA, different concentration; one application selects a concentration area. Same corrections: unsubstantiated 'Full' funding, unverified tuition, and an interview stage in addition to the portfolio. Of the two concentrations, Sound Engineering and Design is the one where his software-engineering background reads as an asset rather than a curiosity.
qualification: M.A. in Music, thesis track (1st Education); non-thesis 2nd Education variant also available (Term Project instead of thesis)
tuition: VERIFIED: 33,300 TL per academic year for international graduate students who entered in 2024-2025 or 2025-2026 (İTÜ Registrar fee schedule), paid in two instalments. Turkish citizens pay 1,115 TL/year at graduate level. 2026-2027 figure set annually by the Council of Higher Education.
scholarshipDetail: Türkiye Bursları (YTB) — confirmed to exist, to be open to non-Turkish nationals at master's level, and to list Music and Musicology among eligible fields. The specific 'Arts Scholarship Programme' sub-track, the three-participating-universities claim and the January-to-February application window could NOT be verified on the official site in this pass.
entry: Same as Sonic Arts and confirmed verbatim: 'GPA: Not required', 'ALES/GMAT/GRE: Talep edilmemektedir', 'There are no department / concentration area requirements', two letters of recommendation, a portfolio relevant to the application area, and online pre-registration at www.sis.itu.edu.tr under 'Müzik/Music'. English proficiency: IELTS is NOT accepted by İTÜ. Master's minimums are İTÜ Proficiency 65/100, TOEFL iBT 78/120, PTE Academic 62/90 (67/90 from 2026-2027 fall), YDS/e-YDS/YÖKDİL 65/100, OTE Advanced 111/140, e-Tep 50; TOEFL iBT and PTE must be sat at exam centres in state universities.
acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — 'There are no department / concentration area requirements', no GPA and no ALES/GRE, and a 0-credit preparatory semester (including Studio Practices) exists for entrants without music training. The practical filter is not the degree but the portfolio: three of the candidate's OWN multitrack mixes, each containing at least one microphone-recorded acoustic track, with no borrowed, downloaded or AI-generated material. A self-taught in-the-box electronic producer cannot satisfy that from his existing catalogue; he must go and record real acoustic sources. The written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exam is also not waived.
portfolio: UPDATED to the 2026-2027 Fall handbook. Sound Engineering and Design, verbatim: 'Three mixes of recordings made by the candidate are required. Each mix must include at least one track from an acoustic source, recorded with a microphone.' / 'Demos must not contain any material recorded by others, downloaded online, or generated with AI tools.' / '1 page description of the mixes sent.' Example information required in that page: 'When was the recording done? Where was the recording done? What equipment was used? What software was used? Credits.' / 'Photos from recording sessions, as well as other supporting material, are also welcome.' NEW vs the prior cycle: the explicit prohibition on borrowed, downloaded or AI-generated material. Delivery is the same as Sonic Arts — single .zip/.rar, uploaded to Google Drive / Dropbox / OneDrive only, open sharing link submitted via http://tiny.cc/MiamApplication26-27Fall, plus mandatory SIS registration.
audition: Yes. Written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exams (1 July 2026, 10:00-13:00), then a Sound Engineering and Design field exam (14:00-16:00 — SED is explicitly one of the three master's field exams), then an individual interview across 1-3 July. Handbook rule: in person at İTÜ Maçka Campus for Turkish candidates; 'International candidates have the option to do an online interview via Zoom as well' — the Zoom option is stated for the interview only, not the written or field exams. The secondary claim from the prior record that applicants demonstrate microphone recordings during the interview is NOT in the official handbook — treat as UNVERIFIED.
deadline: CURRENT CYCLE (Sept 2026 entry) — already closed. 2026-2027 Fall handbook: portfolio and SIS registration both due 26 June 2026; written exams 1 July 2026 10:00-13:00; SED field exam 1 July 2026 14:00-16:00; interviews 1-3 July 2026. For SEPTEMBER 2027 entry the 2027-2028 Fall handbook is NOT YET PUBLISHED — expect a late-June 2027 deadline on the same pattern.
opens: Autumn handbook posted on the MIAM news page in May (2026-2027: 13 May 2026; 2024-2025: 23 May 2024); spring handbook in late January. 2027-2028 dates unpublished.

study: CONFIRMED from the concentration-areas page. Verbatim: 'The core of the MIAM SED program consists of the following four courses: Studio Practices, Multitrack Recording and Mixing, Advanced Mixing and Mastering. However, the students are encouraged to expand their sonic knowledge by taking courses of their interest, such as Computer Music, Audio Programming and Classical Production.' Also verbatim: 'The opportunity for the students to work as both assistants and in some cases primary engineers at MIAM's recording studios during their studies is one of the most invaluable aspects of the program. These recording and mixing experiences compel the students to prepare different recording setups, mixes and masters for various genres and ensembles.' The concentration 'seeks to address the technical, commercial, and musical aspects of the discipline in equal measure' and requires students to take courses from every other concentration area as well. Compulsory-pool courses shared with all MIAM masters include Music Technology, Multitrack Recording and Mixing, Critical Listening, History of Electronic Music, Audio Programming, Music Business and Management.
recommendation: The most industry-facing English-taught recording and mixing master's in the region, at public-university prices, and formally open to a non-music bachelor. But it has the strictest gate in this slice for someone in his exact position: three self-made mixes, each with a microphone-recorded acoustic track, no downloaded or AI material. He has none of that today. Realistic plan: treat SED as the 2028 target and Sonic Arts at the same institution as the 2027 door — same building, same studios, same faculty, and he can take Multitrack Recording and Mixing, Advanced Mixing and Mastering and Studio Practices as electives from inside Sonic Arts anyway. If he does want SED for 2027, he needs to start recording live sources (a singer, a guitarist, a drum kit, a string player) within the next few months.

study: IAD's sound training covers the full sound-engineer profession: studio and live recording, mixing, editing, mastering, event sound reinforcement (sonorisation) and sound design. The master combines artistic courses, technical courses and workshops, and trains 'sound engineers who master sound recording tools and techniques in radio, television and multimedia, as well as editors and sound mixers who master editing and sound mixing tools'. Master components: artistic and technical coursework with workshops, an in-depth internship (more advanced than at bachelor level), a final work evaluated by a jury of industry professionals, and a written thesis. Students collaborate with IAD's multimedia, theatre and directing programmes on real productions.
recommendation: A serious, very practical French-language route into professional audio, and the most degree-agnostic admission wording in the Belgian set ('most masters are open to students holding a bachelor's degree or equivalent') — meaning his software-engineering BSc is not automatically disqualifying. Son Studio is the orientation closest to music recording and mixing. Two real frictions: it is a 60-ECTS master built on top of IAD's own 180-ECTS sound bachelor, so the assumed technical baseline is high, and admission requires an in-person jury in Louvain-la-Neuve in late August/early September. No scholarship route was found, so budget c. €4,175 supplement plus minerval as self-pay.

entry: Per the course registers: a level-6 diploma (bac+3 / licence or equivalent) AND 'un diplôme de musique ou équivalent'. Full verbatim conditions d'accès could NOT be retrieved — formations.univ-gustave-eiffel.fr returned HTTP 503 on repeated attempts. UNVERIFIED at the exact-wording level.
acceptsNonMusic: PROBABLY NOT AS WRITTEN, BUT UNVERIFIED. The register wording requires a bachelor 'and a music degree or equivalent' — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies the first limb and not the second. 'Ou équivalent' is the opening: SAE's own admissions culture is competence-based rather than degree-based, and the sister licence at Gustave Eiffel is 'Arts — parcours Musique et métiers du son', a technical route. NO DIRECT QUOTE COULD BE OBTAINED — this is the most important single question to put to master.musique@univ-eiffel.fr.

The sister MIM parcours requires transcripts, a motivation letter, a short CV and a research or research-creation project; MPM being the professional parcours, expect a production portfolio instead, but NO track count, length or format is published.

Whether a practical production test is set is UNKNOWN and should be asked directly — for this candidate the answer decides everything.

Combines 'les aspects créatifs, théoriques et de recherche' from Université Gustave Eiffel (formerly Paris-Est Marne-la-Vallée) with SAE Institute Paris's '40 years of professional and technical expertise in sound engineering education' on professional-grade studio equipment. M2 aims to 'poursuivre une démarche pratique et créative' and to 'développer la capacité à concevoir et mener à bien des tâches variées en musique et production audio'. Stated careers: 'directeur de studio d'enregistrement, producteur/réalisateur musical, directeur artistique, compositeur, arrangeur, orchestrateur, adaptateur, technicien du son.'

institution: Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg
programme: Filmton / Sounddesign (Diplomaufbaustudium – postgraduate diploma)
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: Three independent blockers, any one of which is fatal: it demands German at B2 and he has none; it ends in a Filmakademie Diplom rather than a recognised master's degree; and admission runs through an in-person multi-day entrance exam including a 72-hour practical task that assumes existing studio and DAW craft. It is also film post-production, not electronic music.
correction: DEGREE TYPE: the input treats this as a master-level option. It is not a master's — it awards a "Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg" from a Diplomaufbaustudium, not an accredited second-cycle degree. GATE: 'Exam/interview only' understates it — the exam includes a 72-hour set practical task plus a colloquium, in person. LANGUAGE: German B2 (Goethe B2 / TestDaF 4 / DSH-2) is required and is not flagged in the input.
qualification: Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg. IMPORTANT CAVEAT NOW CONFIRMED: this is an institutional diploma, described by the academy as 'vergleichbar berufsbefähigenden Abschlüssen' of state art universities under Baden-Württemberg law — i.e. comparable to a professional qualifying degree. It is NOT an accredited M.A./M.F.A. and the pages do not state an EQF/ECTS master equivalence. If he needs a recognised master's degree (for a visa track, a later PhD, or recognition in Tunisia), verify this in writing first.
tuition: CORRECTED AND MORE EXPENSIVE THAN RECORDED: the €1,500 is PER SEMESTER, not a one-off. The academy's fee schedule is €0/semester for a first degree, €650/semester for a second degree or Projektstudium, and €1,500/semester for non-EU citizens, plus a €131.50 semester contribution for everyone. As a Tunisian national over 5 semesters that is roughly €7,500 in fees plus ~€658 in contributions — about €8,150 total, before living costs. The Diplomaufbaustudiengänge are exempt from the second-degree fee, but NOT from the non-EU fee.
scholarshipDetail: None found at the academy. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships (Film/Fine Art strand), Deutschlandstipendium. DAAD/Tunisia eligibility NOT re-verified in this pass. Note that DAAD art/film scholarships generally target accredited degree programmes, so the non-master status of this Diplom should be checked against DAAD's eligibility rules before counting on it.
entry: General/subject-specific Hochschulreife (with a talent clause, the 'Begabtenpassus' under §10 of the exam regulations, for applicants without Abitur — an extended interview substitutes). For the Diplomaufbaustudiengänge specifically, an 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' is required, submitted as an officially certified copy. Applicants must bring working knowledge of studio audio technology, microphones and DAW operation. B2 German per the academy's general standard.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — most likely YES, but with one conflicting signal. The programme-overview table requires only 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' with NO subject restriction, and no music degree is anywhere demanded — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies that on its face. However, the general application page summarises Diplomaufbaustudium entry as requiring a 'completed degree in a related field', which introduces a relatedness test that is not defined for Filmton. A software-engineering degree is plausibly 'related' to audio technology, but he must get this confirmed in writing before applying. The decisive filter in practice is the Pro Tools practical exam, not the bachelor subject.
portfolio: PARTIAL. Own projects/work samples are uploaded via the online portal, and applicants must clearly identify their individual contribution to each. Published technical limits (example spec, varies by department): video up to 1 GB, MP4 container, H.264 codec, data rate 15 MB/s, typically 5–7 minutes maximum. The exact number and duration of AUDIO samples required for Filmton/Sounddesign is not published — UNVERIFIED. Also submit certified copies of the Hochschulreife and of any Vordiplom/Diplom/Bachelor/Master.
audition: YES — pre-selection on the file, then an on-site Aufnahmeprüfung conducted IN PRO TOOLS. Confirmed: 'Die Aufnahmeprüfung für Filmton/Sounddesign wird mit dem Programm Pro Tools durchgeführt. Bewerber*innen sollten daher Grundkenntnisse in den Disziplinen Aufnahme, Sounddesign, Mischung und Bouncing mitbringen.' There is NO instrumental audition and no music-theory paper — the gate is a DAW competence test. This is by far the most learnable audition of the six programmes here.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February, annually and without a year published on the programme page. The 2026 cycle ran with a portal opening on 7 January 2026 and the standard 15 February deadline (other departments had later dates: Motion Design 15 May 2026, Werbefilm Producing lateral entry 7 April 2026). For a 2027 start plan on 15 February 2027 and confirm when posted.
opens: The online portal opened 7 January in the current (2026) cycle. Expect a comparable early-January opening for the 2027 cycle — confirm.
duration: 4 semesters plus 1 diploma semester for the final project = 5 semesters total. ECTS NOT published — UNVERIFIED.
study: CONFIRMED: production of the audio layers of film and television. Year 1 concentrates on original sound recording on set; year 2 on post-production. Content includes location recording, sound design, mixing in a DAW, cinema film mixing and Dolby Atmos, working with Foley artists, film-music recording and mixing, and dialogue editing. Optional specialisations in media design and sound for games. Entirely project-based — students work on the academy's own film productions.
recommendation: The most realistically ENTERABLE film-sound route in Germany for someone without a music degree — the gate is a Pro Tools practical test he can genuinely train for, not a conservatory audition or a theory paper, and no music bachelor is demanded. But verification worsened two things: the fee is €1,500 PER SEMESTER (~€8,150 total, no funding found), and the award is an institutional Diplom rather than an accredited master's. And it makes film and game sound designers, not DJs or producers. Only worth an application if he decides he genuinely wants a screen-audio career alongside producing, and only after confirming both the degree recognition and whether his SE bachelor counts as 'related'.

Theoretical and applied acoustics, digital audio, sound signal processing, music technologies, multimedia systems. correction: DUPLICATE: indexes 33 and 34 are the same Saint Louis Music Production biennio, entered twice with contradictory cost bands (EUR 1.5k-5k/yr vs EUR 5k-15k/yr) and contradictory funding ('Partial' in both, but index 33 lists 'Partial' and the sibling Live Electronics rows differ). qualification: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello (Master-level)
