The exact biennio figure is set case by case and is calculated from an ISEE income certificate submitted each year — request a formal quote (preventivo) from the Segreteria Didattica. TREAT AS UNVERIFIED.
scholarshipDetail: LAZIODISCO (Lazio regional right-to-study agency) grants; Saint Louis also publishes its own scholarships/funding page (saintlouis.eu/borse-di-studio)
entry: Stated requirement: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio" (conditional enrolment possible). Attendance is compulsory at a minimum of 80% of classes; a part-time route exists for students who cannot attend everything. Erasmus+ mobility of up to 12 months within the biennio is available.
acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — this is the weak point. The published requirement names a "diploma accademico triennale di primo livello" (an Italian first-level academic diploma in music). Italian law generally allows a university laurea to serve as the entry title for a biennio, and Saint Louis runs an international students office, but the page does NOT say so. He must confirm in writing whether a BSc in Software Engineering is accepted, and whether they would require bridging credits.
portfolio: VERIFIED and exact for the pre-selection stage: "Registra uno o più video contenenti 3 brani, eseguiti da te in gruppo (minimo trio) che siano rappresentativi della tua attività artistica" — record one or more videos containing THREE PIECES, performed by you in a group of at least a TRIO, representative of your artistic activity; files must be uploaded to YouTube or a similar web portal and the LINKS entered in the application form. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this ensemble-video wording is the shared text used across Saint Louis's academic courses and is clearly written for performer tracks — for the Music Production biennio you should ask the Segreteria in writing what the equivalent production portfolio is (most likely produced/mixed tracks rather than a live trio video). Also mandatory: download and check the Piano di studi, which lists the competences tested in each individual prova.
audition: Two-stage: (1) pre-selection on the submitted video links; (2) for those who pass, admission tests held ON SITE in Rome over TWO CONSECUTIVE DAYS, in the June and September sessions. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year, drawn from Saint Louis's own first-level graduates plus external candidates selected by audition.
deadline: 30 April (published standing window: "dal 3 febbraio al 30 aprile"); later applications considered only against remaining places. Admission tests in June and September. Confirm the 2027 edition.
opens: 3 February (published standing window). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm the 2027 dates, but Saint Louis states this as its annual rule rather than a one-off date.
duration: 2 years; approx. 300 contact hours per year. CFA total UNVERIFIED (the standard is 120 CFA for an Italian biennio).
study: Verified from the official page. Each student learns to run a music-production project through every phase, from the creative idea to arrangement with real and virtual instruments, recording, mixing and mastering. Named modules: LABORATORIO DI PRODUZIONE — developing original projects with a music-producer's approach to the whole production chain; TECNICHE DI RIPRESA E REGISTRAZIONE — each specialising student produces TWO TRACKS end-to-end, from pre-production and arrangement through rehearsals, recording and overdubbing, microphone choice and placement, editing, mixing and mastering; ORCHESTRAZIONE — professional virtual orchestration, arrangement, real and virtual instruments, sound construction within the production; ANALISI DELLA PRODUZIONE MUSICALE — evolution of the producer's role, the approaches of the most influential producers in history, and the compositional/structural/expressive techniques of the main contemporary popular-music languages, completed with sound design applied to the timbral character of a track; DIRITTO D'AUTORE, ROYALTIES E CONTRATTUALISTICA — copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts. The bienni are explicitly "costruiti intorno alle inclinazioni artistiche di ciascuno studente", built around each student's own artistic direction, with original productions and third-party commissioned work running through the whole degree.
recommendation: The single closest match in this whole slice to 'I want to be a producer': the syllabus is arrangement, recording, mixing, mastering, sound design and music-industry contracts, and each student ships two fully produced tracks plus original productions built around their own artistic direction. Two real obstacles: (1) it is fee-paying, so it is a partial-funding rather than fully-funded route; (2) the stated entry title is an Italian first-level music diploma, so his non-music BSc needs written confirmation before he invests in an application. Fortnightly two-day teaching blocks also make it unusually compatible with continuing to work.

And from music for media to games and interactive installations.' The Music Production strand is genuinely about making records; the pathway as a whole spans media/games too.

institution: Music Production Academy
programme: Full Course (Beginners), Full Course (Advanced), Full Course Year 2, DJ Lessons, Private Lessons
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's
qualification: NO RECOGNISED QUALIFICATION — but a CORRECTION to my earlier 'nothing is awarded'. The site does state that the Full Courses lead to an 'Ableton and Steinberg certified diploma'. Read that carefully: it is a VENDOR/SOFTWARE certification from two DAW manufacturers, NOT an educational accreditation. Ableton and Steinberg are companies selling software; their certification programmes attest to software proficiency and to the trainer's status as an approved trainer. It carries no ECTS, no degree status, no ministerial or NVAO recognition, and no standing with any immigration authority or university admissions office. It is a useful line on a CV and nothing more. Not a master, not a degree.
accreditation: NOT NVAO — CONFIRMED. No CRKBO, no NRTO, no educational accreditation of any kind is claimed anywhere on the site. The ONLY 'certification' claimed is vendor certification from Ableton and Steinberg, which is a commercial software-partner scheme, not accreditation. This remains the weakest accreditation position of any provider in this slice: AV Sound Education at least holds CRKBO. Private, 'niet-bekostigd', wholly outside the Dutch education system. Practical consequence: no CRKBO means no 0% VAT exemption either.
tuition: UNVERIFIED — no figure published anywhere on the site. I will not estimate. VAT treatment also unknown (no CRKBO, so no exemption).
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — nothing published. Registration fees, materials, studio access charges and exam or certification fees are all unknown. Note that Ableton and Steinberg certification exams normally carry their own vendor fees; whether those are included is not stated.
totalCost: CANNOT BE ESTIMATED — no pricing is published at any point on the site. Any figure would be invention. He must obtain a written quotation covering tuition, VAT, registration, materials and certification fees before engaging.
scholarshipDetail: NONE published. No bursary, no non-EU award, no Tunisian-specific support. Not eligible for the Holland Scholarship or DUO, both of which require accredited institutions.
entry: Beginners course: none published — open commercial enrolment, consistent with a course explicitly aimed at beginners. portfolio: None published for the Beginners course. For the Advanced course an audition is required but its specification — what to prepare, what is assessed, how it is delivered — is NOT published. UNVERIFIED.

deadline: UNVERIFIED — no deadline published. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
opens: UNVERIFIED — no application window, process or opening date is published. Enquiry appears to be by direct contact only.
duration: CORRECTION — DURATION IS NOW VERIFIED. The Full Course is a ONE-YEAR programme: the site describes it as granting 'the knowledge for a lifetime in a one-year program'. englishTest: NONE published. No IELTS, no language certificate requirement appears anywhere. Given the language of instruction itself is unstated, this is moot until that is confirmed.
study: Music production across a beginner-to-advanced one-year progression, plus a second year focused on 'development as a composer, audio engineer and performing artist', plus DJ lessons and fully customisable private lessons ('your genre', 'your DAW'). recommendation: AVOID. This is the thinnest proposition in the slice. Verification this cycle added only two facts — that the Full Course runs one year, and that it leads to an Ableton/Steinberg VENDOR certificate — and both make the picture worse rather than better: he would be committing a full year, at an undisclosed price, to a course whose only credential is a software-manufacturer badge. Set against that: no accreditation, no price, no syllabus, no dates, no named staff, no visa. And note the asymmetry that matters most — it advertises to exactly his profile (non-EU international student) while being structurally incapable of sponsoring him and quietly handing the visa problem to an outside agency. Anything that does that deserves scepticism as a matter of principle. There is nothing available here that he cannot get better, cheaper, more transparently and with published pricing from DJ School Amsterdam, which quotes EUR 2,499 openly, teaches one-to-one in English, and can be done inside a tourist visa. Do not engage.

institution: SAE Institute Amsterdam
programme: Advanced Mixing & Mastering Certificate (4 months) — ONLINE

qualification: SAE Certificate. NOT a master, NOT a degree, NOT NVAO-accredited, no ECTS. A short vocational certificate issued by SAE itself.

tuition: VERIFIED on the official 2026/2027 fee page: €2,960 UPFRONT (= €500 registration + €2,460 tuition) or €3,404 MONTHLY (= €500 registration + 4 × €726). No EU/non-EU differential is published — a non-EU student pays the same. Paying monthly costs €444 more.
otherFees: CORRECTION — the €500 registration fee is ALREADY INCLUDED in the €2,960 / €3,404 headline figures; it is NOT an additional charge on top. Earlier records double-counted it. No enrolment, materials, exam or insurance fee is published. NOT included and unpriced: his own Pro Tools licence, computer and monitoring (see equipmentRequired).
totalCost: €2,960–€3,404 all-in for tuition and registration, with NO travel or accommodation cost since it is online. Add €300–€1,500 for a Pro Tools licence and monitoring if he does not already own them. Realistic total: €3,000–€4,900. scholarshipDetail: NONE. No scholarship, bursary, fee waiver or discount of any kind for non-EU or Tunisian applicants. Not eligible for Dutch student finance (non-degree, private institution).
entry: No formal entry requirement published for this certificate. SAE's institutional baseline is age 18, intermediate secondary education and intermediate English. The 'Advanced' label implies prior production familiarity but no prerequisite is stated on the course page — CONFIRM in writing with admissions.
acceptsNonMusic: YES in practice — no music degree, diploma or prior qualification is required or mentioned anywhere on the course page. SAE operates open entry across its certificate range. However nothing is published that positively confirms a complete beginner is welcome on this specific 'Advanced' course, so the wording cannot be quoted verbatim. Treat as: accepted, but he should already be comfortable in a DAW.
portfolio: NONE. No portfolio, demo or showreel is required — verified absent from the course page. This is one of the very few audio programmes anywhere he could enter TODAY with no portfolio built.
audition: None. No audition, interview or entrance test published.
deadline: No published hard deadline — rolling admission until the intake fills. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: only the September 2026 and January 2027 starts are published. A September 2027 equivalent is likely but NOT yet announced.
opens: Rolling — registration is open now via saeamsterdam.com/registration. No fixed opening date; SAE admits until cohorts fill.
duration: 4 months, ONLINE delivery. No ECTS, no credit. Structure verified: weeks 1–8 two lessons per week; week 9 event week; weeks 10–16 three 90-minute mixing sessions, three 90-minute mastering sessions, plus weekly 1-on-1 mentorship.
englishTest: NO IELTS requirement published for this certificate, and no formal test score of any kind. SAE's general baseline is 'intermediate English' assessed informally. He would almost certainly NOT need to sit IELTS for this course — a genuine cost saving. UNVERIFIED in writing; confirm.
study: VERIFIED published syllabus: Summing, Levelling & Metering; Phase Management; Stereo Bus Processing; Creating Space & Headroom; Limiters & Clippers; Multi-band Compression & Group Processing; Ambience Matching & Mix Cohesion. Taught in Pro Tools. Weeks 10–16 add six supervised 90-minute mixing/mastering sessions plus weekly one-to-one mentorship. Head instructor: Federico Naccari (MA Sound Design, Bath Spa University; runs a professional Amsterdam studio).
recommendation: THE ONLY ENTRY IN THIS SLICE HE CAN ACCESS RIGHT NOW, FROM TUNISIA, WITH NO VISA AND NO PORTFOLIO. That is a real and unusual advantage and it is why this ranks above the two Abbey Road entries despite costing a fraction as much. It also targets exactly the craft he named (mixing, mastering, studio workflow) and would let him BUILD the portfolio that Abbey Road and every accredited master will demand of him. But be clear about what it is not: it is not a degree, carries no ECTS, will not transfer toward a September 2027 master, and will not support any visa. At €2,960 it is priced like a qualification and delivers training. MY ADVICE: do NOT treat this as a substitute for an accredited master. If he has €3,000 spare AND already owns a Pro Tools rig, it is a defensible investment in portfolio-building ahead of 2027 applications. If money is tight — and the brief says it is — the same €3,000 is better spent on gear, a Pro Tools licence and self-directed work, keeping the cash for application fees, IELTS and relocation. Confirm in writing before paying: (1) that the course is online and what campus access, if any, is included; (2) whether a Pro Tools licence is provided or must be bought; (3) whether a September 2027 intake will run.

city: Belgrade (delivered in person at the Be…
institution: Univerzitet Metropolitan
programme: Master akademske studije MUZIČKA PRODUKCIJA (MAS Music Production), Fakultet digitalnih umetnosti
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: Taught entirely in Serbian, which he does not speak, and structurally blocked besides: he needs 240 ECTS and holds 180, so he would first pay for a fourth undergraduate year, then sit differential exams as a non-cognate applicant, then pay €4,500 for a one-year 60-ECTS degree with zero funding available to foreigners. Every part of that is money and time spent to end up with half a master's in a language he cannot study in.
correction: The record's gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' is WRONG — no audition, no portfolio and no entrance exam are published anywhere; the only hurdle is documentary plus differential exams for non-cognate applicants. The record also fails to flag the two killers: the programme is Serbian-language only with no English variant on the accreditation register, and it requires 240 ECTS, which a 180-ECTS Tunisian licence does not meet.
qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS), 60 ECTS, 1 year, 2 semesters. Professional title: 'Master muzički producent' (Master Music Producer). Field declared as IMT (interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary/dual-field); areas: Dramatic and Audiovisual Arts + Management and Business. This is a genuine second-cycle academic degree, not a private certificate — confirmed by its presence in the national register of accredited programmes.
accreditation: ACCREDITED — CORRECTED and now pinned to a specific decision, replacing the previous record's 'specific accreditation decision number/date NOT published — UNVERIFIED'. The National Body for Accreditation and Quality Assurance in Higher Education (NAT) register of 21 July 2026 lists, under Univerzitet „Metropolitan“, entry 53: 'ИМТ МАС - МУЗИЧКА ПРОДУКЦИЈА, 03.06.2025, БС 20'. So: accredited 3 June 2025, field IMT, approved annual intake 20 students, valid 7 years to June 2032. This is newer than the Novi Sad programme's accreditation and comfortably covers a 2027 entry. Institution accreditation 04.06.2010 / 21.07.2017 / 21.01.2025.
tuition: EUR 4,500 for the degree — CORRECTED, and this is the single most important change to this record. The previous agent reported the non-EU rate as 'NOT PUBLISHED, do not assume it is EUR 4,500, private Serbian universities commonly charge non-regional students more' and built its whole recommendation on that warning. That is wrong. Metropolitan's official master admission page states, under 'Upis stranih državljana': 'Strani državljanin može se upisati na studijski program pod istim uslovima kao i domaći državljani, KAO I POD ISTIM USLOVIMA FINANSIRANJA ŠKOLARINE' — a foreign national enrols under the same conditions as domestic citizens AND under the same tuition-financing conditions. There is no separate foreigner tariff. A Tunisian therefore pays EUR 4,500, the same as a Serbian. The residual caveat is real but minor: the price tables themselves are headed 'ŠKOLARINE ZA NOVE STUDENTE (u EUR) za državljane Srbije i bivših republika SFR Jugoslavije', so the two official statements sit in tension and it is worth one confirming e-mail — but the correct working figure is EUR 4,500, not 'unknown and probably higher'.
otherFees: CORRECTED from 'not published'. Published figures: administrative fee 1,000 RSD payable with the enrolment documents; on enrolment all students must pay a 20% deposit (akontacija) — EUR 900 for this programme — plus a further 20% as the first instalment, no later than 1 October; enrolling after 1 September requires 40% of the tuition up front; the remaining balance runs as 11 monthly instalments of EUR 327.27 with no interest. DISCOUNT: candidates who enrol preliminarily and pay the 20% deposit by 31 March receive a 10% tuition discount, valid for the first year of studies only, and discounts cannot be combined. Nostrification/recognition of his Tunisian diploma is required and is charged separately by the recognising body. Health-insurance cost for foreign students — UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: EUR 4,500 tuition for the one-year 60-ECTS master, or about EUR 4,050 with the 31 March early-payment discount, plus ~1,000 RSD administrative fee and separate diploma-recognition costs, before living costs in Belgrade, visa and health insurance. If his degree is 180 ECTS he must first fund a fourth bachelor year at Metropolitan, which on the published bachelor table runs EUR 2,990–3,990 depending on programme — pushing the realistic total past EUR 7,000–8,500. Against the state Academy of Arts Novi Sad at EUR 1,800 for a comparable one-year MAS, this is roughly 2.5x on tuition alone. It fails his 'self-pay only if genuinely cheap' test.
scholarshipDetail: CONFIRMED: nothing a Tunisian master applicant can win. Re-checked the official Stipendije page. What exists: (1) competition-based full four-year bachelor scholarships for Serbian secondary-school pupils; (2) internal merit scholarships for existing Metropolitan undergraduates in years 2–4, six per year, one per faculty per year level, with fourth-years able to continue tuition-free into a master; (3) a dual-education package created with A+Crowd of Toronto offering free study, EUR 100/month and a guaranteed job, aimed at school-leavers entering IT, management or design. None is open to an incoming foreign master applicant in music production. Anything else would have to be negotiated directly with upis@metropolitan.ac.rs.
entry: MATERIALLY CORRECTED — the previous record's claim that entry requirements are 'NOT PUBLISHED' is WRONG. They are published in full at https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/upis/upis-na-master-akademske-studije/ under 'Opšti uslovi upisa na Master studije'. (1) BASE RULE: 'Na studijske programe Master akademskih studija mogu se upisati studenti koji su prethodno završili četvorogodišnje i ostvarili uslov od 240 ESPB' — a completed four-year bachelor with 240 ECTS, the same gate as Novi Sad. (2) BUT THERE IS A PUBLISHED ROUTE OUT, which Novi Sad does not offer: 'Studenti koji su završili tri godine osnovnih akademskih studija i stekli 180 ESPB bodova imaju mogućnost da upišu četvrtu godinu akademskih studija Univerziteta Metropolitan i nakon završetka iste steknu zvanje diplomirani, na taj način ostvarivši uslov za upis na Master studije' — a holder of a three-year 180-ECTS bachelor may enrol in the FOURTH YEAR of a Metropolitan bachelor programme, obtain the 'diplomirani' title, and thereby qualify for the master. That is directly relevant to him if his Tunisian licence is 180 ECTS, at the cost of an extra year and extra fees. (3) COGNATE vs NON-COGNATE: 'Iz srodne oblasti, određuju se predmeti programa za nastavu u trajanju od godinu dana. Iz nesrodne oblasti, komisija određuje uslove upisa, predlaže nastavni plan i program, utvrđujući broj diferencijalnih ispita koje kandidat mora da položi.' A non-cognate first degree is expressly provided for, via differential exams set by a faculty commission. (4) DOCUMENTS: certified copy of the diploma (or graduation certificate); certified copy of the transcript of passed exams (or diploma supplement); birth certificate showing citizenship; two identical 3.5x4.5 cm photographs; proof of payment of a 1,000 RSD administrative fee; proof of payment of the first tuition instalment; ŠV-20 form (completed at the faculty, not purchased). (5) FOREIGN NATIONALS: they submit a NOSTRIFIED diploma stating the ECTS achieved, or, if recognition is still running, a certificate that the procedure is under way.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — CORRECTED from the previous record's 'probably yes on marketing copy, UNVERIFIED'. It is published policy, not marketing: the master admission rules expressly contemplate applicants 'iz nesrodne oblasti' (from an unrelated field) and provide the mechanism — a faculty commission sets the admission conditions and the number of differential exams. The programme page separately states the studies are intended for 'muzičare, muzičke producente, izvođače, kao i sve zainteresovane kandidate koji žele da kreiraju ili unaprede sopstvenu karijeru u muzičkoj industriji'. So a software-engineering graduate is admissible in principle, subject to differential exams. What he cannot avoid is that those differential exams, like the degree, will be in Serbian.
portfolio: No portfolio required — this is now a confirmed published finding rather than an unknown. The official master admission page describes the full procedure (online application, then scanned diploma and transcript, then referral to the faculty commission which issues individual admission conditions) and no portfolio appears anywhere in it, nor on the programme page. For an applicant with no body of work yet, this is a genuine structural advantage over both Novi Sad programmes.
audition: No entrance exam or audition for master entry — confirmed by the published admission procedure, which routes the application to a faculty commission that sets conditions and any differential exams rather than testing the candidate. (The prijemni ispit and the 'direct enrolment without an entrance exam' offer advertised elsewhere on the site relate to bachelor admission.)
deadline: No published application deadline — rolling admission. The binding dates are financial and immigration ones, not academic: 20% deposit plus 20% first instalment by 1 October; 40% up front if enrolling after 1 September; 31 March for the 10% early-payment discount; and, dominating all of these, the visa D and residence-permit timeline plus the diploma-nostrification timeline, which he should start at least six months ahead.
opens: Rolling, online via the university's application portal. After the online application the candidate receives procedural instructions and submits scanned diploma and transcript; the file then goes to the faculty commission, which issues individual admission conditions and any differential exams. Practical planning date: pay the 20% deposit by 31 March 2027 to secure the 10% discount for a 2027/28 start.
duration: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED on the official programme page. Note the university's generic master page markets 'master diploma in 10 months'.
languageReq: Not published for this programme — UNVERIFIED. The published master admission rules impose no language certificate. In practice, delivery is Serbian-only, so functional Serbian is a de facto requirement whatever the paperwork says. Ask upis@metropolitan.ac.rs in writing.
englishTest: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and irrelevant: the programme is not taught in English, so no IELTS/TOEFL band would help him here.
study: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official programme page. Semester 1: AD511 Muzička produkcija 1 (audio technology, music software, arranging, microphone placement, instrument miking, basic mixing and mastering); AD560 Kreativna radionica zvuka (creative sound workshop — practical sound-design projects, experimentation with digital audio tools, sound installations, history of music-scenic performance); AD570 Novi mediji i tehnologija u performansu; Elective block 1 (MK520 Kreiranje digitalnog brenda / MK525 Digitalne marketinške kampanje); Elective block 2 (AD535 Advertajzing / AD565 Digitalna kultura). Semester 2: AD512 Muzička produkcija 2 (theory of analogue and digital recording and sound processing, equipment and techniques, sound formats and carriers); MG525 Upravljanje inovacijama i tehnologijama; Elective 3 (MG535 Digitalno preduzetništvo / MG545 Strateški menadžment i liderstvo); AD591 Završni rad muzičke produkcije – SIR; AD592 Završni rad – izrada i odbrana. Roughly a third of the taught credits are management/marketing, which a software engineer would handle comfortably.
recommendation: This record needed substantial correction and the programme comes out of it looking better on paper and worse in practice than the previous assessment implied. Three corrections he must hear. FIRST, the previous warning that the price is unknown and probably higher for a non-EU national is WRONG: Metropolitan's own admission rules state that foreign nationals enrol under the same conditions and the same tuition-financing conditions as Serbian citizens, so he pays EUR 4,500 — the published figure, not a mystery. SECOND, the claim that admission requirements are unpublished is also WRONG: they are published in detail, and they are more accommodating than anything at Novi Sad — 240 ECTS required but with an explicit route for a 180-ECTS three-year graduate to complete a fourth Metropolitan bachelor year first; non-cognate first degrees expressly admitted via commission-set differential exams; no entrance exam; no portfolio; rolling admission; full document list published. THIRD, the accreditation is now nailed down: NAT register, accredited 3 June 2025, approved intake 20, in-person Serbian delivery. So it is a real, state-recognised, visa-supporting second-cycle degree — the AVOID verdict reserved for master-priced non-degrees does not apply. What actually blocks him is language and money, not admissions. The programme is accredited for Serbian-language in-person delivery only — the register carries no English-language flag, unlike Metropolitan's own IT and business masters — so an Arabic/French/English speaker cannot follow it in September 2027. And EUR 4,500 (EUR 4,050 with the March discount), or EUR 7,000+ if he must buy a fourth bachelor year first, is 2.5x the state Academy in Novi Sad for a private-university degree with no scholarship he can win. Action if he still wants it: one e-mail to upis@metropolitan.ac.rs asking (a) to confirm in writing that the EUR 4,500 rate applies to a Tunisian national given that the price table is headed for Serbian and ex-SFRY citizens, (b) whether his specific BSc counts as 240 ECTS or requires the fourth-year route, (c) how many differential exams a software-engineering graduate would be set, (d) whether any part of the programme can be followed in English, and (e) whether they issue the enrolment documents needed for a Serbian study visa D.
url: https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/master-studije/muzicka-produkcija/ (official programme page — 60 ECTS, title Master muzički producent, full course list with descriptions, AS Studioton partnership, in-person delivery, EUR 4,500 fee table headed for Serbian/ex-SFRY nationals); https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/upis/upis-na-master-akademske-studije/ (official master admission rules — 240 ECTS requirement, fourth-year route for 180-ECTS holders, cognate vs non-cognate differential exams, full document list, and the foreign-national clause confirming identical tuition-financing conditions); https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/upis/skolarine/ (official 2026/27 price list — master table headed 'nastava na srpskom jeziku', EUR 4,500 with EUR 900 deposit and 11 x EUR 327.27, 31 March 10% discount, 1 October payment rule); https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/o-univerzitetu/akreditacija/ (work licence 2010 with amendments to Nov 2025, accreditation decisions 2017 and 2025); https://www.metropolitan.ac.rs/stipendije/ (scholarships — none for incoming foreign master applicants); https://www.nat.rs/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Vodič-za-studente-21.07.2026.pdf (Serbian National Accreditation Body register, 21.07.2026 — Univerzitet „Metropolitan“ entry 53, IMT MAS Muzička produkcija accredited 03.06.2025, intake 20, no English-language and no distance-learning variant)

institution: CICE — La Escuela Profesional de Nuevas Tecnologías
programme: Máster en Producción Musical Discográfica e Ingeniería de Sonido — Oficial de AVID (MPD)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's
qualification: A CICE private professional certificate branded 'Máster', bundled with software-vendor certifications (Avid Pro Tools, Waves Level A). No university validation, no ECTS, 300 teaching hours.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL — and the naming is actively misleading. The word 'Oficial' in the title 'Máster ... - Oficial de AVID' means OFFICIAL AVID CERTIFICATION, a software-vendor credential, NOT Spanish academic accreditation. There is no ANECA verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no EHEA status and no PhD access. Independent confirmation of its nature: the Emagister listing describes the outcome as conferring professional specialisation status 'rather than an academic degree'. It is a private certificate course. The decisive new number is the DURATION: 300 teaching hours (with roughly 600 hours of total student dedication). A genuine 60-ECTS master implies about 1,500 hours. At 300 taught hours this is one-fifth the size of the cheapest real master in this batch — it is a short course wearing the word 'máster'.
tuition: €4,233 (IVA included, after a 17% discount) for the 300-hour programme. Undiscounted list price appears to be around €5,100. No separate non-EU rate is published. UNVERIFIED against CICE directly.
otherFees: CONFLICTING EVIDENCE, resolve before paying. The Emagister listing states the certifications are included, naming both the 'Certificación Oficial de Waves Level A' and official AVID certification as part of the programme. A separate source indicated the price includes Waves Level A but NOT the Avid Pro Tools certifications. Since those vendor exams are the programme's entire selling point, this ambiguity is material — insist on a written statement naming every exam included and every exam billed separately, with amounts. Application, enrolment and materials fees UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: Roughly €4,233 for the course itself, plus a Mac and a Pro Tools subscription, plus possibly unbundled certification exam fees. As a route to Spain the figure is moot — it cannot support a visa, so Madrid living costs do not arise. As a skills purchase for someone already resident: €4,200–€6,000 all in.
scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED — none published, and nothing for non-EU applicants.
entry: Published prerequisites are technical, not academic, and VERIFIED: 'Conocimientos de Sistema Operativo Mac, nivel usuario'; 'Conocimientos de Protools u otra plataforma similar, nivel usuario'; and basic English proficiency. No degree requirement of any kind is stated.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — trivially. No academic or music prerequisite exists at all; the bar is Mac OS and Pro Tools user-level familiarity, which a software-engineering graduate clears immediately. But read this the right way: a programme with NO degree requirement whatsoever is not a postgraduate qualification in any meaningful sense, whatever it is called.
portfolio: None.
audition: None.
deadline: No published deadline. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates; the Lectiva listing still shows a May 2018 start date, which is how stale some of this school's published data is.
opens: Rolling / 'fechas a elegir'. In-person Madrid enrolment currently shown as closed.
duration: 300 teaching hours, with approximately 600 hours of total student dedication. No ECTS published. NEWLY VERIFIED — the input recorded duration as entirely unknown.
englishTest: No IELTS. 'Elementary English competency' is a stated entry requirement (for vendor documentation), but instruction is in Spanish.
study: Ten modules, VERIFIED: (1) Sound and Capture; (2) Processors and Production Phases; (3) Capture History and Advanced Techniques; (4) Analysis Keys for Productions; (5) Introduction to Mixing and Mastering; (6) Mixer History and Studio Performance Optimisation; (7) Mixing Architecture; (8) Dynamic Control and 3D Depth Mixing; (9) Official Waves Level A Certification; (10) Mixing According to Musical Styles. Note what is ABSENT: no synthesis, no sound design, no composition, no live performance, no DJ technique, no music business.
recommendation: AVOID as anything to do with his move to Spain. This is a 300-hour vendor-certification bootcamp with the word 'máster' attached and the word 'Oficial' borrowed from Avid's marketing rather than from ANECA. It cannot support a student visa — 300 hours cannot produce 20 contact hours a week over 90+ days, and it is sold online as readily as in person. It is also aimed at the wrong craft: pure studio engineering, with no synthesis, no sound design, no composition, no live performance and no DJ content anywhere in the ten modules. For a software engineer who wants Pro Tools and Waves credentials cheaply it has genuine, narrow utility — but that is a €4,000 skills purchase for someone already living in Madrid, not a postgraduate route into Europe for a Tunisian graduate. If he ever does pursue it, insist first on a current written price stating exactly which certification exams are included, because the advertised figure already carries a 17% discount and the exam bundling is contradicted between sources.

accreditation: Accredited FWB master. VERIFIED — ARTS² publishes the 2025/26 'MU MASTER À FINALITÉ SPÉCIALISÉE' ECTS programme grid.

otherFees: Belgian residence permit and commune registration; mandatory health insurance; proof of means for the visa (~€800+/month solvency requirement). UNVERIFIED specifics.

scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED AND IMPORTANT: whether a WBI bursary covers the €4,175 droits d'inscription spécifiques could not be confirmed from an official page. entry: Entry is by artistic admission examination (épreuve artistique d'admission), organised each year in MAY and SEPTEMBER. Prior-degree requirements for master entry are UNVERIFIED — ARTS² normally requires a bachelor in music from an FWB ESA or a recognised equivalent, subject to an equivalence procedure for foreign diplomas.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED IN WRITING — no quote found stating a non-music bachelor is accepted. However the admission épreuve itself is unusually open in what it accepts as evidence (see portfolioSpec), and it is judged on demonstrated ability rather than prior schooling. A foreign non-music BSc would require an FWB equivalence decision. TREAT AS: worth asking, not confirmed.
portfolio: EXACT VERBATIM from the official 'CONTENUS ÉPREUVES ARTISTIQUES D'ADMISSION' document, OPTION COMPOSITION (Y COMPRIS COMPOSITION - MUSIQUES APPLIQUÉES): 'Présentation par le candidat de compositions écrites ou enregistrées, même inachevées.' NOTE TWO THINGS: (1) RECORDED works are accepted, not only written scores; (2) works may be UNFINISHED ('même inachevées'). NO minimum number of works, no length limit and no file format are specified anywhere in the document — this is the least prescriptive portfolio requirement found in the entire territory.
audition: NOT A PERFORMANCE AUDITION. VERBATIM, the full épreuve is: 'Présentation par le candidat de compositions écrites ou enregistrées, même inachevées. Évaluation par le jury du parcours artistique du candidat, de sa maîtrise suffisante des langages musicaux et des techniques instrumentales et/ou électroniques. Évaluation des connaissances générales. Entretien de 20' avec le jury d'admission, sur les motivations du candidat et ses aspirations.' So: portfolio presentation + jury assessment of musical-language and instrumental AND/OR ELECTRONIC technique + general knowledge + a 20-minute interview. The phrase 'et/ou électroniques' is important — electronic technique alone can satisfy the technical assessment, so no instrument is strictly required. But 'maîtrise suffisante des langages musicaux' still demands real musical literacy.
deadline: Admission examinations are held in MAY and SEPTEMBER each year. Exact 2027 dates and the application-file deadline are UNVERIFIED. A September session exists, which is unusually late and useful as a second chance — but non-EU visa processing makes the May session the realistic target for a September 2027 start.
opens: UNVERIFIED. Non-EU applicants to FWB institutions normally face an early 'demande d'admission' deadline (often around 30 April) separate from the artistic examination.
duration: 2 years, 120 ECTS (master à finalité spécialisée; 30 of the 120 credits sit in the finalité).
languageReq: French. FWB institutions normally require a French proficiency examination or a recognised certificate for applicants whose prior schooling was not in French — level UNVERIFIED for ARTS².
study: Composition for image, performing arts and new technologies, described as 'une formation unique en Belgique'. Careers listed: composer for cinema, theatre, video games, advertising and interactive media; sound design and sound creation; production and distribution of original works. Studio and stage production technique is taught in the sister Informatique musicale tradition. CAVEAT: the centre of gravity is COMPOSITION TO ORDER (music for image/games), not producing artists' records — adjacent to Field B, not squarely in it.

institution: 3iS — Institut International de l'Image et du Son

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: It will take anyone with any bachelor and no portfolio, which is exactly the problem: he would be paying €15,000 a year for a school diploma that is not a French national master's degree and carries no state recognition, with no scholarship of any kind. A private diploma at that price, from an institution outside the public system, buys him neither the credential nor the network he would need — and 'they will definitely let me in' is not a reason to spend €30,000. If he wants a French route, the public universities are the ones worth the effort.
correction: MAJOR CORRECTION. This is NOT a master's degree. 3iS's own page says graduates "receive a school diploma recognized by industry professionals" — a private school diploma, not a diplôme national de master and not a diplôme visé. The record calls it 'Master in Recording & Music Production' without qualification, which materially misrepresents what a Tunisian applicant would be buying for €30,000. Also note the fee is a flat €15,000/yr for everyone — no French frais différenciés apply because 3iS sits outside the public-university regime.
qualification: 'A school diploma recognized by industry professionals' — a private school diploma, NOT a French state master or grade de master. RNCP level not stated — UNVERIFIED.

scholarshipDetail: 3iS advertises internal scholarships on social and merit criteria, 'with aid varying from 1,000 euros to 50% coverage of training costs, available from the 2nd year of studies' — so no first-year relief. Not verified on an official page for this specific master — UNVERIFIED.

The related 3iS English-taught programmes state English B2 minimum with accepted certifications including IELTS 5.5, TOEFL 72, Linguaskill 60, TOEIC 785, Duolingo 95, Cambridge 160. Enrolment begins October 2026 for the current cohort.

portfolio: No portfolio requirement published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. Contact International@3is.fr / +33 1 85 53 30 43 for the current admission file.
audition: None published — no audition, no on-site concours found. Admission appears to be file-based with an interview. UNVERIFIED.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published deadline for the 2027 intake. Private schools generally admit on a rolling basis until places fill; contact International@3is.fr.

duration: 2 years full-time, 30 ECTS per semester, stated as 180 credits across the programme (note: the page's own arithmetic is inconsistent for a 2-year course — UNVERIFIED).
study: Core modules: acoustics, equipment technology, sound recording and editing, mixing and mastering techniques, music analysis, studio commissioning, audio post-production, artistic direction, computer-assisted music (MAO), and French cultural awareness. Project-based: EP production, live recording, digital music creation, film scoring, audio post-production. Classes 'limited to 25 students' with personalised mentorship from industry professionals.
recommendation: The only entry in this slice whose curriculum is squarely music production and mixing, taught in English, with a bachelor 'in any field' accepted and no audition — on paper the frictionless option for his exact goal and background, requiring only an English test (IELTS/TOEFL, which he has yet to take). The cost is the problem: €15,000/year with no first-year scholarship, versus €300-600/year at ENS Louis-Lumière or ENSATT and €0 plus €1,400/month at DIGICREA. It is also a private school diploma, not a state-recognised master, which matters for later visa/PhD/public-sector routes. Correctly classified as a labelled self-pay fallback: apply only if the funded routes fail, and verify the studio facilities and the RNCP status first.

institution: Abbey Road Institute Germany

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it

Weakness: it funds only ONE year of a two-year master, so it is a top-up, not a full package. Sequence it as: secure the IADT offer first, then apply for GOI-IES; use it as the fallback if the ReSound Erasmus Mundus scholarship does not land.

institution: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (IE) · Universidade Lusófona (PT) · Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre / …
programme: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: This is the one door in the sweep whose published entry list actually names his degree — IADT writes "computational science" into the accepted bachelors — and there is no live audition, only an online interview after a scored file. Two things he must resolve first: he must sit IELTS and clear 6.0 (a low bar, but he has not taken it), and he must build three pieces totalling 10-15 minutes with written reflections, because the Erasmus Mundus scholarship that makes the €15,000 affordable is won on the strength of that portfolio alone. Without the scholarship the €15,000 plus three-country living costs is beyond what he said he can pay, so treat the scholarship as the whole point of applying.
correction: The record's cost band 'EUR 5k-15k/yr' is WRONG — €15,000 is the total for four semesters (€7,500/yr), not per year. The record's gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' is right only in the sense of an ONLINE interview: there is no exam and no audition. Most importantly, the record does not flag that IADT's published entry list explicitly includes computational science, which makes this by far his strongest eligibility match; nor that no 2027 call is yet published. NOTE ON DUPLICATION: indices 47, 48, 50 and 51 are the SAME single Erasmus Mundus programme (ReSound, IADT code DL935) recorded four times under different spellings of the consortium — IADT Dún Laoghaire with Universidade Lusófona Lisbon and the Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre Vilnius. It was verified once and the identical verdict is written to all four; they should be collapsed into one row.
qualification: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master — joint diploma supplement 'MA in Sound (ReSound)' PLUS multiple degrees: IADT 'Master of Arts in Sound', Lusófona 'Master's in Sound Production Technology', LMTA 'Master of Arts in Film'
tuition: €15,000 total for the whole 4-semester programme for non-scholarship holders, paid €7,500 before semester 1 and €7,500 before semester 3. Identical for EU and non-EU. Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders pay nothing. Fee covers all classes, insurance, enrolment at each partner, examinations and the final diploma; it does NOT cover travel, visas, accommodation or living costs. Living costs estimated at €600–1,000 per month.
scholarshipDetail: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Scholarship, "awarded on the basis of excellence" — open to any nationality including Tunisian; eligibility is holding a first higher-education degree or recognised equivalent, and not already having held an EMJM/Erasmus Mundus scholarship. "A maximum of 24 places are offered at ReSound each year. An Erasmus Mundus scholarship will be available only to a percentage of those places." CORRECTION: the site says "only to a percentage", not "a significant percentage".
entry: Bachelor's degree in sound, music, film or media studies (minimum EQF Level 6 or equivalent; NARIC Ireland used to check equivalence). Other fields considered with relevant prior experience. Also required: passport copy, headshot, stamped degree documents + transcripts (certified English translation if needed), CV of professional qualifications and experience, TWO letters of recommendation (at least one academic, addressed to 'board members of ReSound'), letter of motivation (max 1000 characters, explicitly 'do not use AI / Large Language Models'), a 500-character description of a proposed final thesis project, portfolio, English proof. English: IELTS 6.0 with no component below 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 79 / Duolingo 110 / Cambridge B2 / LanguageCert ESOL, taken within the last two years; OR a full EQF Level 4+ qualification of at least one academic year taught through English. Final-year undergraduates may apply (conditional offer). No age limit and no time limit on when the bachelor was obtained.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — the strongest wording in this batch. "ReSound is open to both European and non-European students who hold a bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, or media studies. Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies." FAQ: "I have not formally studied sound. Is prior experience in sound a requirement for admission? It is not a requirement to have formally studied sound specifically." CORRECTION to the draft: the current published eligibility text does NOT name "computational science" as an accepted field — the accepted list is sound, music, film, media studies, plus the other-fields-with-relevant-experience clause. A software-engineering BSc therefore goes through the discretionary clause and needs demonstrable sound/music practice, which his DJ/producer work can supply.
portfolio: "Portfolio of previous sound/media related work. Please include a short reflective paragraph on each piece explicitly stating your role in the work. Please supply no more than 3 examples. You can supply a single hyperlink to a portfolio website or a compilation audio or video file. entry: Three-year university or academic degree (or equivalent) plus a minimum of 15 years of schooling; certified translation plus Dichiarazione di Valore or a CIMEA Diplome statement.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes, and this is the least music-dependent of the four. Formal entry needs only a three-year degree plus 15 years of schooling; there is no pre-selection, no portfolio and no performance - just an interview, a technical MCQ on digital audio, Pro Tools, mic technique and MIDI, and a practical mix of a supplied multitrack. A technically minded non-musician who practises mixing for a year has a genuine route in.
portfolio: None required. Instead of submitting work, he sits a practical mixing test on a multitrack provided by Saint Louis - which is arguably easier to prepare for than assembling a portfolio, since it tests trainable craft rather than an existing body of work.
audition: NOW FULLY VERIFIED (previously flagged as needing confirmation). As a Tecnico del Suono course there is no pre-selection: "Per il Corso di Tecnico del Suono non e prevista pre-selezione ma un colloquio attitudinale." The official piano di studi gives the exam as: "1) Colloquio attitudinale. 2) Test scritto a risposte multiple incentrato sui seguenti argomenti: Fondamenti di audio digitale, Pro Tools, Riprese microfoniche, Protocollo MIDI. 3) Prova pratica di missaggio su multi-traccia fornito dal Saint Louis." So: interview, technical MCQ, and a hands-on mix of a multitrack the school supplies. No portfolio and no performance.
deadline: 30 April; tests online January-June for internationals or in person in June. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
opens: "dal 3 febbraio al 30 aprile" per the official piano di studi; internationals from 1 January. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027/28 dates.
duration: 2 years, 120 CFA - NOW VERIFIED from the official piano di studi (previously unverified). Year 1 = 60 CFA (12 + 30 + 12 + 6); Year 2 = 60 CFA (9 + 30 + 12 + 9). The 30-CFA core module in each year is the mix/recording practice, making this the most concentrated single-skill plan of the four. Fortnightly lessons over two consecutive days.
englishTest: No IELTS or TOEFL requirement published anywhere.
study: Recording studio practice (microphone technique, critical listening, editing, mix setup, vocal, ensemble, string and brass recording); Mix (progressive supervised individual sessions, plug-ins, reverbs, effects, multi-stylistic professional sessions); Mastering both in the box and with dedicated outboard; Fondamenti di acustica degli strumenti musicali e della voce. Each student engineers record productions and delivers at least two finished records; the best are released on the Saint Louis labels to international streaming platforms. Avid Pro Tools 210M and 310M certifications are pursued within the course.
recommendation: The safest admission and the wrong ambition - take it only as a deliberate career hedge. Everything about the gate suits him: no portfolio, no audition, a studiable written exam and a practical mix test on material the school hands him. And it produces a real MUR degree plus Pro Tools 210M/310M certification, which is directly employable. But it trains the engineer who serves other people's records, not the artist who makes his own - if the goal is to DJ and release music, Music Production is the same money for a far closer fit, and Sound Design is equally winnable with more distinctive skills. Only pick Mix & Mastering if he consciously wants a studio-technician day job to fund the DJ ambition. Before committing, get the price of the extra Pro Tools courses and the 210M/310M certifications in writing - it is the only figure in this batch the school refuses to publish.

totalCost: Fees: roughly €7,900-€9,200 in year one (tuition band + €240/€290 registration + €140 regional tax, with the €250 deposit absorbed) and €7,900-€9,300 in year two (including the €500 diploma exam fee), so about €15,700-€18,400 over two years, plus any extra Pro Tools modules. scholarshipDetail: (1) SAINT LOUIS INTERNAL SCHOLARSHIPS — partial exemptions from the fees, worth €500 to €2,500 per year of the course for full-time attendance, restricted to first- and second-level academic courses. FIRST-YEAR criteria are two, jointly: an ISEE below €22,000 AND merit. For a student who has NOT come through Saint Louis pre-academic courses, the merit test is 'la media delle prove di ammissione deve essere pari o superiore a 26/30', with a 1-point penalty on the average for each subject carried as a debit. Application window 2-31 JULY each year. SECOND-YEAR renewal: ISEE still below €22,000, plus at least 50 CFA with a weighted average of 26/30 or higher by the September session. Not available for years fuori corso. AS A NON-EU APPLICANT HE WOULD NEED AN ISEE PARIFICATO built from consular-legalised Tunisian tax and property documents to prove the €22,000 test — the same exercise described in the IED entry, and it must be started months ahead. It is a performer's award, open to 'musicisti, cantanti e songwriter'. A sound-design student who does not perform is outside its scope. Do not budget for it. (3) BORSE DI COLLABORAZIONE — annual competition for student collaboration grants across all departments; amounts UNVERIFIED. (4) LAZIODISCO / DiSCo LAZIO REGIONAL SCHOLARSHIP — awarded through a separate regional call on income and merit. Non-EU students are eligible and, under Art. 13(3) d.p.c.m. 9/04/2001 (quoted verbatim in the IED entry), are automatically classified 'fuori sede', the highest-value bracket. Saint Louis confirms compatibility: 'Gli esoneri parziali dal versamento delle quote sono compatibili con le borse di studio LazioDisco, è possibile conseguire entrambi' — so a Saint Louis internal exemption AND a LazioDisco award CAN be stacked. This is the only genuine stacking opportunity found anywhere in this batch. LazioDisco amounts for Saint Louis students UNVERIFIED. (5) Convenzione with Sapienza and other partnership discounts — details UNVERIFIED. (6) FINANCING via Banca Sella and Intesa Sanpaolo 'per Merito': the Banca Sella application requires an Italian tessera sanitaria/codice fiscale and, above €7,000, an Italian income document from the borrower — effectively closed to him before he is resident.
entry: VERIFIED and quoted. 'Level II Academics: EU or NON-EU Citizens holding a Three-year University or Academic Diploma (or equivalent), obtained in Italy or in their home country, may apply for admission. Proof of a minimum of 15 years of schooling is also required.' The degree must be submitted as a scanned original with certified translation and a Declaration of Value (DOV) from the Italian Embassy or Consulate, or alternatively a CIMEA Diplome certificate. A Tunisian BSc after 13 years of school plus a 3-year degree gives 16 years — but he must count this precisely against his own transcripts, because falling short of 15 diverts him to Pre-Academic courses.
acceptsNonMusic: THIS IS THE REAL BARRIER, AND IT IS WORSE THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. The programme page states: 'Bachelor of Sound Technician graduates gain access by right to one of the two-year degrees listed above. Graduates in other disciplines who have prior experience in phonics may enter upon entrance examination.' He is a graduate in another discipline WITHOUT prior experience in phonics (audio engineering). On the published wording he does not currently meet the alternative route. Compounding this, the international page warns: 'Students whose incoming preparation is NOT CONSIDERED SUITABLE for direct entry into Academic Level Courses will be eligible for more appropriate Pre-Academic Level Courses' — i.e. he risks being offered a pre-academic year instead of the biennio. GET A WRITTEN RULING FROM THE SEGRETERIA DIDATTICA BEFORE INVESTING IN THIS PATH, and use the year to 2027 to build demonstrable audio work.
portfolio: VERIFIED and favourable. The pre-selection route differs by department. For Jazz/Pop/Songwriting/Classical the candidate must record four songs performed, at least three in a group of at least a trio — that would be impossible for him. BUT for 'Composition/Electronic/Applied Music' the requirement is: 'Prepare a link containing Portfolio (video, audio, sheet music) of your most indicative and recent works.' A self-built production portfolio is therefore admissible on the correct track. For the Sound Technician course there is no pre-selection at all, only an aptitude interview. He must confirm which pre-selection route the Sound Design biennio follows.
audition: No performance audition on the portfolio track. After pre-selection there are ADMISSION TESTS — the course page says they run 'over two consecutive days'; the international page says they can be taken online between January and June on individually agreed dates, or in a single in-person session in June. Results feed a merit ranking (graduatoria). Test contents are published in the Course Catalog.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027 entry, but the pattern is stable and the dates are early. For a SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 START he should expect: applications 1 January - 30 APRIL 2027; Very Early Bird payment deadline 30 APRIL 2027 (15% off); Early Bird admission completed by 15 JUNE 2027 (10% off); registration fee €240 by 30 May 2027; internal scholarship application 2-31 JULY 2027; regular upfront payment by 5 September 2027. The binding constraint is 30 April 2027 — which means the portfolio, the DOV/CIMEA and the language evidence must all be ready by roughly March 2027.
opens: VERIFIED. Applications for admission to academic courses, complete with pre-selection links, are accepted each year from 1 JANUARY and no later than 30 APRIL. Late applications are considered individually at the discretion of management, subject to places. Admission tests: online between January and June on individually agreed dates, or a single in-person session in June; the course page also mentions June and September sessions. Scholarship applications: 2-31 July annually.
duration: 2 years, 120 CFA (Diploma Accademico di II livello). VERIFIED CONTACT HOURS: 'Approximately 300 hours of classes per year', with classes 'mostly held on a fortnightly basis', mandatory attendance of at least 80%. A part-time route exists and may extend the course beyond 3 years. 300 h/year is roughly 10 hours a week — LOW, and he must check that it satisfies the Italian study-visa full-time expectation before relying on it.
englishTest: IELTS is NOT the binding requirement and is not mentioned. Language proficiency is assessed in the aptitude interview, in 'English (or Italian)'. If the biennio is delivered in Italian he will need real Italian; if an English route exists, English suffices. CONFIRM WHICH — this is the highest-value single question to put to the Segreteria.
study: VERIFIED module list. Sound Design — techniques and concepts of sound design and audio post-production, recording, construction and manipulation of sound effects for film, TV series, video games and media, Pro Tools with a detailed focus on the audio post-production and sound-design workflow, plus other sound-manipulation software and plug-ins. Wwise Nonlinear Interactive Audio — audio nonlinearity in interactive video-game sound design using Audiokinetic Wwise. Audio Sampling and Post Production — Kontakt and its engine, modulators, envelopes, zones, groups, mapping, and building a custom sample library. Sound Branding — analysis, composition, implementation, mix and mastering of a sound brand. Technologies and Techniques of Audio Restoration — restoration and audio forensics from film to tape to digital, in specialised laboratories. Mix e Mastering — mix and mastering sessions finalising multimedia products. Students are also involved in projects with the Saint Louis Composition and Music Applied to Images departments and with the film/animation departments of RUFA, Vigamus and others. Career outcomes: Sound Designer, Sound Restorer, audio post-production sound engineer, Sound Designer for gaming.
recommendation: This remains the best SUBJECT fit in Italy for him and the cheapest genuinely accredited second-level route in this batch — a real Diploma Accademico di II livello in Sound Design and Audio Post-Production, taught on Pro Tools, Wwise and Kontakt, from a MUR-authorised music school with an AEC membership and a Sapienza relationship. But three corrections change the plan. FIRST, THE PRICE: it is not €2,800 a year. As an international student he pays €7,230 to €8,500 a year depending purely on how early he commits, plus €240-€290 registration, €140 regional tax a year, a €500 diploma exam fee and chargeable extra Pro Tools modules — about €15,700-€18,400 over two years. The €1,270-a-year gap between Very Early Bird and Regular instalments is the single easiest saving available to him anywhere in this batch: commit and pay by 30 April. SECOND, ADMISSION IS NOT ASSURED: the published rule gives access by right only to Sound Technician graduates, and admits 'graduates in other disciplines who have prior experience in phonics' by entrance examination. He has none. He must (a) get a written ruling from the Segreteria Didattica now, and (b) spend the year to April 2027 producing demonstrable audio work so that the 'prior experience' claim is real — the good news is that the Composition/Electronic/Applied Music pre-selection route accepts exactly that, 'a Portfolio (video, audio, sheet music) of your most indicative and recent works', with no group-performance requirement. THIRD, KNOW WHAT HE IS BUYING: this is sound design for film, TV, games and restoration, not electronic music production or DJing. If his goal is genuinely to become an international DJ/producer, this teaches him the professional audio craft underneath that ambition but not the ambition itself. Practical sequence: written ruling on eligibility and on teaching language first; then Italian to B2 if the answer is Italian; DOV or CIMEA started by autumn 2026; ISEE parificato paperwork started in spring 2027 for the 2-31 July scholarship window; application filed by 30 April 2027 to capture the 15%; and LazioDisco pursued in parallel, since the school confirms in writing that its own exemptions and LazioDisco awards can be held together.

institution: ETIC – Escola de Tecnologias, Inovação e Criação (private school, Lisbon; Pearson BTEC Accredited Centre sinc…

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
verdictWhy: This is a Pearson BTEC Level 5 professional certificate from a school that says in writing it is not a higher education institution. Level 5 is below the BSc he already holds, so it is an academic step backwards and cannot support a master's-level student visa route. Bank loans are the only published funding.
correction: TWO corrections. (1) This is not a master's and was collected as though it were: the award is a 'Pearson BTEC Level 5 Professional Certification (240 CATS)' and the school states 'ETIC is not a higher education institution.' Level 5 is below bachelor's level. (2) Gate recorded as 'Portfolio + exam/interview' — wrong on the portfolio: the page states portfolio submission is 'not mandatory'. The real gate is a motivation letter plus an interview.
qualification: CORRECTED AND SHARPENED. The award is a "BTEC Higher National Diploma, Level 5, carrying a total of 240 CATS credits" — ETIC's own wording. The page also calls it a "Pearson BTEC Level 5 Professional Certification (240 CATS)". It is an HND: NOT a mestrado, NOT a pós-graduação, NOT a Portuguese degree, and NOT a bachelor's. ETIC states plainly on its own page: "Certification follows the British education system; ETIC is not a higher education institution." NEW FINDING: the optional 3rd year is a separate award — "ETIC / SOLENT UNIVERSITY RECOGNITION / 120 CATS", taking the total to 360 CATS, i.e. a UK bachelor's-level top-up recognised by Solent University (Southampton). So the 2-year route ends BELOW bachelor's; only the 3-year route reaches bachelor-equivalent — still nowhere near a master.
accreditation: NOT a Portuguese degree — VERIFIED IN ETIC'S OWN WORDS. It is NOT accredited by A3ES or DGES, is NOT a mestrado, and is NOT a pós-graduação in the Portuguese academic sense. It is a UK Pearson BTEC Higher National Diploma at Level 5, assigned its level "by Ofqual (Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation) under the Regulated Qualifications Framework (RQF), which forms part of the UK qualifications system", delivered in Portugal by a DGERT-certified vocational provider. ETIC states: "ETIC is not a higher education institution." It describes the programmes as "internationally recognised, enabling direct entry into the labour market as well as progression to further studies" — "progression to further studies" is the operative admission: an HND Level 5 is a stepping stone TOWARD a bachelor's, which is exactly what the optional Solent third year completes. For someone who already holds a BSc, the two-year award is a step DOWN and the three-year award is at best lateral.
tuition: CORRECTED to €11,640 for the full 2-year programme by instalments (24 x €485), or €11,058 if paid promptly in 2 x €5,529 with the 5% discount. The previously reported €11,200 was wrong. CRITICAL FOR THIS CANDIDATE: a separate line applies to him — "CITIZENS WITHOUT TAX RESIDENCE IN PORTUGAL: 1st instalment: €3,492 + 23 instalments: €354,26", totalling €11,639.98. Same total, but with a €3,492 lump sum demanded up front instead of €485. As a Tunisian national with no Portuguese tax residence, this is the schedule he would face. The table is dated 2025 and carries the warning "Prices and payment conditions may change until enrollment begins."
otherFees: MAJOR CORRECTION — application fees DO exist and were previously reported as absent. The published table states "APPLICATION: YEAR 1: 700€ | YEAR 2: 200€", footnoted "Amount to be paid upon enrollment and non-refundable, except in the case the course does not open." That is €900 in non-refundable fees on top of tuition. No separate materials, insurance or exam fees are published; UNVERIFIED whether a Pearson registration/certification fee is charged separately, and this should still be asked about explicitly. Cost of the optional Solent-recognised third year is UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: CORRECTED. Tuition €11,640 over two years (or €11,058 prompt-paid) PLUS €900 non-refundable application fees = €12,540 total to ETIC on the instalment route, or €11,958 prompt-paid. His first-year outlay as a non-tax-resident is front-loaded: €700 application + €3,492 first instalment = €4,192 due immediately, then €354.26/month. Add Lisbon living costs — the cheapest of the four capitals in this slice but now expensive for housing, realistically €900-€1,200/month. All-in over two years, tuition plus modest living: roughly €34,000-€41,000. ETIC publishes no living-cost estimate (UNVERIFIED).
scholarshipDetail: None published for this course — the only fee reductions are the 5% prompt-payment and 6% alumni discounts, neither of which he can use (he is not an alumnus, and prompt payment means finding €11,058 at once). ETIC's site carries an "Erasmus+ Scholarships" menu item and offers Erasmus+ international internship mobility after completion subject to performance, but that is a placement scheme, not a fee reduction. Net position: essentially no scholarship access.
entry: VERIFIED verbatim: a motivation letter outlining professional goals; a "portfolio or showreel" listed as OPTIONAL; attendance at an interview; and a "recommended english entry level: B1". Places are limited: "Enrolment in a specific timetable is limited to the number of available places" and "the opening of each course, class or timetable is subject to a minimum number of enrolments."
acceptsNonMusic: Yes, comfortably. VERIFIED: no degree, no music background and no formal prior qualification is required. Entry is by motivation letter, an OPTIONAL portfolio and an interview. His BSc sits far above the entry bar — which is precisely the problem.
portfolio: Portfolio or showreel is OPTIONAL — VERIFIED. This remains genuinely notable: with no portfolio yet built, this is one of the very few audio programmes across the four countries he could apply to today without producing a single finished track.
audition: Interview only. No audition, no test, no entrance exam. VERIFIED.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published application deadline. With a hard cap of 16 places, entry is effectively first-come. For a non-EU applicant the binding constraint is not ETIC's deadline but the Portuguese visa timeline, which ETIC itself warns "can take several months". PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
opens: UNVERIFIED — not published. Admission is enquiry-and-interview based: select the course, submit the application form, receive an email with interview dates, then enrol on approval.
duration: "Duration: 2 years + 1 (optional). Level: 5" — ETIC's own wording. 240 CATS after year 2 (BTEC HND, Level 5); a further 120 CATS with Solent University recognition in the optional year 3, totalling 360 CATS. CATS is a UK credit unit, NOT ECTS; 240 CATS is nominally 120 ECTS but the LEVEL is what matters, and Level 5 is below bachelor's.
englishTest: No IELTS required — VERIFIED. The published requirement is a "recommended english entry level: B1", and no standardised test is demanded at all. This is dramatically softer than Berklee Valencia's IELTS 7.5 or SAE's IELTS 6.0, and it is the single most accessible English requirement found in this research.
study: CORRECTED — the module content was previously UNVERIFIED and is now confirmed in detail from the official page, and it is not what a producer/DJ needs. Verified units: sound design for film, documentary and animation; adaptive audio systems for video games, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR); sound design for installations, exhibitions and public spaces; technical installation and operation of Public Address (P.A.) systems including tuning and calibration; Lighting Control fundamentals covering the DMX system, cabling, projectors and digital lighting consoles; Broadcast and LUFS Standards (sound engineering for TV and radio, loudness measurement and regulatory volume standards); Sound for Arts, Theatre and QLab (setup, automation and playback control for live performance); Sound Systems for Museums and Installations (multi-channel and distributed audio design); and Sonic Interactivity and Prototyping using sensors and Arduino/Raspberry Pi. Stated career outcome: "Sound Designer specialising in recording and post-production for video games, film, theatre, advertising and sound installations." Schedule: Mon-Friday 14:00-18:00, in person, project-based, max 16 students. Erasmus+ international internships available on completion, subject to performance.
recommendation: Cheap, English-taught, visa-supported and genuinely accessible — and still the wrong course, for two independent reasons. First, LEVEL: the two-year award is a BTEC Higher National Diploma at Level 5, which is BELOW bachelor's. ETIC says outright it is not a higher education institution. Paying €12,540 and two years to obtain a sub-bachelor vocational diploma when he already holds a BSc is a downgrade, not a postgraduate step. The newly-verified optional third year (Solent University recognition, +120 CATS, 360 total) only brings him back up to bachelor-equivalent — still not a master, and now three years and considerably more money. Second, and previously unverified, CONTENT: the module list is now confirmed and it is media, live-event and installation sound design — film and documentary post, game/VR/AR adaptive audio, P.A. rigging and calibration, DMX lighting control, broadcast LUFS compliance, QLab theatre playback, museum multichannel systems, Arduino sensor prototyping. There is no music production, no electronic music, no DJing, and the stated career outcome is "Sound Designer specialising in recording and post-production for video games, film, theatre, advertising and sound installations". That is a different profession from the one he wants. Correct the money on the record: tuition is €11,640 not €11,200, the schedule is 24 x €485 not 10 x €560, there IS a non-refundable application fee of €700 in year one plus €200 in year two, and as a non-tax-resident he must pay €3,492 up front rather than a first monthly instalment — so his day-one cash requirement is €4,192, not €560. What still makes it worth keeping on the page: it is the only entry in this batch with a published price, English delivery, NO IELTS requirement (B1 recommended only), an OPTIONAL portfolio, and explicit written non-EU visa support including an AIMA enrolment letter. If his real constraint turns out to be that he cannot reach IELTS 7.5 or cannot build a portfolio in time for a 2027 master's, this is the fallback that would still take him — but he should choose ETIC's music production certification rather than this sound design one, because this one does not teach what he wants to do. And the honest structural finding stands: Portugal has no international private chain master's in this field at all, so if Portugal matters to him the search must move to private Portuguese universities such as Universidade Católica Portuguesa's Som e Imagem mestrado.
