institution: Abbey Road Institute London (Abbey Road Training Limited)
programme: Advanced Diploma in Music Production and Sound Engineering — NOT A MASTER'S; ACCREDITED AT LEVEL 5
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: Advanced Diploma. MAJOR CORRECTION TO PRIOR RECORD: there IS a named awarding organisation, and the level IS published — it was on the course-info page, not the courses index. Verbatim: "NCFE is an awarding organisation recognised by the qualification regulators for England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Our qualification has been developed to meet the specific needs of our students and has been accredited by NCFE as demonstrating quality and rigour." And: "Our Advanced Diploma in Music Production and Sound Engineering has been accredited as a Customised Qualification and we have benchmarked the qualification's learning outcomes and assessment criteria at Level 5 (using a national framework's level descriptors)." LEVEL 5 = below a bachelor's (Level 6) and two levels below a master's (Level 7). Certificate is issued by NCFE. Confirmed by the progression route: "We have partnered with the University of West London... once you have successfully completed your training with us you can apply to join the SECOND YEAR of one of the following degree courses".
tuition: NOW VERIFIED (prior record said unpublished): "Fees for International Students (all applicants applying from outside the UK who need a visa) — Total Course Fee: £23,950 (Tuition Fee of £23,500 and £450 Application Fee)", and "As an international student, you will be required to pay your fees in full before you enrol." For comparison, UK/EU-settled applicants pay £17,900 (£16,900 if paid upfront). He is in the £23,950 band, payable in full up front, and "During your studies, you will not have any working rights in the UK whilst on a Student Visa."
scholarshipDetail: None found on the fees & funding page. Only payment plans (12 monthly instalments, or a discounted upfront payment). No bursary, no scholarship, no loan available to a non-UK applicant.
entry: NOW VERIFIED. No academic degree is required — "We encourage applications from a wide range of backgrounds and levels of experience." Required to apply: (1) a music portfolio, (2) music qualifications — "we require applicants to have an understanding of the fundamentals of music theory. If you are new to music theory we recommend you attend our 2-day Music Theory Fundamental for Producers course and/or study online for your ABRSM grade-1 music theory qualification", (3) a cover letter, (4) photographic ID/passport — "The minimum age requirement to take a course at Abbey Road Institute in London is 18", (5) a £450 application fee (refundable minus £150 admin if unsuccessful). For visa nationals: "IELTS (Academic) – Grade B2 Overall and in each area (Reading, Writing, Speaking, Listening)", taken at a UKVI-approved SELT centre.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes, explicitly — "We encourage applications from a wide range of backgrounds and levels of experience" and there is no degree requirement at all. A software-engineering BSc is neither required nor a barrier. The real gate is the music portfolio and basic music theory, not the subject of his bachelor's. But note this cuts both ways: an award with no degree entry requirement is, by construction, not a postgraduate qualification.
portfolio: NOW VERIFIED AND EXACT (prior record said unpublished): "A Music Portfolio (4 productions in which you demonstrate different roles, such as performer, producer, engineer, writer etc). Please label the portfolio and submit further documentation to explain your role in each production. The tracks need to be submitted in MP3 format in order to be accepted. We do not expect to receive high-quality productions but are simply looking for evidence that you have been attempting to create and produce music for a period of time." That last sentence is genuinely encouraging for someone at his stage — 4 MP3s, polish not required.
audition: No live audition. An INTERVIEW is part of admission: "So that we can assess your suitability for the course and offer you an interview you will need to submit the following..." — i.e. portfolio and documents first, then interview. Format (in person / online) not stated.
deadline: No application deadline is published for London. Published full-time START dates (genuinely current, not prior-cycle): 28 September 2026, 1 February 2027, 24 May 2027. The part-time Audio Post Production for Film and TV diploma starts 9 November 2026. A September 2027 start date is not yet published — expect it to appear alongside the 2027 cycle; label any 2027 autumn date as unconfirmed until published.
opens: Rolling, multiple intakes per year. International applicants are warned to apply early: "Our international student allowance is currently small, so we would recommend that international students apply well in advance to avoid disappointment."
duration: One year full-time. No credits, no ECTS, no FHEQ level — but benchmarked at Level 5 against national framework descriptors (see degree field). Three terms.
study: Practical, studio-centred music production and sound engineering over three terms, covering audio engineering and acoustics (principles, tools, DAW), production and music theory, and management/music business, taught largely in Pro Tools, Logic and Ableton Live, with recording sessions and workshops. Certificate of achievement issued by NCFE on completion.
recommendation: STILL NOT A MASTER'S — but the correct verdict is now sharper than "unaccredited marketing". It is a real, NCFE-accredited, Home-Office-overseen, Level 5 vocational qualification, and Abbey Road Institute London genuinely holds a Student Visa sponsorship licence: "Abbey Road Institute London holds a Student Visa sponsorship licence. This means that we are now able to accept a limited number of international students who require a Student visa to study on the UK." So a Tunisian national CAN legally come and study here, unlike the Amsterdam campus. The problem is value, not legitimacy. He would pay £23,950 in full up front, with no work rights, to earn a Level 5 award — one level BELOW the BSc he already holds, and worth nothing towards a master's, a Level 7 recognition in Europe, or doctoral progression. The teaching and the Abbey Road access are probably excellent, and the portfolio bar ("we do not expect to receive high-quality productions") is realistically within reach for him. But as a step after a completed bachelor's, paying nearly £24k to move DOWN the qualification framework is hard to justify, especially with zero funding. RATED C for that reason, not because it is fake. If he wants the Abbey Road name cheaply, the 4-day Song Production Masterclass (10-13 Oct 2026, one day at Abbey Road Studios, three at Angel Studios, with Sylvia Massy) is the sane version of this.

qualification: MA (Master of Arts)
tuition: £13,500 International (£12,500 UK), total programme cost, as published July 2026. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO CARRY FORWARD: the page states "Fees frozen until September 2026 intake" — the freeze therefore does NOT cover his September 2027 target intake, so budget for an increase. Explicitly acceptable alternatives: audio, music and dialogue editing; mixing and mastering music (before/after examples "appreciated"); any audio-to-picture work; field recording and foley; practical or musical sound design. NEWLY CONFIRMED DETAIL: "You are allowed to use sound libraries. Sound effects created and manipulated by you are encouraged, but using sound libraries is a key part of a sound designer's workflow so you can use these in your application." Applicants must "make it clear in the covering letter where loops or any other pre-recorded audio that is not your own has been used." No fixed number of works, duration or file format is prescribed.

deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No hard deadline is published; admission is rolling against a fixed 14 September start date. The Sept 2027 start date is not yet published.
opens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Page currently reads "Accepting applications for September 14th start" (2026 cohort). Rolling admission model, so a 2027-start window should appear around late 2026 — recheck from about October 2026.
duration: 12 months full-time (~30 hrs/week); 24 months part-time (~15 hrs/week); 36 months part-time (~8 hrs/week). Page states credits verbatim as "180 UK / 90 ECTS / ~36 US academic credits".
study: Confirmed module-by-module. M1 Foundations of Game Audio (audio to moving image, industry roles, spotting cutscenes, non-linear design). M2 Game Audio Technologies (middleware Wwise and FMOD, game engines Unity and Unreal, recording, sound design technique, mixing, profiling). M3 Research and Critical Reflection (5,000-word report). M4 Interactive Audio (vehicle sounds for racing games, advanced loop editing, personal style). M5 3D Audio Environments (3D world implementation, dynamic mixing, VR/AR audio). M6 one elective from FMOD / Unreal & Blueprint / Musical Sound Design / Audio Post-Production / Career Development for Sound Designers — page warns electives are "provisional", "subject to change" and need minimum enrolment. Final Major Project (12 weeks, plus 2,500-word report) OR a dissertation of "12,000 words (+/- 10%)". Practical assignments carry 1,500-word commentaries — note this is a genuinely writing-heavy degree.
recommendation: Lowest-barrier entry of the whole slice: any degree (or none) accepted, no audition, no English test stated, and a portfolio brief he could build in a few months by redesigning the sound of game and film clips — with sound libraries explicitly permitted, which removes the usual field-recording bottleneck. The Wwise/FMOD/Unity/Unreal stack is where his software-engineering background converts directly into an advantage. Against it: zero funding for a non-UK student, £13,500 self-pay and rising after the 2026 fee freeze lapses, and — most important for HIS actual goal — it is online-only. No relocation, no residence permit, no European club or label network, and the curriculum is game sound effects, not club music production or DJing.

Take the entry spec and treat it as his 12-month build target: 4 to 8 finished productions in MP3 or WAV, deliberately spanning DIFFERENT roles (performer, producer, engineer, writer), each accompanied by a written description of exactly what he contributed. That is concrete, achievable from where he stands today, and it is close to a universal currency — it would materially strengthen a Berklee Valencia application and almost any other portfolio-gated route. Build to that spec and apply elsewhere. On the programme itself, three reasons to rule it out: the visa wall is explicit and in writing; €19,000–€20,000 buys a non-accredited diploma with no credits and no academic standing; and it is a studio-engineering course rather than a DJ or electronic-music one, so it is off-target for his stated goal even setting the other problems aside. One correction he must not miss: applications DO close, one month before the start date, so this is not the open-ended rolling admission previously assumed. Finally, note the pattern — both Dutch private providers in this slice are visa-dead for identical reasons, which means the Netherlands as a whole should drop down his country list unless he finds an NVAO-accredited, bekostigd institution.

whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: 'SAE Professional Diploma' — an internal school award. NOT a master, NOT a bachelor, NOT a Dutch degree, and not credit-bearing. The University of Hertfordshire validation that SAE advertises applies to its BA/BSc (Hons) degree routes only, NOT to this standalone Diploma. Anyone reading 'SAE' plus 'University of Hertfordshire' on the same page should check which product the validation actually attaches to — here, it does not attach to this one.

The institution is therefore NIET-BEKOSTIGD (private, government-unfunded) and sits outside the Dutch higher-education system entirely. SAE's own accreditation page confirms that only its degree programmes carry external validation and that the validation comes from the University of Hertfordshire in the UK, not from any Dutch authority. The Diploma has neither NVAO accreditation nor UH validation.
tuition: Audio Production Diploma, 18 months, 2026/2027 fees: €16,210 upfront; €18,095 across 3 semester instalments; €19,040 across 18 monthly instalments. otherFees: A €500 registration fee is included in all quoted programme prices per SAE's fee page — included, not additional. No separate application, materials, exam or insurance fees are published; UNVERIFIED whether any exist in practice.
totalCost: €16,210 total for 18 months if paid upfront (the €500 registration fee is included), rising to €19,040 on the monthly plan. portfolio: None published for the Diploma. UNVERIFIED whether an informal work sample is requested at interview.
audition: None published.
deadline: No published deadline — rolling admissions. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for September 2027 specifically; that intake is not yet individually published.
opens: Rolling — SAE states courses can be applied for at any time.
duration: 18 months. No ECTS — this is not a credit-bearing Dutch qualification and does not sit in the EHEA framework.
englishTest: IELTS IS accepted — but the published scores apply to DEGREE courses: IELTS 6.0 undergraduate / 6.5 postgraduate with minimum 5.5 in each band; TOEFL 72 UG / 79 PG; Duolingo 120 UG / 105 PG; Cambridge B2 First / C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency; GCSE/IGCSE English grade C or above. For the non-degree Diploma no specific score is published — UNVERIFIED. Worth noting only as a data point on what IELTS band the SAE group considers adequate; it is useful benchmarking for his other applications even though this programme is closed to him.
study: Concentrated practice in recording, 3D audio and mastering, plus technical and practical audio skills. Full module list not captured — UNVERIFIED. As with the Spanish campuses, this is general audio engineering rather than DJ or club-music training, so it is an imperfect fit for his stated goal even before the blocking issues.
recommendation: Rule out on visa grounds alone, and stop there — no further analysis is needed. SAE states in its own words that its registration 'cannot grant you a Student Visa in the Netherlands' and that as a private institute 'its students are not eligible for a Visa, nor a student loan via DUO'. For a Tunisian national with no independent route to Dutch residence, that ends the conversation regardless of the quality of the teaching. Even setting the visa entirely aside, €16,210–€19,040 buys an internal school diploma with no NVAO accreditation, no degree status, no ECTS and no credit transferability — poor value measured against a genuinely accredited master, and he would be paying master-level money for a certificate. Two things are worth carrying forward from this entry even though the programme is closed to him: the fee transparency is exemplary and shames SAE Spain, and it establishes the principle he should apply everywhere — check whether the institution is a recognised visa sponsor BEFORE evaluating anything else, because that single question eliminates candidates faster than any other.

The award's standing comes ENTIRELY from the UK: 'awarded by and quality assured by the University of Hertfordshire' for 2026/27, with students enrolled before 1 January 2022 under Middlesex University. Alternatives confirmed on the page: TOEFL, Duolingo 120, Cambridge, PTE, and GCSE/IGCSE English at grade C or above. IELTS 6.0 with 5.5 per band is a far softer target than Berklee Valencia's 7.5.

recommendation: Rule out on two independent grounds, either of which is fatal. He already holds a BSc; paying €25,000–€37,000 plus two to three years of Amsterdam living costs for a second bachelor's is not a rational use of a budget-sensitive plan. And the Netherlands route is closed regardless, because SAE cannot sponsor a residence permit — a point worth internalising, since BOTH Dutch private providers in this slice are visa-dead for the same reason. Two things are genuinely worth extracting. First, the English bar: IELTS 6.0 with 5.5 per band, with Duolingo 120 and even GCSE English grade C accepted as alternatives. portfolio: NOW VERIFIED — previously unpublished, now fully specified. englishTest: IELTS ACCEPTED, and NOW VERIFIED AT A MATERIALLY LOWER LEVEL — this was previously recorded as unknown. study: NOW VERIFIED on the programme page. Three modules: CORE — Performance Studies, Music Production, Entrepreneurship; FINAL PROJECT — Master's Advising, Culminating Experience; ELECTIVE — Performance Studies, Music Languages and Techniques, Technology and Innovation, Pedagogy and Research. The programme integrates studio recording and mixing processes with performance development across jazz, Latin, world music, pop, rock and electronic styles, and covers 'strategies for producing and marketing their performance projects'.
recommendation: Rule this out — the gate is absolute and it is not about money. Admission requires three performance videos including at least one live performance, and the school demands an 'advanced level of instrumental or vocal technique'. He has no instrumental or vocal training whatsoever, so there is no version of the next twelve months in which he becomes an advanced performer. Applying would waste the $150 fee and the preparation time. Two pieces of genuinely useful intelligence come out of verifying it anyway. First, the Berklee Groove Scholarship of up to 90% of tuition is the largest award anywhere in this batch — but it is bound to this programme and to accomplished drummers, bassists and rhythm-section players, so it is unreachable for him and should not appear in any budget scenario. Second, and more practically, this is the ONLY Berklee Valencia master with a reduced English requirement: IELTS 6.5 rather than 7.5, TOEFL 80 rather than 100. That confirms the 7.5 he faces for MPTI is a programme-level choice, not a negotiable institutional minimum, so he should plan his IELTS preparation around the harder number. Included here specifically so he does not discover the performance requirement after paying an application fee.

He satisfies the published entry requirement today: a 2:1-equivalent BSc plus a stated interest in a music career. No portfolio gate, no music degree, no audition, and September 2027 is published as the start date. The supporting statement must address: what you previously studied and what you learnt about music production; why you want to study MA Music Production at Leeds Beckett; who your influences are as a songwriter/performer/producer and why; what music you are currently listening to and why; the type of music you like to write/perform/produce and why; an example of something you found particularly challenging in previous studies and/or music production work and how you met it; what you want to do after your studies. The rule literally names the case: 'at least a second class honours degree in a NON-COGNATE SUBJECT supported by evidence of an aptitude for the subject applied for'. Examples can include: Sound/video recordings of your production work; Original sound recordings that you have composed, recorded, mixed, arranged or produced. Your work should be uploaded to a media-hosting site such as YouTube, Soundcloud or Bandcamp. You should also include a PDF document with an overview of each of the examples (i.e. when, where and for whom was the production completed?) and identify your role/s in the production process (Are you the performer, composer, producer or recording engineer?). Links to these documents should be added to the supporting statement in your application.' No maximum duration is imposed.

duration: 1 year full-time. Start date 21 September 2026 for the 2026 cohort (so expect ~20 September 2027 for the 2027 cohort). 180 UK credits ≈ 90 ECTS.
study: 'Build upon your practical and theoretical experience of contemporary music production and apply a range of creative production approaches in industry-standard studio facilities.' You 'explore the technical and creative aspects of recording, arranging, mixing and producing', 'produce a wide range of commercial and non-commercial musical projects', 'critically analyse the productions of others', and 'work with peers and collaborate with other artists and producers'. Facilities in the new Leeds School of Arts building: dedicated music studios, Foley studios, dubbing and music recording studios, acoustic labs, post-production suites, a 220-seat Dolby Atmos-accredited cinema. Artist-in-Residence sessions have included Utah Saints, I Monster, Chris T-T, Ian Prowse, Tom Williams, Matt Deighton.

institution: Netherlands private higher-education sector (systematic check across NVAO/CROHO-registered private institutio…
programme: MARKET-LEVEL FINDING — no private NVAO-accredited master in sound design or music production exists in the Netherlands
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background; portfolio required, so build it
qualification: NONE EXISTS. After searching in both English and Dutch ('master muziekproductie', 'opleiding sound design particulier', 'niet-bekostigde opleiding', 'master sound design Nederland particuliere hogeschool NVAO'), I found NO privately-run, NVAO-accredited master's degree in sound design, music production, audio engineering, music technology, immersive audio or electronic music performance anywhere in the Netherlands.
accreditation: DEFINITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING. In the Netherlands the audio/music education market splits cleanly in two, with nothing in between. (1) ACCREDITED = PUBLIC. Every NVAO-accredited master in this field belongs to a government-funded ('bekostigd') public institution: HKU Utrecht (Master of Music pathway Music Design; Sound Design and Audio Design at bachelor level), Conservatorium van Amsterdam / AHK (Master Immersive Audio — NVAO-assessed; plus the AEMA associate degree for electronic musicians, English-taught), Codarts Rotterdam, and the Institute of Sonology at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague. These are all excluded from this brief as public. (2) PRIVATE = UNACCREDITED. Every private audio provider in the country (SAE, Abbey Road Institute, Sound Education, Pro Audio Education, DDMA, Master The Mix, AV Sound Education, DJ School Amsterdam, Music Production Academy) holds at most CRKBO and/or NRTO registration. CRKBO is a short-vocational-education register that governs VAT exemption; NRTO is a private-training trade association quality mark. NEITHER IS AN ACCREDITATION AND NEITHER CONFERS DEGREE STATUS. The sole exception — SAE's MA/MSc — is a UK University of Hertfordshire award delivered fully online, with no Dutch status and no campus component. Meanwhile private institutions that DO hold NVAO accreditation (Tio, Wittenborg, Nyenrode) operate exclusively in business and hospitality.

The mid-market one-year full-time option is Abbey Road Institute at €18,860–€20,160. Amsterdam living costs add roughly €14,000–€18,000 per year on top.
scholarshipDetail: SECTOR-WIDE FINDING: NOT ONE private Dutch audio provider publishes any scholarship, bursary, fee waiver or discount available to a non-EU or Tunisian applicant. The only financial mechanisms found were (a) upfront-payment savings of €1,300–€5,670 versus instalment plans, (b) alumni/staff discounts of 25% at SAE UK, (c) 35–50% student software discounts at Sound Education and AV Sound Education, and (d) a Dutch study-cost INCOME TAX deduction promoted by Abbey Road Institute and Pro Audio Education, which requires Dutch taxable income and by Abbey Road's own admission 'doesn't apply to those receiving governmental benefits or who aren't yet employed'. That last one is effectively worthless to an incoming international student and should be discounted entirely when comparing prices. Dutch DUO student finance is unavailable at every private provider without exception.

recommendation: BOTTOM LINE FOR THE NETHERLANDS: DO NOT BUILD THE SEPTEMBER 2027 PLAN AROUND A DUTCH PRIVATE SCHOOL. There is no private NVAO-accredited master in this field in the country, and no private audio provider can sponsor his residence permit — so the two things he needs (an accredited master + a visa) are simply not purchasable from the Dutch private sector at any price. It also, separately, includes a real production test (scoring a film clip in Pro Tools) — but that is the third of three parts and cannot be reached without passing the first. (2) The record does not note that instruction requires DSH-1 GERMAN, nor that entry requires a subject-specific BFA in Sound or Tonmeister. Its 'Possible' chance rating is wrong; this is closed to him.

institution: HAW Hamburg – Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften Hamburg, Dept. Medientechnik
programme: Zeitabhängige Medien / Sound – Vision (M.A.) — the Sound–Vision branch of Sound–Vision–Games
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in German — language is the real gate
verdictWhy: Painful, because on every axis except one this is the best-designed option he will find: it explicitly welcomes IT and media-informatics graduates, the gate is a work sample and an interview with no audition or ear test, and it costs €397 a semester including a nationwide rail pass. But instruction is in German at C1, and he has none. C1 from zero is not achievable for September 2027, so the door is shut for this cycle.
correction: TWO corrections. (1) The record does not mention that the programme is TAUGHT IN GERMAN and requires C1 — the single fact that decides the case. Its 'Possible' rating is therefore wrong; it is not possible for him in this cycle. (2) Gate recorded as 'Portfolio + exam/interview' — there is no exam. It is a work sample, then an interview, then language proof. Also worth recording as a genuine positive for a later cycle: this is the only programme in the batch whose entry rule names IT and media informatics as accepted backgrounds.
qualification: M.A. (Master of Arts)
tuition: No tuition fee for anyone, including non-EU students — DAAD confirms international students pay the same as domestic students with no additional tuition. Semester contribution: the official HAW page states €397 including the semester ticket and the Germany-wide Deutschlandticket rail pass; the DAAD entry states 'currently EUR 335.60'. Take €397 as the current figure from the university's own page and expect minor annual variation. This is the cheapest option of the six.
scholarshipDetail: No institutional scholarship found. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines, Deutschlandstipendium. DAAD/Tunisia eligibility NOT re-verified in this pass. Note DAAD funding conventionally starts 1 October, which sits awkwardly with an April intake — check whether DAAD will fund a summer-semester start.
entry: A completed Bachelor's or Diplom degree with a MINIMUM OF 210 ECTS in 'media technology, media systems, computer science, IT (applicants with a degree in applied IT or with a specialism in media are welcome), communication design, illustration or a related subject'; German C1; English B1 (tested at interview); and a passed aptitude assessment. A rating of 3.0 or better in part 2 of the aptitude assessment qualifies for admission.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly, and this is the single best formal fit of the six. The accepted-degree list names 'computer science, IT (applicants with a degree in applied IT or with a specialism in media are welcome)' by name. THE REAL GATE IS CREDITS, NOT SUBJECT: the minimum is 210 ECTS. A three-year 180-ECTS bachelor is short by a full semester; a four-year US-style BSc such as SMU MedTech's is likely to clear 210, but he must obtain a formal ECTS credit statement from SMU MedTech and, if short, ask HAW how the shortfall can be made up. No music background of any kind is required and there is no instrumental audition.
portfolio: CORRECTED to less specific than previously recorded. The official page states only: 'A sample of your work that provides a detailed and comprehensive demonstration of your interest in and your aptitude and potential for your chosen branch of the degree course.' The page does NOT publish a number range, and the previously recorded 'between 3 and 10 work samples' with the enumerated accepted media types (video, animation, light design, installation, soundscape, music production, performance, interactive work) could NOT be confirmed in this pass — treat the count and the media list as UNVERIFIED and request the current Arbeitsproben specification from the Fakultät DMI in writing.
audition: NO live audition and no music-theory test. Two-stage Eignungsfeststellung, confirmed: 'Part 1: Submission of a sample of your work' — reviewed by the selection committee in early November — and 'Part 2: Interview, to which you will be invited if your performance in Part 1 merits it.' German C1 and English B1 are verified at the interview. A grade of 3.0 or better in part 2 qualifies for admission.
deadline: TWO-STEP AND PARTLY CURRENT. Step 1, aptitude-test registration with work samples: 1–31 October, confirmed as 01.10.2026 – 31.10.2026 for the next intake (one secondary source says 'until 14 October' — resolve this discrepancy with the faculty before relying on the end of the month). Step 2, formal application for the study place: 1 December – 15 January. CRITICAL: entry is SUMMER SEMESTER ONLY, starting early April. There is no September/October intake at all. His options are April 2027 (register Oct 2026, apply Dec 2026–Jan 2027 — very tight, and impossible at C1 German from a standing start) or April 2028.
opens: 1 October — registration for the aptitude test opens. CONFIRMED CURRENT: the DAAD database publishes the window as '01.10.2026 – 31.10.2026' for the aptitude test, i.e. the live window for the April 2027 intake opens in about ten weeks.
duration: 3 semesters. The official HAW page and the DAAD entry both state 3 semesters and neither prints the ECTS figure; German programme databases give 90 ECTS, which is consistent with 210 + 90 = 300 ECTS. Treat 90 ECTS as PARTIAL-verified.
study: CONFIRMED as project-centred study at the intersection of science, technology and creative design, combining sound and moving image as the central means of expression in film, video and music production as well as event and performance technology. Modules span audio technology and sound design, video technology and image design, VFX, interactive design, lighting technology and design, and production/project management. The parallel Games branch covers concept art, 3D animation, level and game design and interactive programming with industry partners. Graduates go to audio/video/lighting manufacturers, production studios and theatres. Nationally distinctive in linking sound, moving image and games in one degree.
recommendation: Structurally the friendliest German public option for a software-engineering graduate — computer science and IT are named as welcome, there is no audition or theory paper, and the total institutional cost is about €397 a semester. But three real obstacles stack up against his stated plan: German C1 is the highest language bar on this list; the 210-ECTS minimum may formally exclude his degree and must be checked with a credit statement; and there is NO September intake, so September 2027 is impossible — realistically April 2028, with the October 2026 window arriving too soon. It is also media and event technology rather than club-music production, so even on success it would not directly serve a DJ/producer career.

institution: Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln (HfMT Köln)

verdictWhy: This is the best value proposition in the batch and deserves to be at the top of his list. A real Master of Music in contemporary popular music production, from a German state university, with no tuition fee; entry demands only two self-produced tracks plus a production made from raw material they send him — a production test, not an audition, with no ear-training exam and no instrument; and the German requirement is A2, not C1, which he can genuinely reach by March 2027. Confirm with Prof. Podmore that a software engineering BSc counts as an 'affine subject', and treat the 2 March non-EU deadline as the real date.
correction: THREE corrections, all substantial. (1) Gate recorded as 'Portfolio + exam/interview' — this misses the defining feature. The gate is a PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST: 'you prepare a production from the (raw) material you receive from us in advance after the application deadline'. That is the job, not a barrier, and it should never be filed with the auditions. (2) The record does not capture that the German requirement is only A2 — far below HAW Hamburg's C1 and Babelsberg's DSH-1 — which is what makes this the one reachable German programme in the batch. (3) The record gives no deadline; the operative one for a Tunisian is the non-EU deadline of 2 March for winter-semester entry, not the general deadline.
qualification: Master of Music (M.Mus.)

tuition: €0 tuition (North Rhine-Westphalia charges no tuition to non-EU students)
otherFees: Semester contribution UNVERIFIED (NRW typically approx. €250–300/semester incl. Semesterticket)
totalCost: Tuition €0; approx. €1,100 in semester fees over 2 years; Cologne living costs approx. €1,000–1,200/month

Compare the sister programme Elektronische Komposition at the same institution, which demands a FOUR-YEAR BACHELOR IN COMPOSITION. Whether a BSc Software Engineering counts as 'affine' to music production MUST BE CONFIRMED with Prof. Jonathan Podmore (jonathan.podmore@hfmt-koeln.de), but the wording is materially more open.

Only two tracks — the lowest portfolio volume of any Field B programme found in the territory.

This is a practical production test — exactly the kind of assessment a self-taught producer can prepare for, and it does NOT test classical instrumental skill or conservatoire ear-training.

entry: Verbatim: 'A completed university degree in science, engineering, humanities, social science, arts, business, or law'; plus 'knowledge of higher mathematics (analysis, linear algebra) at the level of the basic lectures of a science or engineering degree (at least 10 LP)'; plus 'Evidence of programming language or computer algebra system knowledge'. Admission is described as open ('open admission' / no NC), subject to meeting these prerequisites.
acceptsNonMusic: YES, EMPHATICALLY — AND IT IS BUILT FOR SOMEONE LIKE HIM. Quoted verbatim: 'A completed university degree in SCIENCE, ENGINEERING, humanities, social science, arts, business, or law.' Music is not among the required subjects at all; what IS required is 'knowledge of higher mathematics (analysis, linear algebra) at the level of the basic lectures of a science or engineering degree (at least 10 LP)' and 'evidence of programming language or computer algebra system knowledge'. A BSc Software Engineering satisfies BOTH mathematical and programming prerequisites outright. ON SUBJECT GROUNDS THIS IS THE SINGLE BEST-MATCHED PROGRAMME IN GERMANY FOR HIM. It is the language, not the subject, that closes it.
portfolio: NONE. No portfolio, no tracks, no recordings are required — admission is on transcript evidence of mathematics and programming. For a candidate with no portfolio, that is a significant advantage.
audition: NO AUDITION, NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM, NO PRODUCTION TEST. The programme is described as open admission with subject prerequisites verified from the transcript; no aptitude examination of any kind is published. THIS IS THE CLEANEST GATE IN GERMANY — and it is unreachable only because of the C1 German requirement.
deadline: Not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. TU Berlin master deadlines for international applicants are typically 15 January for the winter semester (via uni-assist), and the university warns that 'Master's programs may have different (and significantly earlier) application deadlines'. Applicants with foreign degrees normally go through uni-assist, which adds weeks. VERIFY DIRECTLY.

languageReq: GERMAN C1 for applicants with foreign qualifications, AND English B2. This is the hardest language combination in the sweep and rules the programme out for a September 2027 start.
englishTest: B2 CEFR English required in addition to C1 German. Accepted certificates not specified on the page read — UNVERIFIED.
study: Verbatim curriculum coverage: 'technical acoustics, room acoustics, electro-acoustic systems, empirical methods for analyzing language and music reception, digital audio signal processing, psychoacoustics, and acoustic media art design.' FIT NOTE: this is audio ENGINEERING and audio SCIENCE — DSP, acoustics, psychoacoustics, empirical research. It is squarely in the Toningenieur/audio-technology part of the field, but it is a research-and-engineering degree, not a studio-craft or record-making degree. It would make him an audio engineer or researcher, not a record producer.

External applicants must also pass an admission examination and submit 'certificates of your musical-artistic background' to the KUG Studien- und Prüfungsabteilung by 30 June.

The rule is 'gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigtes Studium' judged by the dean, with 'up to 30 additional ECTS from the bachelor program may be required' — an engineering/computer-science bachelor is the natural equivalence route here, unlike the pure music schools. BUT the candidate must still pass the KUG artistic aptitude test and produce 'certificates of your musical-artistic background', which he does not have. This is the single most engineering-friendly entry in the DACH territory for a software-engineering BSc.

Held online.

study: Inter-university Tonmeister/audio-engineering master combining electrical engineering and IT coursework with music practice, recording studio work, acoustics, audio signal processing and sound engineering. Taught jointly by TU Graz and KUG (home of the IEM).

correction: CONFIRMED AND UPGRADED. The record hedged this as a programme whose 'latest announcements and application-date pages [are] all 2021-22'. That suspicion is now confirmed from the department's own current master's index: the programme is listed with no call, while two sibling programmes carry live 2025-26 and 2026-27 calls. qualification: Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (ΔΜΣ) in 'Τεχνολογίες Ήχου, Βίντεο και Μετάδοσης'. On paper a real second-cycle Greek state degree established by Government Gazette decision. IN PRACTICE THIS IS NOW DOUBTFUL — see accreditationStatus. A degree cannot support a residence permit if the programme does not admit students.
accreditation: ESTABLISHED BY ΦΕΚ Β' 3257/8-8-2018 BUT ALMOST CERTAINLY DEFUNCT — the previous record's caution is now upgraded to a firm finding on the basis of six independent signals gathered by reading the programme's own site directly: (1) the most recent call for applications on the site is for academic year 2021-22, closing 23 September 2021 — FIVE consecutive admission cycles (2022-23 through 2026-27) with no call; (2) the site's 'ΗΜΕΡΟΜΗΝΙΕΣ ΑΙΤΗΣΕΩΝ' (application dates) menu contains entries only for 2018-19, 2019-20, 2020-21 and 2021-22; (3) every announcement, timetable and thesis-topic page is frozen at 2021-22; (4) the site has no valid HTTPS certificate and serves only over plain HTTP, with a '© 2018' footer; (5) its 'Διεθνείς Φοιτητές' (International Students) link points to teipireuofficegr.blogspot.gr — the blog of TEI Piraeus, an institution that ceased to exist when UniWA was created in 2018; (6) the fee regulation still cites Ν.4485/2017 art.35(2), a law REPEALED and replaced by Ν.4957/2022, under which every Greek ΠΜΣ had to be formally re-established — there is no evidence this one was. Decisively, the department's own MSc list shows its sibling programmes carrying live 2025-2026 and 2026-27 προκηρύξεις while this one carries none. It also does not appear in the Ministry's public 'Study in Greece' programme finder. The department page listing is a stale entry, not evidence of an operating programme.
tuition: The same €700 per semester — Greece operates no separate non-EU rate for this ΠΜΣ and the published fee applied to all admitted students. CONFIRMED from the programme's own fees page, BUT that page has not been updated since 2018 and still cites the repealed Ν.4485/2017. The figure is real but historical; it describes a programme that is no longer admitting.
otherFees: Recognition of the Tunisian degree (ΔΟΑΤΑΠ/ΑΤΕΕΝ) would carry a fee; plus Greek residence-permit fee, health insurance, certified translations. Amounts UNVERIFIED and moot.
totalCost: Had it been running, roughly €1,400–€2,800 in tuition depending on programme length, with Athens living costs dominating. Academically the cheapest good technical fit found — which is exactly why its apparent closure matters.
scholarshipDetail: The programme states it MAY award 'υποτροφίες αριστείας' (excellence scholarships) depending on its annual finances, by decision of the Departmental Assembly on the Coordinating Committee's recommendation, and only to full-time students who have not taken study extensions — CONFIRMED verbatim, but no amount, number or criteria were ever published. No dedicated non-EU scholarship. Moot while the programme is not admitting.
entry: Holders of a first-cycle degree from a Greek university/TEI department or an equivalent internationally recognised institution. Selection procedure CONFIRMED verbatim from the programme's own page: assessment of the candidate's file AND an interview, participating EQUALLY (ισοβαρώς) in the ranking; the selection committee is composed of departmental professors appointed by the Departmental Assembly; the interview assesses overall preparation, motivation and interest, and the candidate's training in relation to the ΠΜΣ subject. Candidates are NOT notified individually — the interview invitation is posted on the noticeboard and website. 25 places were advertised in the last (2021-22) call.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — this is an engineering MSc that expects no musical training at all, and priority is given to Electrical and Electronic Engineering graduates. A BSc in Software Engineering would be a plausible file. His engineering background would be an ADVANTAGE here, unlike at the conservatories. This is precisely what makes the programme's apparent death so unfortunate.
portfolio: None. No portfolio required — file plus interview only. It was the only programme in this batch a candidate with no portfolio could enter on academic record alone.
audition: None. No audition. An interview before a committee of departmental professors, weighted 50% against the file.
deadline: 23 September 2021 for the last published cycle (25 places). No subsequent deadline exists.
opens: NO CALL SINCE 2021. Historical pattern: the 2020-21 call closed 18 September 2020 and the 2021-22 call closed 23 September 2021, both with extensions. Nothing has been published for 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 or 2026-27. There is no basis for expecting a call in summer 2027.
duration: Never published on any page of the programme site — STILL UNVERIFIED after reading the site in full. Fees are quoted per semester with provision for part-time study at 50% and for 'extension' semesters, implying at least three teaching semesters.
languageReq: Never published — UNVERIFIED and now moot. Greek ΠΜΣ of this type normally require documented Greek plus a certificate of English for the literature.
study: Signal-level engineering of sound and picture: studio and broadcast technology (course AVB.2.7 'Τεχνολογία Στούντιο και Μετάδοσης'), image and video processing (AVB.1.4), acoustics, compression and coding, digital broadcasting. This is broadcast/audio engineering, not music production or DJing.
recommendation: AVOID — CORRECTED FROM 'BEST-FITTING GREEK OPTION' TO A CLOSED FILE. The previous record hedged that the programme 'often means it has stopped admitting'; reading the programme's own site directly turns that hedge into a finding. The last call for applications was for 2021-22, closing 23 September 2021. Five consecutive admission cycles have passed with no call. The application-dates menu stops at 2021-22. Every announcement, timetable and results page is frozen at 2021-22. The site has no valid HTTPS certificate and a 2018 copyright footer. Its 'International Students' link points to the blog of TEI Piraeus, an institution abolished in 2018. Its fee regulation still cites Ν.4485/2017, repealed by Ν.4957/2022, under which every Greek ΠΜΣ had to be re-established — with no sign this one was. And the department's own MSc page shows the sibling programmes carrying live 2025-26 and 2026-27 calls while this one carries none. That is a dead programme with a stale directory entry, not a dormant one. This is doubly unfortunate because it was, on paper, the best academic fit in the whole set for him: an audio and broadcast ENGINEERING master requiring no portfolio and no audition, selecting on file plus interview weighted equally, at €700 a semester in a public university, where his software-engineering degree would have been an advantage rather than an oddity. Two things killed it anyway even if it revived: everything is in Greek, which he does not speak, and there is no evidence of English-medium delivery. Action: one cheap email to eee@uniwa.gr and mscavb@uniwa.gr asking whether the ΠΜΣ will admit for 2027-28 and whether it has been re-established under Ν.4957/2022. Expect no reply or a negative one. Do not build any plan around this.

institution: EMMA — Escola de Música Moderna (founded and run by composer/guitarist Pedro Duarte)
programme: Curso de Produção Musical — MUSIC-SCHOOL TUITION, NOT A MASTER'S AND NOT A DEGREE
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Portuguese — language is the real gate
qualification: NOT A DEGREE AND NOT A POSTGRADUATE QUALIFICATION — CONFIRMED. EMMA is a DGERT-certified training entity issuing its own school diploma. No ECTS, no grau académico, no A3ES or DGES involvement. Its DGERT certification attaches principally to its long-form 'Curso Profissional de Música Moderna' (8 semesters), which it claims is the only one of its kind in Portugal — the Produção Musical offering is ordinary fee-paying music-school tuition alongside it.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL HIGHER EDUCATION. EMMA is certified by DGERT (Direção-Geral do Emprego e das Relações de Trabalho — the labour ministry's vocational-training regulator), a legitimate vocational quality mark and NOT an educational accreditation. It is NOT accredited by A3ES and NOT registered with DGES, so nothing it issues is a Portuguese higher-education qualification: no grau, no ECTS, no Bologna/EHEA standing, no PhD route, no visa weight. It is not a mestrado and not a pós-graduação. Its DGERT certification attaches chiefly to the 8-semester Curso Profissional de Música Moderna; the Produção Musical offering is fee-paying tuition, not a certified programme in its own right — UNVERIFIED whether the production course itself falls inside the DGERT scope, and he should ask. The ICMP London partnership is a commercial/pedagogical partnership only and confers no accreditation, no validation and no award.
tuition: UNVERIFIED as a programme total — billing is monthly with no fixed programme length, and the course spans 3 levels over 1 to 4 years. At the published band a single year would run roughly €720 to €2,880, and the full 3-level path could run far higher over four years. Do not treat that range as a quote; the production course's own rate must be requested directly.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — no enrolment, materials, diploma or exam fee published. Combo is flagged as a paid additional module. Ask for a full fee schedule before committing.
totalCost: UNVERIFIED. Indicative only: €60–€240/month across all the school's courses, i.e. roughly €720–€2,880 per year, with the production course's actual rate unpublished and requiring a direct request. Plus a Cubase licence and MIDI keyboard, and Greater Lisbon living costs if attending in person — none of it visa-bearing.
scholarshipDetail: NONE published — VERIFIED ABSENT.
entry: Open enrolment from age 12 ('A partir dos 12 anos') — VERIFIED. No academic prerequisite, no audition published.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — open enrolment from age 12 with no academic prerequisite. His BSc is neither required nor relevant.
portfolio: None — VERIFIED as open enrolment.
audition: None published — UNVERIFIED whether a level-placement assessment is used, which is common at music schools offering 3 graded levels.
deadline: None.
duration: VERIFIED STRUCTURE, absent from the draft: 3 levels spanning 1 to 4 years, billed as ongoing monthly tuition rather than a fixed-length programme. Lesson formats: 30 minutes or 1 hour, group or individual, online or in person. NO ECTS.
englishTest: None. Not applicable — teaching is in Portuguese, which is itself the barrier.
study: VERIFIED. The production course is described as one of the most vocationally oriented in Portugal for home-studio work and DAW use, taking a track 'desde a ideia à concretização via Cubase e com recurso a teclado midi' — from idea to realisation via CUBASE with a MIDI keyboard — with emphasis on recording techniques, plugin use, mixing and audio mastering. Structure: Produção class + Songwriting class + Especialização (weekly projects), with free additional modules in Teoria Musical & Treino Auditivo, Ritmos Aplicados and Coro de Música Moderna, plus Combo as a paid add-on. The school also teaches guitar, voice and modern singing, piano/keyboard, drums, saxophone, violin, bass, musical initiation, combo, theory and ear training. CRITICAL MISMATCH CONFIRMED: the production teaching is CUBASE-centred, not Ableton — the wrong tool for someone targeting electronic music, DJing and live performance.
recommendation: NOT A SERIOUS CANDIDATE FOR HIS PLAN — AND WEAKER ON VERIFICATION THAN THE DRAFT SUGGESTED. Three verified facts push this further down. It is in QUELUZ, not Lisbon — a suburban commute, not a city-centre school. It teaches CUBASE with a MIDI keyboard, which is the wrong toolchain for electronic music, DJing and live performance; he would be buying skills and software he then has to replace. And it enrols from age 12 over a 1-to-4-year, 3-level structure, which is a children's-and-hobbyists' music school cadence, not a professional intensive. Against that, the honest counterpoint stands: he has NO music training at all, and that — not gear, not software — is his real weakness for a portfolio-weighted selection like ReSound or Lusófona. Somewhere in the €60–€240/month band there is genuine value in theory, ear training and keyboard skills, and EMMA's free Teoria Musical & Treino Auditivo module plus its ICMP London partnership suggest the musicianship teaching is taken seriously. But he can get exactly that in Tunis or online for less, in a language he is fluent in, without a Portuguese commute and without a visa problem. VERDICT: exclude from the Portugal strategy. If he ever wants formal musicianship training, buy it locally or online — and if he wants production training in Portugal, ProDJ's Master Producer is better on toolchain, hours, facilities, English delivery and transparency for a known, fixed price.

programme: Curso Produção e Criação Musical (and sibling short courses: Produção Musical e Identidade Sonora, Hip Hop e Música Urb…
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Portuguese — language is the real gate
qualification: ETIC school diploma, certified nationally through DGERT and classified as 'Outra Formação Profissional' (Other Professional Training). NOT a mestrado, NOT a pós-graduação, NOT a degree, NOT A3ES-accredited, NOT ECTS-rated. Retained in this list only as an explicit warning entry.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL AND NOT A DEGREE — CONFIRMED, and weaker than the earlier brief suggested. The qualification is an ETIC diploma certified through DGERT under the category 'Outra Formação Profissional' (Other Professional Training). DGERT certifies VOCATIONAL TRAINING PROVIDERS, not higher education — it is not A3ES, confers no academic level, no ECTS and no degree. (Note: the earlier brief's emphasis on 'Pearson BTEC accredited centre' was not borne out on this course page, which cites DGERT; ETIC may hold BTEC status for other courses, but this course is not a BTEC award.) There is no mestrado and no pós-graduação here of any kind.
tuition: UNVERIFIED. Likely in the low thousands of euros given the 170-hour scope, but not confirmed.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — not published in readable form.
totalCost: UNVERIFIED — no readable published prices. Whatever the figure, it buys 170 hours of evening classes with no academic credit and no visa basis.
scholarshipDetail: ETIC operates a merit scholarship scheme ('Regulamento de Atribuição de Bolsa de Mérito') worth €300 for ETIC annual courses, awarded on academic merit and financial situation — a token amount. The site also signposts commercial training-finance products from Portuguese banks (Caixa Geral de Depósitos, Santander, Banco CTT, BPI), which are consumer loans, not aid, and would not be available to a non-resident. As a non-degree course it sits entirely outside DGES bolsas de ação social, which in any case exclude international students from direct monetary support. Open access in practice.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — the published requirement is only 'preferably 12th-grade schooling or proven professional experience'. No degree and no music background is required. His BSc far exceeds the entry bar, which is precisely the problem: this is set well below his level.
portfolio: VERIFIED (and more than the earlier brief found): a portfolio or showreel IS required, together with a motivation letter stating career objectives and an interview, in person or online.
audition: No audition. Interview only.
deadline: September, for the October intake. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm.
opens: March (applications run March to September for an October start). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm 2027 dates.
duration: VERIFIED AND DECISIVE: 170 HOURS over ONE SEMESTER. Classes Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, 19:00–23:00, in person. Maximum 16 students. This is an evening short course, not a programme of study — the earlier brief's description of 'annual courses' understated how small it is.
englishTest: NOT APPLICABLE — Portuguese-language course. IELTS is irrelevant. Portuguese proficiency is required.
study: A practical, technical and artistic pass through the music-production process — recording techniques, songwriting, production, audio manipulation, mixing, mastering and marketing — compressed into 170 contact hours.
recommendation: NOT A MASTER'S AND NOT A DEGREE — listed purely so he does not mistake it for one when it surfaces in searches for 'pós-graduação som' or 'produção musical Lisboa'. The verification makes the case even clearer than before: this is 170 hours of evening classes over a single semester, certified by DGERT as 'Other Professional Training', with no ECTS, no academic level, a €300 token scholarship, and no publicly readable price. It cannot support a Portuguese student visa and must never be the basis of a residence application. Where it COULD genuinely help: if he takes the Lusófona or UCP route and is already lawfully resident in Lisbon, a 170-hour evening course at €19:00–23:00 three nights a week is a cheap, practical way to add hands-on production craft alongside an academic master's — and its portfolio-plus-motivation-letter entry process is trivial for him. That is its only sensible role: a supplement AFTER residence, never the reason for it.

institution: Universitat de Barcelona (UB) with Universitat Rovira i Virgili (URV) and Escola Superior de Música de Catalu…

verdictWhy: Wrong subject and wrong language. This is an interdisciplinary music-and-art master's whose preferred applicant is a history-of-art graduate, taught in Catalan and Spanish, with no portfolio, no production element and no studio training published anywhere. It would not teach him to make records even if he could follow the lectures.
correction: THREE corrections. (1) COST BAND WRONG: recorded as 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr', but the published non-EU rate is €82 per credit, which over 60 ECTS is roughly €4,920 — more than three times the recorded band. (2) Gate recorded as 'Portfolio only' — no portfolio requirement is published at all, nor any other gate. (3) The record does not flag that instruction is in CATALAN AND SPANISH, nor that the programme is aimed at humanities and history-of-art graduates rather than producers. Its 'Possible' rating is not sustainable for this candidate.
qualification: Màster Universitari (official university master), 60 ECTS — a real state-recognised second-cycle degree in the university track, giving doctoral access.
accreditation: Official university master awarded by UB jointly with URV and ESMUC. Genuine EQF 7 second-cycle degree.
tuition: CORRECTED IN STATUS, NOT IN NUMBER. Do not budget on €4,920; the current Catalan decree rate will be higher. What survives, and is the genuinely transferable finding, is the STRUCTURE: Catalonia applies an approximately 3x surcharge to non-EU non-resident students on official university masters (€27.67 vs €82 per credit in the published year). That multiplier, not the absolute euro figure, is what he should carry to every other Catalan option including UPF and UB programmes.

A Software Engineering BSc would be an 'other discipline' individual-assessment case — formally possible, which is unusual for Spain.

institution: Hochschule Luzern – Musik (Lucerne School of Music, FH Zentralschweiz)
programme: MA Music — Major Music and Digital Creation (MUDC)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in German — language is the real gate
qualification: Master of Arts in Music, Major Music and Digital Creation — full second-cycle degree. FIELD CAVEAT: this is a music-and-IT master, NOT a record-production or studio-craft degree. Included because the entry gate is by far the most open in Switzerland for a software engineer and the parent should see it.
accreditation: Public Fachhochschule; the institution's own footer states 'Institutionell akkreditiert nach HFKG 2019–2026'.
tuition: CHF 1,300 PER SEMESTER = CHF 2,600 PER YEAR for a Tunisian. Verbatim from the HSLU Musik tuition-fees page: domestic students 'CHF 800.–'; international students 'CHF 1'300.– for international students (for students with foreign citizenship who enter or have entered Switzerland for the purpose of studying.)' — a CHF 500/semester surcharge, applied on entry-for-study rather than on nationality bloc, so a Tunisian pays the same as any other incoming foreigner. This is the HIGHEST Swiss tuition found, though still modest.
otherFees: Substantial and worth counting, all quoted from the fees page: application CHF 200 'per entrance examination (will be credited upon enrolment)'; a further 'CHF 390.– (for two practical examinations)'; one-off enrolment fee CHF 390; HSLU Card CHF 50 one-off; module examination CHF 150; photocopying flat rate CHF 45; service fee flat rate CHF 45; university sports CHF 25 per semester.
totalCost: Tuition CHF 2,600/yr, plus roughly CHF 800–1,000 of one-off entry and card fees and a few hundred a year in flat-rate charges. Lucerne living approx CHF 20,000–24,000/yr (UNVERIFIED). Two-year total including living: roughly CHF 47,000–55,000.
scholarshipDetail: Not published on the pages read. UNVERIFIED.
entry: THE EXCEPTION CLAUSE IS THE POINT. HSLU master admission normally requires, verbatim, 'a Bachelor's degree from the Lucerne School of Music' with preparatory modules, or 'a Bachelor's degree from a music conservatory or comparable educational establishment'. BUT, verbatim and specific to this major: 'For the Music and Digital Creation major specifically, a Bachelor's degree obtained at a university of applied sciences (sur-dossier admission) is sufficient – REGARDLESS OF THE DEGREE PROGRAMME.' Separately, the master overview page states verbatim: 'Für Studierende ohne einen Bachelor-Abschluss einer Schweizerischen Musikhochschule kann eine Standortbestimmung Theorie angeordnet werden. Je nach deren Verlauf muss im ersten Studiensemester Master ein Auflagenmodul erfolgreich absolviert werden, in dem die Zielkompetenzen des Bachelor-Abschlusses der Hochschule Luzern – Musik erarbeitet werden. Vom Bestehen des Auflagenmoduls ist die Fortsetzung des Studiums über das erste Semester hinaus abhängig.' So a music-theory placement check can be imposed, with a remedial module in semester one that you must pass to continue — a real risk for someone with no theory background, but it is remedial teaching, not an entry exam.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY AND UNIQUELY. Quoted verbatim: 'a Bachelor's degree obtained at a university of applied sciences (sur-dossier admission) is sufficient – regardless of the degree programme.' This is the only programme found in Switzerland that states in terms that ANY bachelor subject qualifies. A BSc Software Engineering is exactly the profile the major was built for — HSLU publishes a separate curriculum variant for entrants who already hold an informatics bachelor.
portfolio: NO TRACK PORTFOLIO REQUIRED. Instead, verbatim: applicants must 'submit a project description (one A4 page) three weeks before the exam, outlining a music and IT project to be realized during studies'. ONE A4 PAGE. That is the entire submission — no finished tracks, no recordings, no scores. For a candidate with no portfolio yet, this is decisive: he can apply on an idea rather than on a back catalogue.
audition: NEITHER AN AUDITION NOR AN EAR-TRAINING EXAM. Verbatim: this major has 'no ear training test or traditional instrument audition'; the assessment is 'a jury conversation focusing on project goals, program expectations, training content and aims'. It is an interview about a written project idea. ONE CAVEAT, quoted: 'For applicants without a Music Bachelor, additional practical/theory assessment occurs in their musical specialization' — the scope of that additional assessment is not published and is UNVERIFIED; it may be where a music-theory shortfall surfaces, and it links to the Standortbestimmung Theorie / Auflagenmodul mechanism above. (For comparison, HSLU's Major Komposition also has no ear-training component but demands 'three scores in different instrumentation and recordings' plus a 30-minute written analysis — a much harder ask for him.)
deadline: 28 FEBRUARY, verbatim: 'the deadline is 28 February (in a leap year on 29 February)'. This is a standing annual deadline, not a prior-cycle date, so 28 February 2027 for a September 2027 start. NOTE the portfolio timing: the one-page project description is due 'three weeks before the exam', which is later than the application deadline itself.
opens: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Deadline is fixed at 28 February.
duration: Master of Arts in Music, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS (HSLU standard). Two published curricula exist — one 'for students without a BA in Computer Science' and one 'for students with a BA in Informatics'; HE WOULD FOLLOW THE COMPUTER-SCIENCE TRACK, which is shorter on IT foundations and longer on music.
languageReq: German A2 at the start of year one, B1 from year two. No English test published.
study: Verbatim: the major 'aims to build Information and Communications Technologies competencies and their connection with musical content. It provides students with a conceptual and operational toolkit to strategically leverage digital transformation. In addition to mandatory foundational knowledge and basic competencies, students acquire in-depth competencies in the areas of DATA SCIENCE and DIGITAL CREATION. Students are enabled to integrate new digital, artistic, and pedagogical possibilities into their own repertoire of action and expression.' Related minors available at HSLU that lean toward his interests: Minor Groove und Electronics, Minor Media Composer, Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Digitale Kompetenzen für Musik, Bildung und Kultur. FIT VERDICT: data science plus digital creation applied to music. It is NOT recording, mixing or mastering, and HSLU publishes no studio-craft module for it — so it will not by itself teach him to make records. It could however be a route into a Swiss music school on his existing degree, with the Groove und Electronics / Media Composer minors doing some of the work.

institution: Hochschule für Musik Basel FHNW — Institut Klassik / Elektronisches Studio Basel (ESB)
programme: MA Komposition/Musiktheorie — Studienrichtung Audiodesign (published in English as 'Electronic Music' major)
