scholarship: Eduard Brunner Composition Award (internal); FHNW Stipendien pages; Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships
qualification: Master of Arts FHNW in Komposition/Musiktheorie, Studienrichtung Audiodesign — full second-cycle degree, 120 ECTS
accreditation: Public Fachhochschule (FHNW). Governed by the 'Studienreglement Master of Arts FHNW in Komposition/Musiktheorie' in force 1 December 2024, whose §1(2) names the three Studienrichtungen verbatim: 'Komposition, Audiodesign, Theorie der Alten Musik'.
tuition: CHF 1,250 PER SEMESTER = CHF 2,500 PER YEAR for a Tunisian, under FHNW's published three-tier scale 'Semestergebühr 750 CHF (CH) | 1000 CHF (EU/EFTA-Länder) | 1250 CHF (Nicht-EU/Nicht-EFTA)'. A third-country national pays CHF 500/semester more than a Swiss student and CHF 250/semester more than an EU student.
otherFees: Application fee CHF 200 (FHNW HSM standard). Cost of the Goethe/telc B1 certificate. Compulsory Swiss health insurance.
totalCost: Tuition CHF 2,500/yr + CHF 200 one-off + Basel living approx CHF 20,000–24,000/yr (UNVERIFIED). Two-year total roughly CHF 45,000–53,000.
scholarshipDetail: One named internal prize, verbatim: 'Eduard Brunner Composition Award: Every year, one of our students is awarded a composition prize worth CHF 5,000 as part of an internal sonic space basel competition.' That is a prize for enrolled students, not entry funding. General FHNW scholarship pages exist but were not read — UNVERIFIED.
entry: Verbatim: 'In order to enter the FHNW Master of Arts in Composition/Music Theory programme with an Electronic Music Major, applicants must be awarded a Bachelor in Audio Design or equivalent as well as they must have passed the entrance exam and were offered a free place at the Academy (limited places). Applicants who have submitted all the necessary registration documents in time will be invited to the online entrance exam by mail and online meeting.' And: 'The FHNW Master of Arts in Composition/Music Theory with an Audio Design Major is aimed at holders of a Bachelor degree in sound design, electronic music, composition or equivalent qualification.' REQUIRED SKILLS, verbatim: 'Good skills in recording, producing and sound technology'; 'Good in handling diverse editing software (ProTools, Logic, Nuendo, Ableton Live etc.)'; 'Basic knowledge about an audio programming environment (PD, Max/MSP, Supercollider or Csound)'. Governing regulation §4(2) delegates to the Studienrichtungsreglement 'die Anforderungen an den Nachweis bei ausserordentlicher künstlerischer Begabung gemäss § 3 Abs. 1 StuPO' — i.e. there is an exceptional-talent route for applicants who lack the nominal degree; its detailed terms were NOT located and are UNVERIFIED.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY, AND ON SKILLS RATHER THAN ON A DEGREE. Quoted verbatim: 'aimed at holders of a Bachelor degree in sound design, electronic music, composition OR EQUIVALENT QUALIFICATION' and 'applicants must be awarded a Bachelor in Audio Design OR EQUIVALENT'. The published gate is not 'a music bachelor' but a bachelor in an audio/sound field or equivalent, and the required-skills list is entirely technical — recording, producing, sound technology, Pro Tools/Logic/Nuendo/Ableton, and an audio programming environment (Pd, Max/MSP, SuperCollider, Csound). A BSc Software Engineering plus demonstrable DAW and Max/MSP or SuperCollider work is a far more plausible 'equivalent' here than at any conservatoire Tonmeister course. The FHNW study regulation also preserves an 'ausserordentliche künstlerische Begabung' route under StuPO §3(1). NOT GUARANTEED — but this is the most argueable non-music entry in Switzerland.
portfolio: NOT PUBLISHED IN DETAIL ON THE PROGRAMME PAGE — the required-documents accordion is loaded dynamically and its contents could not be read. UNVERIFIED: the number of works, their length, and the file formats. What IS stated verbatim: 'Applicants who have submitted all the necessary registration documents in time will be invited to the online entrance exam by mail and online meeting' — so a submitted dossier gates the exam. Contact klassik.hsm@fhnw.ch or +41 61 264 57 32 for the exact list.
audition: NOT AN AUDITION AND NOT AN EAR-TRAINING EXAM — a remote, portfolio-and-interview assessment. Verbatim: 'Applicants ... will be invited to the ONLINE entrance exam BY MAIL AND ONLINE MEETING' (German page: the Eignungsabklärung takes place 'per Mail und Videokonferenz'). No instrument performance is demanded anywhere on the page; no Gehörbildung/aural test is published; no live attendance in Basel is required. This is the most accessible admission gate found in Switzerland for someone applying from Tunis — the whole assessment can be done from Tunisia. The precise exam content is UNVERIFIED beyond the format.
deadline: 1 MARCH. Verbatim: 'The registration window is open from 15th December to 1st March.' NOT a prior cycle — the page already lists the start date 13.9.2027, so for September 2027 the window is 15 December 2026 – 1 March 2027, with the German B1 certificate due by 31 May 2027.
opens: 15 December (15 December 2026 for the September 2027 intake).
duration: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, at Campus Musik-Akademie Basel. NEXT START PUBLISHED AS 13 SEPTEMBER 2027 — his exact intake.
languageReq: German B1 (CEFR), all four skills tested separately, ALTE-Q-Mark certificate only (Goethe or telc), submitted by 31 May of the entry year — i.e. AFTER admission. Exceptions at the programme head's discretion.
study: Three specialisation fields are offered inside the major, verbatim: 'electro-acoustic composition / live performance / sound and media installation / performance of electroacoustic music'; 'RECORDING/PRODUCTION'; 'audio design & software development'. The second and third are squarely in field for him; the first is the electroacoustic/installation strand this search excludes, so the programme is only a fit if he takes the recording/production route. Graduate competences listed verbatim include: 'compose, produce, perform electronic music'; 'compose and design film/video audio tracks (incl. music, sound effects, speech)'; 'RECORD AND PRODUCE ANY GENRE OF MUSIC IN A PROFESSIONAL RECORDING STUDIO'; 'devise and develop music software to generate, transform and analyse sound'. Taught at the Elektronisches Studio Basel: 'This study programme is geared as closely as possible to practice and dovetails with the production and research activities of the Electronic Studio. From a very early stage, students are involved in the activities of the Electronic Studio and are also required to initiate and carry out their own projects.' Lecturers: Volker Böhm, Svetlana Maraš. The software-development strand is a direct use of his BSc.

institution: Zürcher Hochschule der Künste (ZHdK) — Zurich University of the Arts
programme: MA Composition and Theory — Major Tonmeister:in (Sound Engineering)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in German — language is the real gate
scholarship: Exzellenzstipendium ZHdK; Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (federal, separate)
qualification: Master of Arts in Music — full second-cycle Bologna degree (not continuing education)
accreditation: Public Fachhochschule of the Canton of Zurich (part of ZFH); institutionally accredited under the Swiss HEdA/HFKG. Degree governed by 'Besondere Studienordnung für den Master of Arts in Music 414.263.515'.
tuition: CHF 1,220 per semester = CHF 2,440 per year for a Tunisian. Composed of the standard CHF 720/semester tuition plus the foreign-student surcharge, quoted verbatim: 'Zusätzliche Semestergebühr für ausländische Studierende — Ausländische Studierende, welche zwecks Studium in die Schweiz einreisen und hier Wohnsitz nehmen, begründen keinen zivilrechtlichen Wohnsitz in der Schweiz. Sie zahlen deshalb eine zusätzliche Semestergebühr von 500 CHF pro Semester.' The programme page states this outright: 'Studiengebühr pro Semester CH / non CH: CHF 720 / CHF 1220'. NOTE: this surcharge is residence-based and applies to ALL incoming foreign students — there is NO extra third-country/non-EU rate at ZHdK. Tunisians pay the same as Germans.
otherFees: CHF 100 enrolment fee for the admission procedure (payable on submission, application invalid until paid). CHF 200 examination fee if invited to the second part of the aptitude assessment. CHF 35/semester ASVZ university sports contribution. CHF 32/semester student association (voluntary, opt-out possible). Medical audiogram at own cost. 'Je nach Studienbereich muss mit Auslagen für Verbrauchsmaterial gerechnet werden.'
totalCost: Tuition CHF 2,440/yr + CHF 134/yr contributions = ~CHF 2,574/yr. Zurich living costs are the real burden: budget CHF 21,000–26,000/yr (UNVERIFIED — ZHdK publishes a 'Merkblatt Studien- und Lebenskosten' not read here). Swiss student-visa authorities require proof of roughly CHF 21,000/yr in guaranteed funds. Two-year total including living: ~CHF 48,000–58,000.
scholarshipDetail: ZHdK Excellence Scholarship — verbatim and restrictive: 'Angehende Masterstudierende mit einer herausragenden Leistung bei der Aufnahmeprüfung oder auch während des Bachelors an der ZHdK werden aufgrund verschiedener Kriterien ermittelt und eingeladen, sich auf das Exzellenzstipendium zu bewerben. Eine Initiativbewerbung ohne Nomination der ZHdK ist nicht möglich.' You cannot apply — you must be nominated. ZHdK otherwise directs applicants outward: 'Stipendien sind im jeweiligen Stipendienamt des Wohnkantons bzw. im Herkunftsland zu beantragen.' Tunisia IS eligible for the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships for Foreign Scholars, but the arts strand is normally routed through separate arts-scholarship procedures — eligibility of this specific MA for a Tunisian: UNVERIFIED.
entry: Verbatim: 'Die Voraussetzungen für die Zulassung zum Studium und Immatrikulation sind der Rahmenordnung der ZHdK (RO § 19 bis 24) zu entnehmen. Zusätzliche Voraussetzungen inklusive der erforderlichen Sprachkenntnisse für die Zulassung zum gewählten Major-Studienprogramm sind der Studienordnung für den Masterstudiengang in Composition and Theory der Zürcher Hochschule der Künste (StO MA Composition and Theory § 4 ff.) zu entnehmen. In Ausnahmefällen kann die ZHdK Personen ohne Bachelorabschluss oder gleichwertigen Abschluss einer anerkannten und akkreditierten Hochschule zulassen.' StO §4(1) verbatim: 'Zum Studium wird zugelassen, wer a. die Zulassungsvoraussetzungen gemäss den Bestimmungen der übergeordneten fachhochschulspezifischen Erlasse erfüllt, b. einen positiven Entscheid des Aufnahmeverfahrens über die Zulassung zum Studium vorweist, c. nachweist, dass sie oder er über die für den jeweiligen Studiengang erforderlichen Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse verfügt.' StO §4(2): 'Die Zulassung zum Aufnahmeverfahren «sur dossier» ist ... möglich.' StO §4(3): 'Die Zahl der Studienplätze ist beschränkt. Die verfügbaren Studienplätze werden im Rahmen des Aufnahmeverfahrens aufgrund einer Bestenliste vergeben.' A medical AUDIOGRAM no older than 2 months must be submitted with the application.
acceptsNonMusic: YES IN PRINCIPLE — the regulation demands only a bachelor from a recognised, accredited higher-education institution, never a music bachelor, and §4(2) explicitly opens the aptitude procedure 'sur dossier'. But the application page attaches an explicit penalty clause, quoted verbatim: 'Zusatzprüfung bei fehlendem Bachelorabschluss in Musik — Instrumentale Praxis: Beherrschung eines Instruments auf einem Niveau, das es der/dem Kandidierenden ermöglicht, sich durch das Instrument musikalisch auszudrücken. Prüfungsinhalt: Performance auf einem Instrument von zwei verschiedenen Stücken; kurzes Partiturspiel. Gehörbildung: Darstellen und Erkennen von Intervallen, Klängen, Akkordstrukturen, Rhythmen, Harmoniefolgen. Musikalische Allgemeinbildung: Kurzanalyse von zwei stilistisch verschiedenen Stücken.' So a BSc Software Engineering is admissible on paper but triggers a supplementary instrument audition AND an ear-training exam. For this candidate that is the decisive obstacle.
portfolio: Verbatim: 'Dossier mit eigenen Aufnahmen (max. 1.95 GB): Reiche 3 verschiedenen Stücke oder Ausschnitte von insgesamt ca. 10 Minuten Länge ein (Partituren/Texte/Bilder als pdf, Audio als mp3, Video als mp4 Datei).' So: EXACTLY 3 pieces or excerpts, ~10 minutes TOTAL (not each), audio as mp3, video as mp4, scores/texts/images as pdf, whole dossier zipped, ZIP under 1.95 GB. Plus 'Gib eine Einschätzung zu diesen Aufnahmen ab (max. zwei A4-Seiten)' saved as 'Einschätzung.pdf' — a written self-assessment of your own recordings. Optional 'Links.pdf' with personal website / SoundCloud / Bandcamp / Vimeo links. Filenames must carry surname+first name and must not contain special characters or umlauts. Also required: Motivationsschreiben max. 2 A4 pages (German or English), tabular CV, passport copy, passport photo min. 320x400 px, and the audiogram. 'Der Einsatz von künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) ist erlaubt und muss bei der Einreichung der Anmeldung angegeben werden.'
audition: THREE-WAY BREAKDOWN. (1) PORTFOLIO — the 3-piece dossier above, screened first: 'A Schriftlich — Mit der Anmeldung reichen die Kandidierenden ein Motivationsschreiben sowie ein Dossier mit eigenen Aufnahmen ein. Bei positiver Beurteilung werden die Kandidat:innen zur mündlichen Eignungsprüfung eingeladen.' (2) PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST — FAVOURABLE, this is the job: a take-home assignment emailed to you ('Einreichen einer Hausaufgabe ... innerhalb der gesetzten Frist ... Umfang: Maximal zwei A4 Seiten'), then 'Tonmeisterliche Praxis (Dauer 25 Minuten). Es steht eine Vorbereitungszeit von 60 Minuten zur Verfügung. Musikübertragung — Themenfelder: Routinierte Bedienung der Infrastruktur (DAW, Peripherie); Klare Vorstellung der Abläufe bei einer Musikproduktion; Zielgerichtetes Mikrofonieren, Editieren und Mischen; Klangästhetische Vorstellung und Fähigkeit, diese umzusetzen; Grundlagen der Aufnahmeleitung. Prüfungsinhalt: Die Kandidierenden bringen eine Session auf dem eigenen System mit, die sie an der Prüfung präsentieren und mit dem Experten diskutieren.' Studiotechnik: 'Anhand der mitgebrachten Produktion werden aufnahmetechnische Fragen diskutiert ... Alternativ oder zusätzlich erhalten die Kandidierenden präparierte Audioclips mit typischen Fehlern oder Artefakten, die gemeinsam diskutiert werden.' NOTE this is a production/engineering test, NOT an audition. (3) TECHNICAL WRITTEN/ORAL EXAM — 'Technische Fächer (Dauer 25 Minuten)' covering Elektrotechnik (charge/current/voltage, network analysis, bipolar transistor and op-amp circuits, filters, microphones and loudspeakers, measurement practice, design and build a simple circuit), Digitale Audiotechnik (sampling and reconstruction, A/D and D/A, data compression, FFT, z-transform, digital filters), Akustik (room acoustics, absorption, reverberation-time measurement, ray tracing, eigenmodes), and Mathematik/Informatik (trigonometric/exponential/log/polynomial functions, Fourier transform, complex numbers, system equations, frequency response, impulse response, differentiation and integration, simple differential equations). A software-engineering BSc is an ASSET here. (4) EAR-TRAINING EXAM + INSTRUMENT AUDITION — applies to him because he has no music bachelor: 'Gehörbildung: Darstellen und Erkennen von Intervallen, Klängen, Akkordstrukturen, Rhythmen, Harmoniefolgen' and 'Performance auf einem Instrument von zwei verschiedenen Stücken; kurzes Partiturspiel'. HE CANNOT PASS THESE. This is the gate that closes ZHdK Tonmeister.
deadline: 1 March (Anmeldeschluss). PRIOR CYCLE OBSERVED (autumn 2026 entry): online application 6 January – 2 March 2026; Hausaufgabe 7–21 April 2026; Eignungsprüfung 2 May 2026; results mid-May 2026; studies begin 14 September 2026. For SEPTEMBER 2027 entry expect: applications open ~6 January 2027, close ~1 March 2027, aptitude exam ~early May 2027. ZHdK states 'Informationen zum nächsten Zulassungsverfahren werden Mitte November hier veröffentlicht' — so the 2027 cycle details publish mid-November 2026.
opens: Early January (6 January in the 2026 cycle). Information day held the preceding 20 November.
duration: 4 semesters (Regelstudienzeit); Studienumfang Major / MA = 90 / 120 credits ECTS. Autumn-semester start only.
languageReq: German B2 expected (ZHdK music admissions standard, telc or Goethe accepted); teaching principally in German with some English. Proof routes accepted verbatim: 'Muttersprache (muss nicht belegt werden); Erforderliche Sprache als Fach im Vorbildungszeugnis, bestanden oder mindestens Note 4; Anerkannte Sprachzertifikate; Hochschulabschluss (Bachelor/Master) in einem Studiengang, dessen Unterrichtsprache den in der Studienordnung geforderten Sprachkenntnissen entspricht.' HE HAS NO GERMAN — this alone is a 1.5–2 year blocker before the ear-training problem even arises.
englishTest: No specific English test score published for this major. An English-taught bachelor can be evidenced via Diploma Supplement instead of a test. UNVERIFIED whether a stand-alone English certificate is ever demanded.
study: The Swiss Tonmeister degree — the bridge between music and audio engineering. Coursework named on the faculty list: Musikübertragung Klassik and Musikübertragung Jazz & Pop (music recording/balancing), Studiotechnik, Filmton, Beschallung (live sound), Elektrotechnik, Digitale Audiotechnik und Akustik, Netzwerktechnik, Videotechnik, Partiturkunde, Gehörbildung für Tonmeister:innen, technische Gehörbildung, Berufskunde. Students realise demanding recording, sound-reinforcement, studio and film-music productions in ZHdK's own recording studios, concert halls and the Mehrspur music club. Individual profiling lets you weight the degree musically, toward production, or technically, in classical / pop / jazz. Access to the Immersive Arts Space (IAS) and the Institute for Computer Music and Sound Technology (ICST).

institution: Zürcher Hochschule der Künste (ZHdK) — Zurich University of the Arts
programme: MA Composition and Theory — Major Sound Design
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in German — language is the real gate
scholarship: Exzellenzstipendium ZHdK
qualification: Master of Arts in Music — full second-cycle Bologna degree
accreditation: Public Fachhochschule of the Canton of Zurich (ZFH); same StO 414.263.515 as the Tonmeister major.
tuition: CHF 1,220 per semester = CHF 2,440 per year for a Tunisian ('Studiengebühr pro Semester CH / non CH: CHF 720 / CHF 1220'). Same CHF 500/semester foreign-student surcharge as above; no separate third-country rate.
otherFees: CHF 100 admission-procedure enrolment fee; CHF 200 exam fee for the second stage; CHF 35/semester ASVZ sports; CHF 32/semester student association (voluntary); audiogram; consumables.

scholarshipDetail: Nomination-only, as above: 'Eine Initiativbewerbung ohne Nomination der ZHdK ist nicht möglich.' ZHdK otherwise refers applicants to their canton or home-country scholarship office.
entry: Identical regulatory basis, verbatim: 'Die Voraussetzungen für die Zulassung zum Studium und Immatrikulation sind der Rahmenordnung der ZHdK (RO § 19 bis 24) zu entnehmen. Zusätzliche Voraussetzungen inklusive der erforderlichen Sprachkenntnisse ... sind der Studienordnung für den Masterstudiengang in Composition and Theory (StO MA Composition and Theory § 4 ff.) zu entnehmen. In Ausnahmefällen kann die ZHdK Personen ohne Bachelorabschluss oder gleichwertigen Abschluss einer anerkannten und akkreditierten Hochschule zulassen.' A medical audiogram no older than 2 months is required. '→ Nach Auswertung der eingereichten Unterlagen entscheidet die Jury über die Zulassung zur Eignungsprüfung.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES, with an added submission. Quoted verbatim from the required-documents list: 'Kandidat:innen ohne Bachelor in Musik: Video künstlerisch-musikalische Performance — Reiche ein Video mit eigenen Aufnahmen ein (insgesamt max. 15 Min. / 1.95 GB / Format .mov oder .mp4). Alle Dateien sind mit Nachname_Vorname_Komponist_Werk zu bezeichnen.' The naming convention (Komponist_Werk) shows they expect performances of repertoire. Milder than the Tonmeister supplementary exam — it is a recorded video rather than a live instrument audition — but he still has to play something musical on camera.
portfolio: Verbatim: 'Dossier mit 3–4 eigenen Arbeiten (max. 1.95 GB): Reiche Werke/Werkausschnitte von insgesamt ca. 10 Minuten Länge ein (Partituren/Texte/Bilder als pdf, Audio als mp3, Video als mp4 Datei).' So 3 TO 4 works, ~10 minutes TOTAL. Each must be commented: 'Kommentiere jede dieser Arbeiten (Konzept, Bedeutung, Entstehungsprozess etc.). Fasse diese Kommentare (max. zwei A4-Seiten) in einer einzigen pdf-Datei zusammen. Benenne diese Datei «Kommentare.pdf».' PLUS a separate application video: 'Bewerbungsvideo (max. 3–5 Minuten / max. 1 GB / Format mp4), in dem du dich in deiner eigenen kreativen Arbeitsumgebung präsentierst.' Optional 'Links.pdf'. Plus the non-music-bachelor performance video (max 15 min). Recording quality spec given for video items: 'HD Video (720p; 1080i; 1080p) mit 265 kbit/s Klangauflösung, Format mov oder mp4. Max 1.95 GB'; 'Verwendung eines Stereo-Mikrofons ist erwünscht.' All zipped into one ZIP under 1.95 GB.
audition: MIXED — one favourable gate and one fatal one. PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST (FAVOURABLE — this is the job, not a barrier), verbatim: 'Praktische Prüfung — Sound Design-Aufgabe (90 Minuten Vorbereitungszeit, 20 Minuten Präsentation und Diskussion)' and 'Mündliche Prüfung Analyse einer kurzen Filmszene, eines Game-Levels, einer Klangszene etc. (60 Minuten Vorbereitungszeit, 10 Minuten Präsentation und Diskussion)' plus 'Mündliche Präsentation / Kolloquium anhand einer der eingereichten Arbeiten (10 Minuten)'. You are handed material and asked to make something — exactly the format that suits a self-taught producer. EAR-TRAINING EXAM (HE CANNOT PASS), verbatim: 'Musikalische Eignungsprüfung — Mündliche Theorieaufgaben (Gedächtnisübung; Darstellen von Rhythmen und Melodien; Intervalle und Akkorde erkennen, benennen und schreiben können; harmonische Aufgabe; Kurzimprovisation), Dauer 30 Minuten.' Recognising, naming and WRITING intervals and chords by ear, plus a short improvisation, is conservatoire aural skill. Combined with the non-music-bachelor performance video, ZHdK Sound Design is also effectively closed to him.
deadline: 1 March. PRIOR CYCLE OBSERVED (autumn 2026): online application 6 January – 2 March 2026; notification of admission to the aptitude exam early April 2026; Eignungsprüfung 13–14 April 2026; results mid-May 2026; start 14 September 2026. For SEPTEMBER 2027 expect the same rhythm, published mid-November 2026.
opens: Early January (6 January in the 2026 cycle).
duration: 4 semesters; Major / MA = 90 / 120 ECTS. Autumn start only.
languageReq: German B2 expected; teaching mainly German. Same proof routes as the Tonmeister major. He has no German.
study: Verbatim programme description: 'Die Arbeit im sich rasch entwickelnden Umfeld von Sound für Film, Podcast, Theater, Computerspiele, interaktiven Medien und Produkten bedingt neben einem breiten Wissen und technischen Fertigkeiten auch hohe künstlerisch-gestalterische Kompetenzen. Dies umfasst sowohl die Klangerzeugung und -manipulation wie auch die lineare und interaktive Tondramaturgie.' FIT WARNING: this is Audiodesign for film, games, podcast, theatre and interactive media — sound-to-picture and interactive audio dramaturgy. It is NOT record-making. Recent student theses are on game reverb simulation, VR language-model sound, and Max/MSP controllers. Listed here because Audiodesign is in-field, but it does not train you to produce, mix and master records — the Tonmeister major does that.

institution: The University of Edinburgh — Edinburgh College of Art (Reid School of Music)
programme: MSc Sound Design
whyChance: Engineering/computing may be accepted, but the wording hedges — ask first
verdictWhy: The portfolio brief is generous — three pieces, and written essays on sound count — but everything else works against him. His degree subject is not on the accepted list, the professional-experience fallback needs experience he does not have, the fee is around GBP 29,900, and no international scholarship is named while Chevening is closed to him. It is also sound design for screen rather than record production.
correction: TWO corrections, the first severe. (1) COST BAND BADLY WRONG: recorded as 'Under EUR 1.5k/yr'. The overseas rate is approximately GBP 29,900 per year — around twenty times the recorded band, and among the three most expensive entries in the batch. Any shortlist built on that figure would be dangerously misleading. (2) The record does not note the two-round deadline structure (Round 1 mid-December, Round 2 early May) or the IELTS two-year validity rule, both of which affect his timing.
qualification: MSc
tuition: UNVERIFIED — the programme page routes fees to a separate 2026-27 fee breakdown page and did not display the international figure. Edinburgh MSc international PGT fees are typically in the low-to-mid £30k band for ECA programmes; budget accordingly and confirm.
scholarshipDetail: "Edinburgh College of Art scholarships" are referenced on the programme page, with further awards searchable on the university funding portal. Names, values and eligibility for a Tunisian applicant are UNVERIFIED.
entry: "A UK 2:1 honours degree, or its international equivalent, in a relevant subject such as music, sound design, media arts, sound engineering, acoustics, film, animation, and art and design subjects." Explicit alternative route: applicants who do not meet the academic entry requirements "may be considered with relevant professional experience." English: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 minimum per component; or TOEFL iBT 92 with 20 per component (pre-21 January 2026 sittings) / the revised 4.5 with 4.0 per component scale thereafter. Tests must be no more than two years old at programme start.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY / CHECK — the listed 'relevant subjects' are all arts, media and acoustics disciplines; software engineering is not among them (note 'acoustics' and 'animation' are, which shows the list is technical as well as artistic). The usable route is the stated fallback: applicants who do not meet the academic requirements "may be considered with relevant professional experience," plus the portfolio. Because game audio and creative coding are core to the syllabus, a software-engineering background is substantively relevant even though it is not on the named list — worth arguing explicitly in the application.
portfolio: "At least THREE pieces of work", submitted as a PDF with explanations of the projects and links to work hosted on a reliable online space. Content may include "sound design examples covering films, games and animations, an essay on sound or sound recordings and other documentation of sound-based projects." Include "a short explanation of your role in collaborative projects." Files over 4 MB must go to an external sharing site with a link provided.
audition: None. Portfolio-based selection with no audition or on-site test.
deadline: 2026 entry ran in rounds: Round 1 closed 15 December 2025 (decisions by 19 March 2026); Round 2 closed 4 May 2026 (decisions by 30 June 2026) — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. Edinburgh states that entry requirements for 2027-28 "will be published on 1 Oct 2026", so the 2027 rounds become authoritative from that date. Expect a Round 1 in December 2026.

In begründeten Fällen können auch hervorragende berufliche Leistungen als Qualifikation ganz oder teilweise anerkannt werden.' The Immatrikulationssatzung annex is stricter, verbatim: 'Das Aufbaustudium mit dem Studienziel Master (M.A.) im Fach Musikinformatik setzt den erfolgreichen Abschluss des grundständigen Studiengangs Musikwissenschaft/Musikinformatik B.A. an der HfM Karlsruhe oder eines entsprechenden Studiengangs an einer anderen Hochschule voraus, wobei die HAUPTFACHNOTE 2,5 ODER BESSER sein muss.' And then the crucial escape clause, verbatim: 'Absolventen eines Bachelor-Studiengangs anderer Hochschulen, die das Aufbaustudium Musikinformatik M.A. belegen wollen, aber KEINEN entsprechenden Bachelor-Abschluss im Fach Musikinformatik oder Musikwissenschaft/Musikinformatik haben, müssen entsprechende gleichwertige Kenntnisse nachweisen und in einer ERWEITERTEN AUFNAHMEPRÜFUNG bestätigen.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES, VIA TWO EXPLICIT ROUTES. First, SPO §4(1) requires only 'ein fachlich affiner erster Hochschulabschluss' — a SUBJECT-AFFINE first degree, not a music degree; a computing degree is plainly affine to Musikinformatik. Second, and unusually, 'In begründeten Fällen können auch hervorragende berufliche Leistungen als Qualifikation ganz oder teilweise anerkannt werden' — outstanding professional achievement can substitute wholly or partly for the degree. Third, the annex provides for entrants without the nominal bachelor: they 'müssen entsprechende gleichwertige Kenntnisse nachweisen und in einer erweiterten Aufnahmeprüfung bestätigen'. The trade-off is an EXTENDED entrance exam, whose extra parts the commission sets case by case: 'Sofern Abweichungen von den Zulassungsvoraussetzungen vorliegen und der Bewerber einen Antrag auf Ausnahmeregelung gestellt hat, kann die Kommission zusätzliche Prüfungsteile festlegen. Diese müssen dem Bewerber mindestens 3 Wochen vor dem Prüfungstermin schriftlich mitgeteilt werden.' You get three weeks' written notice of whatever extra is demanded — so the risk is knowable, not blind.
portfolio: REMARKABLY BROAD, AND SOFTWARE COUNTS. SPO §4(3) verbatim: '1. ein Motivationsschreiben, in dem auf maximal zwei Seiten die persönlichen Erwartungen an das Studium und die Gründe für die beabsichtigte Aufnahme des Studiums dargelegt werden sollen; 2. MINDESTENS ZWEI ARBEITSPROBEN IN DER FORM VON TEXTEN, AUDIO- ODER VIDEODATEIEN, SOFTWARE O.Ä.; DIES KANN AUCH PER LINK ERFOLGEN; 3. Nachweis über Kenntnis und sichere Beherrschung der deutschen Sprache.' So: AT LEAST TWO work samples, and they may be texts, audio files, video files OR SOFTWARE — submittable by link. No track count, no duration, no audio format prescribed. A candidate with no music portfolio but a GitHub history and two audio experiments can satisfy this literally. The motivation letter is capped at two pages.
audition: NO AUDITION, NO EAR-TRAINING EXAM, NO PRODUCTION TEST — a single interview. Verbatim, SPO §4(2): 'Die Aufnahmeprüfung besteht im Regelfall aus einem ca. 20-minütigen Eignungsgespräch, bei dem fachspezifische Vorkenntnisse, Sprachgewandtheit in der deutschen Sprache sowie die Studienmotivation überprüft werden. Für die Aufnahmeprüfung bildet der Prüfungsausschuss des Instituts eine Prüfungskommission.' The Immatrikulationssatzung annex gives the duration as 'ein Eignungsgespräch von ca. 25 Minuten Dauer' for Musikinformatik. Nothing is played, nothing is sung, no intervals are identified. THE ONLY CAVEAT is the 'erweiterte Aufnahmeprüfung' for entrants without the nominal bachelor — its content is set by the commission and is UNVERIFIED, but it is notified in writing three weeks in advance. Note the interview itself is a German-language test.
deadline: 15 JUNE annually for the entrance examination (application deadline). Winter-semester start only. This is a LATE deadline by German standards and gives him far more runway than the February–March Swiss dates.
opens: UNVERIFIED — deadline is fixed at 15 June.
duration: 4 semesters. Winter-semester start; SPO §4(4): 'Der Studienbeginn erfolgt zum Wintersemester. In begründeten Ausnahmefällen kann eine Aufnahme zum Sommersemester erfolgen.' ECTS not read from the SPO — UNVERIFIED (a German M.A. of this length is normally 120 ECTS).
languageReq: German, level per the Immatrikulationssatzung — exact CEFR for this programme UNVERIFIED, working assumption B2 / TestDaF TDN3 based on the school's published levels for its other degrees. Fluency is separately assessed live in the entrance interview.
englishTest: None required — UNVERIFIED whether English is assessed at all.
study: Music informatics at IMWI — the computational side of music. SPO §3: 'Einziges Hauptfach dieses Studiengangs ist das Fach Musikinformatik'; specialisations are possible 'in der durch die Modulhandbücher festgelegten Form'. FIT CAVEAT, AND IT IS A REAL ONE: IMWI Karlsruhe is oriented to computer music, algorithmic composition, music software and musicology rather than to recording, mixing and mastering. It sits close to the 'sonology' territory this search excludes. Recorded here because the ADMISSION GATE is exceptionally favourable to a software engineer, not because it will teach him to make records. The detailed module handbook was not read — the exact production content is UNVERIFIED.

institution: Dutch Dance Music Academy (DDMA)
programme: Music Producer Jaaropleiding ADVANCED (Standard and Premium packages); plus separate 1-on-1 Producer packages (Privé Le…
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Dutch — language is the real gate

accreditation: NOT NVAO-ACCREDITED. VERIFIED this session: NO CRKBO and NO NRTO registration is mentioned anywhere on the pages read — and that absence is genuinely notable, because every comparable Dutch private audio school (Sound Education, Master The Mix, Pro Audio Education) advertises CRKBO prominently. It also means the VAT position is unclear: without CRKBO the tuition may be VAT-liable, so ask explicitly whether the quoted prices are inclusive or exclusive of 21% BTW. The institution is private and 'niet-bekostigd'. The certificate has NO legal or academic standing anywhere.
tuition: Jaaropleiding Advanced is one year, so the tier price is the total: STANDARD €4,097 (lessons and masterclasses, personal coaching, online feedback sessions and Q&As); PREMIUM €5,097 (adds private coaching and studio sessions). ADDITIONAL private studio sessions are €194 per 2-hour session on top. The 1-on-1 packages are one-off purchases at €1,997 / €2,997 / €5,997.
otherFees: VERIFIED: extra private studio sessions €194 per 2-hour block. No registration, application, materials or exam fee published — UNVERIFIED. VAT STATUS UNVERIFIED and this matters: with no CRKBO registration found, 21% BTW may be chargeable, which on €4,097 would be roughly €860 extra. Get the quote in writing marked inclusive or exclusive of BTW.
totalCost: €4,097 (Standard) to €5,097 (Premium) for the year, PLUS possible 21% BTW (unconfirmed, potentially ~€860-€1,070 more), plus €194 per extra 2-hour studio session, plus his own production setup, plus Nijmegen living costs of roughly €10,000-€13,000 if relocation were even possible. Realistic ceiling well above €18,000 for a certificate with no standing — and he cannot get a visa for it anyway.
scholarshipDetail: NONE available to him. The only subsidy promoted is WERKTUIG PPO (up to €2,000) — this is a Dutch fund for SELF-EMPLOYED CREATIVE PROFESSIONALS ALREADY WORKING IN THE NETHERLANDS. A non-EU newcomer with no Dutch business registration cannot claim it; treat its value as ZERO for him. No DUO eligibility (private provider). Up to 50% partner discounts on hardware/software are the only real benefit.
entry: CORRECTED — NOT open access for the Advanced track. VERIFIED: applicants must complete an INTAKE INTERVIEW AND AN AUDITION. The only exemption is prior completion of DDMA's own standard Music Producer Jaaropleiding or its 1-on-1 training. Capacity is capped at 15 places per year (10 shown as remaining for the current cycle). The entry-level Basis/Pro/VIP private packages appear to be open access.
acceptsNonMusic: YES by implication for the entry-level packages — no degree or prior qualification of any kind is published as a requirement, and the academy is aimed at hobbyists moving toward professional production. For the ADVANCED jaaropleiding, admission turns on the audition and intake interview, not on any academic background — so his BSc is neither a help nor a hindrance. No explicit published wording on non-music degrees exists, so this is inference rather than a quote. Instruction is in Dutch regardless.

audition: CORRECTED FROM 'none published'. Format, repertoire and submission method are UNVERIFIED — confirm directly.
deadline: No published deadline; admission is by intake interview and audition until the 15 places fill. UNVERIFIED — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.

duration: One academic year, part-time, running 1 September to 31 August. No ECTS. CONTACT-HOURS WARNING, verified: the Advanced programme runs roughly ONE MASTERCLASS PER MONTH with Q&A/feedback sessions QUARTERLY — that is light contact for the money, and he should count the actual hours before comparing prices with anything else.
englishTest: IRRELEVANT — IELTS is not accepted or used; instruction is in Dutch.
study: Electronic dance music production, mixing, mastering, sound design, live performance and songwriting. Delivery is monthly masterclasses plus quarterly Q&A and online feedback sessions, with personal coaching; the Premium tier adds private coaching and studio sessions. The separate 1-on-1 packages cover DAW use, production workflow, samples, dynamics, music theory, sound design, mixing, advanced synthesis, mastering, template workflows and sidechaining, with the VIP package adding an Ableton Live Bootcamp.
recommendation: NOT VIABLE — DO NOT APPLY. Three blockers, each fatal on its own: instruction is entirely in DUTCH; the award is a private certificate with no accreditation, no ECTS and no recognition; and it CANNOT support a residence permit, so he could not lawfully relocate for it. It also lacks the CRKBO and NRTO marks its Dutch competitors hold, and its VAT position is unclear as a result. Genre-wise this is the best match in the Netherlands for a would-be dance producer, which makes it the most frustrating entry in the slice — but frustration is not a reason to spend €4,000-€5,000 plus possible VAT on something that cannot get him into the country or onto a recognised qualification. Included so the Dutch dance-education landscape is fully mapped.

institution: Sound Education Nederland
programme: Beroepsopleiding Geluidstechniek / Music Producer (1 year, part-time) — FLEX, CLASSIC PRAKTIJK and ELITE PRAKTIJK tiers
whyChance: Names engineering or computing as a welcome background, but taught in Dutch — language is the real gate
qualification: The school's OWN diploma. NOT a master, NOT a degree, NOT NVAO-accredited, no ECTS. Classified as 'kort beroepsonderwijs' (short vocational education).
accreditation: NOT NVAO-ACCREDITED. VERIFIED: registered in the CRKBO register for kort beroepsonderwijs (which is why no VAT is charged) and holds the NRTO keurmerk. CRITICAL DISTINCTION — neither is a higher-education accreditation: CRKBO is a tax/quality register for short vocational training providers, and NRTO is the quality mark of the Dutch TRADE ASSOCIATION for private training companies. Only NVAO accredits Dutch degrees, and this programme is not in that system. The institution is private and 'niet-bekostigd' (not government-funded). The diploma carries NO legal status as a Dutch qualification and no ECTS transferable anywhere.
tuition: As above; the programme is one year so the tier price is the total. FLEX €2,695 — full one-year curriculum, masterclass video library (4 years of content), coaching, career guidance, assessments, diploma; classes followed from home; studio practice NOT included. CLASSIC PRAKTIJK €5,975 — all-inclusive: complete curriculum, ALL practical lessons, homework guidance, assessments, field trips, exam retakes. ELITE PRAKTIJK €14,475 — Classic plus private one-to-one mentoring from a chosen producer/sound engineer, with no obligation if the preferred mentor cannot be booked.
otherFees: NO VAT (CRKBO-registered) — verified. THE HIDDEN COST: on FLEX, private studio practice is charged separately at approximately €40/hour, which can escalate quickly since the tier includes essentially no studio time. A Music Business Course (contracts, promotion, playlist placement, sync deals, admin) is INCLUDED FREE. No application or registration fee published — UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: €2,695 on FLEX plus ~€40/hr for any studio time actually used, up to €14,475 on ELITE. CLASSIC PRAKTIJK at €5,975 all-in is the sensible tier and is honest value for the content — IF you speak Dutch and are already in the Netherlands legally.
scholarshipDetail: NONE published. No non-EU or Tunisian-specific award. NOT eligible for DUO student finance (private provider). The 35-50% student software discounts are the only quantifiable benefit.

The school publishes a 'Vooropleiding?' page and a 'Toelating MBO of HBO muziek' page, indicating it also functions as a preparation route into Dutch MBO/HBO music programmes. Exact requirements UNVERIFIED. Dutch language required de facto.
acceptsNonMusic: Presumed YES — this is an open-access private provider and no prior music qualification is stated anywhere as a condition. No explicit wording on non-music bachelors is published, so this is inference, not a quote. Irrelevant in practice given the language barrier.
portfolio: None published — no portfolio requirement found. UNVERIFIED.

opens: Rolling enrolment. UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.

englishTest: IRRELEVANT — IELTS is NOT accepted or used, because instruction is in Dutch. Dutch proficiency would be the operative requirement.
study: Microphone technique, recording technique, music theory, mixing and mastering, production, live-sound engineering, and sound for games and film. Genuinely broad and relevant content for his interests.
recommendation: NOT VIABLE FOR HIM — DO NOT APPLY. Three independent blockers, any one of which is fatal: (1) instruction is entirely in DUTCH and he does not speak it; (2) the award is a private diploma with no NVAO accreditation, no ECTS and no legal standing — CRKBO and NRTO are a tax register and a trade-association badge, not accreditation; (3) it is part-time and partly online, so it CANNOT support a student residence permit and he could not lawfully move to the Netherlands for it. To be fair to the school: this is one of the better-run private audio academies in the Netherlands, its pricing is transparent, its instalment and cooling-off terms are genuinely fair, and CLASSIC at €5,975 all-in is decent value — for a Dutch-speaking resident. None of that reaches him. Reported for completeness of the Dutch private-market picture.

deadline: CORRECTION TO PRIOR DATA — a window IS published: applications run March to September for the October start, i.e. the effective deadline is SEPTEMBER of the start year. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for the 2027 cohort. Places are capped at 18 and allocated by enrolment order, so the practical deadline is when the cohort fills, not September.
opens: CORRECTION TO PRIOR DATA — ETIC DOES publish an application window: 'Março a Setembro' (MARCH to SEPTEMBER) for an October start. For his SEPTEMBER 2027 target the equivalent window would be roughly March–September 2027, but that specific cycle is not yet published: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
duration: CONFIRMED 170 hours over ONE SEMESTER. No ECTS ('ECTS not mentioned in course documentation' — the concept does not apply to OFP training). Classes Monday/Wednesday/Friday 19:00–23:00. Maximum 18 students per cohort (confirmed).
englishTest: NONE — no English test of any kind, IELTS is irrelevant here. CONFIRMED instruction is in Portuguese, so PORTUGUESE is the real and unavoidable language requirement. Note ETIC publishes no Portuguese proficiency test either, but a candidate who does not speak Portuguese cannot follow 170 hours of technical instruction. This is the binding constraint, not IELTS.
study: CONFIRMED five modules: Introduction to Sound (audio fundamentals, physics, perception); DAW Avid Pro Tools; Audio Cable Maintenance (identification, soldering, troubleshooting); Capture, Recording & Mixing (studio technique, microphone placement); Live Sound 1 (PA systems, consoles, event management). Project-based, in Portuguese.
recommendation: NOT A MASTER'S — DO NOT CONFUSE THIS WITH ONE, AND IT CANNOT GET HIM A RESIDENCE VISA. The course fee is honest and fully published, the kit is excellent for €2,125, and it is pitched exactly at his current level: no audio background needed, online interview possible, 12th-grade minimum against his BSc. Its real use to him is PORTFOLIO FUEL, not a destination — the thing he is missing for any accredited programme is demonstrable sound work, and 170 hours of hands-on Pro Tools, microphone technique and mixing would produce it. Three things kill it as a plan: (1) it confers no degree and no ECTS, so it advances neither his academic position nor a later master's application; (2) at best it supports a temporary E9 stay visa, not a residence permit, and ETIC publishes nothing about sponsoring even that; (3) it is taught entirely in PORTUGUESE, which he does not speak — this alone is disqualifying today and is a bigger barrier than the money. Add €5,000+ of Lisbon living costs and the arithmetic fails for a budget-sensitive candidate. Verdict: skip unless he is already in Portugal for another reason and speaks Portuguese.

But it is worth knowing about for one specific and strategic reason: his portfolio is his single biggest gap, and every serious programme in this search — ENTI's director interview, and any competitive music master — will judge him on work he has not yet made. €3,225 for 9 months of small-group (max 12) Ableton production training at a Pioneer DJ- and Ableton-partnered school is a rational, low-risk way to build that portfolio, and it is far better value than paying five figures for a título propio 'máster' that carries no official standing. As a portfolio-building step ahead of a real master's application in a later cycle, the Curso de Producción Musical is the smartest cheap option in this slice.

qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — specifically a 'Máster de Formación Permanente', 60 ECTS. VERIFIED on both the official programme page and the official UCAM brochure PDF. This is UCAM's OWN diploma. It is NOT an official Máster Universitario, does not appear in the RUCT catalogue of official degrees, and does not give direct access to a Spanish doctorate.

The INSTITUTION is legitimate — UCAM is a recognised Spanish private university listed in RUCT and legally entitled to issue títulos propios under art. 7 of Ley Orgánica 2/2023. But THIS AWARD is not ANECA-verified and is legally a university certificate, not an official master's degree. In practice: credible and university-branded with genuine industry weight, but it will not be treated as a master's degree by a foreign ministry, a public-sector employer or a doctoral programme.
tuition: EUR 3,900 total tuition for the whole 60-ECTS programme. VERIFIED for the currently advertised edition. Confirm for the 2027/2028 edition.
otherFees: VERIFIED and complete as published: pre-enrolment fee EUR 235 (non-refundable) and school insurance EUR 59.12 (non-refundable). No application fee, materials fee or exam fee is published. The Cubase licence is included in the materials, not charged separately.
totalCost: EUR 4,194.12 in institutional costs (3,900 + 235 + 59.12) — VERIFIED exactly. This is by far the cheapest credible university-branded music-production master in this slice: roughly one third of the UFV three-month certificate, one third of the La Salle official master, and about one fifteenth of Berklee's all-in cost. Add Murcia living costs (cheap by Spanish standards, roughly EUR 700–900 per month) and the visa proof-of-funds requirement (IPREM, approximately EUR 600 per month in 2026) — but note that the living-cost calculation only matters if the visa question resolves favourably, which on current evidence it may not.
scholarshipDetail: No scholarship specifically identified for non-EU applicants on the programme page or brochure — UNVERIFIED, and likely none for this título propio. UCAM's general postgraduate financing is described as payment plans and financing through partner banking entities, which realistically requires a Spanish bank relationship he will not have before arrival. Assume he self-pays the full EUR 4,194.12. At that price this is far less damaging than it would be elsewhere.
entry: VERIFIED from the official brochure: open to any holder of an official university degree or equivalent non-university higher education at Grado or official Máster level, national or foreign, 'sin necesidad de homologación de sus títulos' — no homologation required, subject to UCAM verifying that the qualification is equivalent to a Spanish official degree and grants access to postgraduate study in the issuing country. This no-homologation provision is a genuine practical advantage for a Tunisian degree holder. 12 places only. Campus de los Jerónimos, Murcia.
acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly and by name. VERIFIED wording from the official brochure: the programme 'de forma especial se dirige a egresados en áreas de Comunicación Audiovisual, Periodismo, Musicología, Magisterio Musical, INGENIERÍAS EN TELECOMUNICACIONES E INFORMÁTICA, así como a titulados del Conservatorio Profesional.' A BSc in Software Engineering maps directly onto 'Ingenierías en... Informática'. This is one of only two programmes in the slice where his exact degree family is named as a welcome entry profile, and the only music-production programme where that is true.
portfolio: No portfolio requirement is published anywhere on the programme page or in the official brochure — UNVERIFIED but apparently none. Admission runs through the UCAM postgraduate admissions portal. For a candidate with an unfinished portfolio this is a meaningful advantage.
audition: None published — UNVERIFIED but apparently none.
deadline: No published deadline — places are capped at 12, so admission is effectively first-come, first-served. UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle. With only 12 places, early application is essential.
opens: Rolling, through the UCAM admissions portal at www.ucam.edu/admision. Exact 2027 opening UNVERIFIED.
duration: 60 ECTS over one academic year, structured in three cuatrimestres: September–December, January–April, May–July. Class timetable, verified: Fridays 16:30–20:30 and Saturdays 09:30–13:30 plus 15:30–19:30 — 12 contact hours per week, weekends only.
englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is taught in Spanish, so no IELTS is required. This removes the English-test obstacle entirely but replaces it with a Spanish-language one. Required Spanish level is not published — UNVERIFIED.
study: VERIFIED module structure and credit weights from the official brochure: I. Herramientas de trabajo para la producción musical (13.2 ECTS); II. Fundamentos de la Producción Musical (11.2 ECTS); III. Producción Musical Profesional (9.6 ECTS); IV. Trabajo Final de Máster (16 ECTS); V. Prácticas en empresa (10 ECTS). Total 60 ECTS. Note the shape: only 34 ECTS is taught content — 26 ECTS, well over a third, is final project plus work placement. Stated career outcomes: productor musical, técnico especialista en mezcla, técnico de mastering, técnico asistente en estudio de grabación. Graduates receive official Steinberg Cubase professional certification, and a Cubase licence is included in the materials.
recommendation: On paper the best value in this slice by an enormous margin — EUR 4,194.12 all-in, verified to the cent, for a 60-ECTS university-branded music production master with Sony Music España involvement, named Spanish electronic producers teaching, an included Cubase licence and Steinberg certification. His software-engineering degree is named explicitly as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, no IELTS is needed, foreign degrees are accepted without homologation, and it starts in September, matching his target. If he were already living legally in Spain, this would be the clear recommendation. But he is not, and that is where it breaks. THREE ISSUES, in order of severity. (1) THE VISA. I verified Spain's actual rules rather than assuming: títulos propios ARE admissible for a student authorisation, which is better than feared — but the binding constraint is the teaching load, and UCAM's own brochure publishes a weekend-only timetable of 12 contact hours per week in a semipresencial format. The requirement is 20 hours per week, or at minimum 12 hours that are genuinely in person for concentrated programmes, plus at least 50% in-person delivery overall. This programme sits at or below that floor. On the published evidence it likely does NOT support a student residence permit. (2) LANGUAGE. It is taught entirely in Spanish, including a 16-ECTS final project. (3) THE AWARD is a certificate, not a degree — acceptable for industry, worthless for a future PhD or any title-dependent role. VERDICT: outstanding return on euro, but probably not a relocation route. ACTION: before anything else, email UCAM's international office and ask three specific questions in writing — what percentage of the programme is delivered in person, how many presencial hours per week, and has UCAM successfully supported non-EU students onto a student visa for THIS programme. If the answers are weak, this option is worth nothing to him as a route to Europe, however cheap it is.

audition: PRACTICAL/TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT PLUS COLLOQUIUM — NOT a performance audition and NOT an ear-training test. The entrance exam evaluates: "Sound quality reflective of AES/EBU standards, Originality, Technique, Musicality, Knowledge of musical styles, Creative personality, General knowledge of music and culture", and the candidate must "converse on a variety of topics reflecting professional competence and knowledge of culture and society (colloquium)". VIDEO/REMOTE POSSIBLE: EAMT permits entrance by video recording, but only "if the examination panel has no doubts about authenticity of the recording, the quality of the recording is sufficient for evaluation and the candidate’s performance meets the highest standards, clearly exceeding the admission threshold." entry: Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (or equivalent) obtained in Italy or abroad + minimum 15 years of schooling. duration: 2 years. Credits: 120 CFA is the standard AFAM II-livello load; the page does not state the credit figure explicitly — UNVERIFIED on-page. Lessons fortnightly, concentrated in two consecutive days (compatible with part-time work).

study: Sound Design (recording, construction and manipulation of sound effects for film/TV/games, Pro Tools workflow); Audio Interattivo non Lineare with Audiokinetic Wwise (implementation, events, spatialisation, non-linear mixing, game-engine integration); Campionamento audio e post produzione (custom sample-library building, mapping, modulators, envelopes); Tecnologie e tecniche del Restauro Audio (digitisation, remastering, forensic audio); Tecniche di ripresa e registrazione; Storia del Sound Design. Original projects developed jointly with Saint Louis's Composizione and Musica Applicata departments and in collaboration with RUFA and Vigamus (Rome video-game museum).
recommendation: STRONGEST ITALIAN OPTION IN SCOPE, but not for a September 2027 start without a year of preparation. This is the only Italian private route that gives him a genuinely OFFICIAL degree (MUR Diploma Accademico di II livello) in exactly his craft (sound design, Wwise, Pro Tools) at a price a self-payer can survive — about €8.3k a year against NABA's €22k. His software-engineering degree formally qualifies him, and the Live Electronics/Wwise/SuperCollider content plays directly to his coding background. The two real obstacles are (1) a portfolio-based audition he cannot currently pass, and (2) teaching partly in Italian. Realistic plan: build a serious sound-design portfolio during 2026, apply by 30 April 2027 for the Very Early Bird rate, and be prepared for Saint Louis to route him into a pre-academic year (which, usefully, is itself visa-valid as a Foundation Course).

Beyond that, the 25-ECTS volume is below the 60-ECTS statutory floor for a Máster de Formación Permanente under RD 822/2021 — so calling it a 'Máster' is not merely marketing gloss over a título propio, it is inconsistent with the Spanish regulation governing that exact award name. Second, the good news I can give him is a correction — his non-EU administrative fee is €677.60, not the €1,440 previously assumed, because that higher tier applies only to official degrees. Note the contrast with UCAM, which names computer engineering graduates as a welcome profile, and with La Salle, which requires no music background at all.
portfolio: Not published — UNVERIFIED.

deadline: No fixed deadline — rolling until places fill. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the published cycle is the September 2026 edition; 2027 dates are not yet available.

englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is taught in Spanish. No IELTS required.
study: Module 1 — audio fundamentals, music theory, songwriting, Pro Tools training (41 hours). Module 2 — pre-production techniques and workflow (22 hours). Module 3 — production processes and creative direction (32 hours). Module 4 — post-production, mixing, mastering and industry contracts (57 hours). Roughly 152 contact hours in total. Taught inside a working production facility.
recommendation: AVOID for his purposes, and the reason is now legal rather than a judgement call. This is not a master — it is a 30-ECTS certificate delivered over three months of two-hour evening classes, and at 10 contact hours per week it falls below BOTH thresholds in Spain's student-authorisation criteria (20 hours per week generally, or at minimum 12 in-person hours for concentrated programmes). It therefore cannot support a student residence permit, which makes it useless as a September 2027 relocation plan regardless of its merits. Compounding that: its published entry profile expects prior music or sound training that he does not have; it is taught entirely in Spanish; it costs more per credit than La Salle's official Máster Universitario; and UFV's own page contradicts itself on the price by EUR 400. On the positive side it is a genuinely good short skills course — real facilities, Warner Music Spain professionals, and two portable certifications (Avid PT101/PT110 and a perpetual Ableton Live 12 Suite licence) that he would otherwise pay for separately. The only scenario where it makes sense is as a paid upskilling course taken once he is already legally resident in Madrid on some other basis. Do not build a relocation plan around it, and if he does ever enrol, get the correct total price in writing first.

institution: Scuola Mohole
programme: Produzione Musicale e Sound Design — Bachelor of Arts (3 years) / Corso Annuale (1 year). NOT A MASTER
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Italian — language is the real gate
qualification: NOT A MASTER, AND NOT AN ITALIAN RECOGNISED DEGREE. The awarding/accrediting body is now IDENTIFIED (it was not in the prior entry): EABHES — the European Accreditation Board of Higher Education Schools. Mohole advertises a "Laurea Europea Bachelor of Arts — riconosciuto in UE, UK e USA", EQF Level 6, 180 ECTS. It also issues an Attestato di competenza professionale from Regione Lombardia and RSL (Rockschool London) certifications. It is NOT a MUR/AFAM Diploma Accademico and Mohole is NOT in the AFAM system. The one-year option (60 ECTS) is simply year one of the same undergraduate course — not a postgraduate qualification of any kind.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL in the Italian system — and the accreditation claim is now RESOLVED rather than merely doubted. Accrediting body: EABHES, verified on eabhes.eu as "one of the largest PRIVATE networks of internationally recognised professional and academic institutions", ~60 member schools, ~300 accredited programmes, self-described as aligned to ECTS and the Bologna Process. EABHES is a PRIVATE ASSOCIATION, not a state or national accreditation agency, and its own site does not claim its awards are state-recognised degrees. What this means in practice: the "Bachelor of Arts / Laurea Europea" carries NO valore legale in Italy — it is not a titolo di studio recognised by MUR, cannot be used for Italian public competitions, and is not automatically recognised by any EU, UK or US authority despite the marketing wording "riconosciuto in UE, UK e USA". Recognition would fall to each receiving institution or employer case by case. The only credentials here with a defined Italian legal identity are the regional Attestato (Regione Lombardia) and the RSL music certifications. So: the prior entry's red flag was correct on substance — the marketing overstates what a private-network accreditation delivers — but the awarding body IS named, just not the kind of body the wording implies.
tuition: Approx. €25,500 for the three-year Bachelor of Arts at €8,500/year, BEFORE the undisclosed multi-year discount. €8,500 for the one-year annual course alone.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — Mohole's dedicated costs page (/iscrizioni/costi-agevolazioni/) publishes NO figures at all: no enrolment fee, no materials fee, no exam or certification fee, no RSL certification cost. It lists only the existence of discounts and financing and directs enquirers to phone or email the segreteria (+39 02 3651 3670 / segreteria@mohole.it). Assume undisclosed extras and demand an itemised written quote.
totalCost: €8,500/year verified tuition; approx. €25,500 over three years before discounts; plus €1,500–3,000 of Mac/DAW equipment, plus undisclosed enrolment and certification fees, plus Milan living costs of roughly €12,000–15,000 per year. Realistic three-year all-in exposure: €65,000–80,000 — for a qualification with no Italian legal value and no clear visa route.
scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED and now looking weaker than the prior entry suggested. The costs page does NOT publish any scholarship amounts, criteria or eligibility, and says nothing about non-EU applicants. 'Borse di studio' are discussed only at the orientation interview. For a non-EU applicant who must budget before applying for a visa, an undisclosed discretionary discount decided in a sales conversation is not a financial plan.
entry: Orientation interview (colloquio conoscitivo). No prior experience required — the school's own wording is "si parte da zero" ("you start from zero"). A secondary-school diploma is required for conferral of the Bachelor of Arts; minimum age 18 for the professional competency certificates. No degree required — this is undergraduate-entry, meaning he would be starting a bachelor's again despite already holding one.
acceptsNonMusic: Yes — no prerequisites at all. The school's own wording is "si parte da zero"; entry is by orientation interview and a secondary-school diploma is the only formal document needed for the BA. But this cuts against him, not for him: it is undergraduate-entry, so a graduate with a BSc would be starting a first degree over again, alongside school-leavers.
portfolio: None required. Nothing to prepare — which also means nothing filters the cohort.
audition: None. Orientation interview only, in Italian.
deadline: No fixed deadline published — rolling until places fill, with an early-enrolment promotion that locks a reduced rate. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for any 2027 entry.
opens: Rolling. Entry is by booking a 'colloquio conoscitivo' (orientation interview) online at any time; a 'Super Early Bird' promotion rewards enrolling well ahead.
duration: 3 years / 180 ECTS (EQF 6 claimed), or a 1-year / 60 ECTS single annuality which is year one of the same course. Monday–Friday full-time attendance. October 2026 start.
englishTest: Not applicable, and IELTS is of no use here. The course is delivered in Italian; English appears only as a taught subject. Italian proficiency is the real language requirement and no level is published — ask.
study: Year 1 (= the one-year annual course): Music Production 1, Sound Design 1, Linguaggio Musicale 1, Musica d'insieme, Logic Pro, Ableton Live, piano/keys, complementary instrument, Tecniche del suono 1, Scenari musicali, English, plus workshops. Year 2: Music Production 2, Sound Design 2, Music Industry, Tecniche del suono 2, DJ | Tecniche di mix. Year 3: Music Production 3, Sound Design 3, Music Management, AI e Musica, Sound Design per Videogiochi, DJ | Live Performance, Social e Brand Identity, showreel/portfolio and thesis project. Software taught, verified: Logic Pro, Ableton Live, MuseScore and Unreal Engine (the latter for game audio).
recommendation: RIGHT SUBJECT, WRONG EVERYTHING ELSE — and verification has now hardened this from suspicion to fact. Three things changed since the prior entry: the €8,500/year fee is CONFIRMED on Mohole's own page; the awarding body is CONFIRMED as EABHES; and EABHES is CONFIRMED, from its own website, to be a private association rather than a state accreditation agency. So the 'Laurea Europea recognised in EU, UK and USA' is a private-network award marketed in the vocabulary of official recognition. Add the rest: it is an undergraduate course for a man who already has a degree, taught entirely in Italian, with no published visa pathway and no AFAM status to fall back on. If he ever contacts them, three questions in writing, and do not enrol without all three answered on paper: (1) is the Bachelor of Arts recognised by MUR and does it carry valore legale in Italy — yes or no; (2) can you issue the documentation for Universitaly pre-enrolment and a type-D study visa for a Tunisian national — yes or no; (3) send the full itemised cost sheet including enrolment fee, RSL certification fees and the actual value of the early-bird and three-year discounts. Expect the answer to (1) to be no and to (2) to be evasive. Until then, unusable.

Listed because it is the best film-sound master in Flanders and worth knowing about.

acceptsNonMusic: FORMALLY YES, PRACTICALLY NO — this corrects the previous 'No'. portfolio: EXACT, from the official 2026/27 specific conditions (uploaded via https://prihlaska.amu.cz after the application closes and the fee is paid): (1) A list of ALL your own sound works created during bachelor studies — audiovisual or multimedia works, music recordings, radio and theatre sound work — each with title, genre, director's first and last name, plus production, running time and year of production, ordered by date of creation, INCLUDING works still in progress. (2) TWO audiovisual works on whose sound component you contributed significantly, with detailed written explications for both, PLUS your own theoretical work in the field. (3) A written project for master's study at FAMU: your intended specialisation, expected study outputs, which elective courses at FAMU or other universities you would take, and any interest in a study-abroad placement. FORMATS: files named "TASK NUMBER - TASK NAME - SURNAME FIRSTNAME" without diacritics; audio as WAV; video preferably MP4/MOV, H.264, max 10 Mbit/s; all written documents as PDF with a header giving programme, name and address. A SIGNED SWORN DECLARATION OF AUTHORSHIP is mandatory, and it explicitly requires you to declare whether generative AI was used (permitted only for research, language/grammar checking, or consulting narrative quality of finished text) — failing to respect this means the admission condition is not met.
audition: TWO ROUNDS, and round 2 is IN PERSON IN PRAGUE. Round 1 (2026/27 date: 14 Sept 2026) assesses talent from the submitted works only, with no applicant present; the commission decides who advances. Round 2 (2026/27 date: 17 Sept 2026, prezenčně) is an oral examination before the departmental board: the master's project and the list of your own sound works form the basis of the interview; you must demonstrate theoretical knowledge of the artistic and technical problems of the field at the level of a FAMU Sound Design BA graduate, AND musical erudition by one of — playing a musical instrument (melodic, rhythmic OR ELECTRONIC), singing, or another suitable form of live performance. You then also sit a PITCH-MEMORY TEST and a RHYTHMIC DICTATION. Pass mark 40 of 60 points overall plus a minimum in every sub-exam.

programme: Máster en Diseño de Sonido Cinematográfico (film and audiovisual sound design)
whyChance: Explicitly open to a non-music/any bachelor's, but taught in Spanish — language is the real gate
qualification: A PRIVATE SCHOOL CERTIFICATE. The award described on the Educaweb listing is 'Curso de Diseño de Sonido Cinematográfico por ECIB' — a CURSO, not a máster — even though ECIB markets the programme under the name 'Máster en Diseño de sonido de cine y sonido audiovisual'. No ECTS, no validating university and no official award are published for this programme.
accreditation: NOT OFFICIAL. No ANECA or AQU verification, no validating university, no ECTS, no official Spanish award of any kind. This is ECIB's own certificate. The gap between the marketing name ('Máster') and the award actually described ('Curso ... por ECIB') is precisely the discrepancy pattern he must learn to spot. NOTE A FURTHER UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY: the Docenzia aggregator describes ECIB 'máster' programmes generically as 1 year / 60 ECTS, but does not list the sound design programme at all, and no ECTS figure appears on any listing specific to this course. Two sources also give conflicting durations — Educaweb says 248 hours plus filming practice, while ECIB's own marketing says 500 hours including internships. Neither is reconcilable with a 60-ECTS master (which implies roughly 1,500 hours of student workload).
tuition: UNVERIFIED — no published figure from any source.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED. Note that the Pro Tools annual licence is stated to be INCLUDED, which is a genuine cost offset of roughly €300 per year.
totalCost: UNVERIFIED — no price is published anywhere in any source read, and the school actively blocks automated access to its own pages. This opacity is itself a warning sign for a programme with no accreditation.
scholarshipDetail: UNVERIFIED — none published, and nothing specific to non-EU applicants.
entry: Deliberately open. VERIFIED from the Educaweb listing: students aged 17 and over, from Spain or internationally, with or without prior audiovisual or sound experience; cinema enthusiasts welcome. No degree of any kind is required.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — completely open access. No degree, no music background and no prior experience required. But note the flip side: open access means the qualification carries no selection signal whatsoever, and therefore no market value as a credential.
portfolio: None. No portfolio and no prior experience are required.
audition: None.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published deadline anywhere. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for any 2027 start.
duration: CONFLICTING SOURCES. Educaweb: 248 hours of classes plus filming practice hours. ECIB's own marketing: 500 hours including internships. No ECTS published under any source. Schedule: Mondays and Tuesdays, 16:00–20:00 — eight contact hours per week, part-time.
englishTest: No IELTS and no English requirement. Taught in Spanish, so Spanish proficiency is the real gate.
study: Five theory-practice modules following the phases of film sound: initial treatment of sound in the script; selection of materials and technical equipment in pre-production; capture and recording of sound on set; and editing and mixing in final post-production. Includes hands-on work on professional-standard short films and documentaries plus internships on real film productions. VERIFIED addition: students work with Avid Pro Tools as the reference program, and ECIB states it guarantees an INDIVIDUAL ANNUAL LICENCE for each student — a genuine and quantifiable benefit worth roughly €300.
recommendation: Wrong discipline, wrong structure, wrong level — skip it. This is film post-production sound, not music production or DJing, and nothing in it moves him toward an international DJ or producer career. Structurally it is disqualifying regardless of content: eight contact hours a week cannot support a Spanish student visa, so as a non-EU national he could not legally relocate to Barcelona on this programme at all. Add no accreditation, no ECTS, no published price, a school that blocks its own pages from being read, and marketing that calls a 'curso' a 'máster', and the verdict is straightforward. The Atmos 7.4.1 studio and the free Pro Tools licence are real assets and would matter to someone already living in Barcelona who wanted film sound — that person is not him. Keep it on the list only as a worked example of the 'private certificate marketed as a máster' pattern he must learn to recognise before he spends money.

scholarshipDetail: Yes — Tunisian nationals are eligible. DAAD maintains a Regional Office in TUNIS (covering Tunisia, Algeria, Libya, Morocco) with pre-application consultation in Arabic and French, and Tunisia appears in the DAAD scholarship database as a supported country. Confirm the Tunisia entry for the specific music line each year, since country lists are refreshed annually.
entry: A first degree in music (the scheme targets graduates who have "exhausted all training opportunities" at home). Degree must be no more than 6 years old at the deadline. You must not have lived in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline. Cannot fund a programme already started in Germany. Documents: tabular CV, 1-3 page letter of motivation, transcripts with grading explanation, degree certificate, language certificate (max 3 years old), German/English translations, a supervision confirmation from a lecturer at the German host institution, plus the Master's profile form and the letter of admission before the scholarship starts.
acceptsNonMusic: No, as written. The DAAD music line addresses applicants with "a first degree in music". A software-engineering BSc does not meet the stated profile — he would more plausibly use the parallel DAAD line for Fine Art/Design/Visual Communication/Film (listed separately below), or a general DAAD Master line if the German programme is academically rather than artistically classified.
portfolio: Artistic work samples uploaded to a DAAD media database within TWO WEEKS of receiving the access link. VIDEO files only (mp4, max 1080p). Exception: composition and AUDIO ENGINEERING applicants may submit audio (mp3, wav). MIDI realisations and technically manipulated files are NOT accepted. An overview form listing the recorded pieces is required.
audition: No DAAD live audition — the media-database work samples are the audition. A dedicated DAAD committee of professors from German art, music and film colleges decides. Separately, the German Musikhochschule will almost certainly run its own ENTRANCE EXAM, usually on-site in Germany — that is the real audition and it is the host institution's requirement, not DAAD's.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Deadlines are set annually and vary by line and country; the arts/music lines have historically closed in the autumn preceding the October start. For a 1 October 2027 start expect the portal open 1 June 2026-2027 window — CONFIRM the exact 2027 date on the DAAD portal and with DAAD Tunis.
duration: 10-24 months of funding for a degree programme (2-4 semesters); 12 months (extendable) for non-degree advanced studies
study: Whatever the German host programme delivers — the scheme is the money, not the curriculum. IMPORTANT LIMIT: "This programme only funds projects in the artistic field." Musicology, music education and scientific/technical projects belong to other DAAD lines. Sound engineering / music production is fundable ONLY where the host programme is artistically classified — verify the classification with the intended Musikhochschule before applying.
recommendation: The scheme itself is excellent value (fee-free public conservatories + full living stipend) and DAAD Tunis gives him local support in French/Arabic. The blocker is eligibility: the music line expects a first degree IN MUSIC, and German Musikhochschulen run demanding on-site entrance exams. He should treat DAAD as the funding layer for a German target school and check whether that school's programme is artistically or academically classified, because that determines which DAAD line he uses.
