entry: CRITICAL CORRECTION — the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page states: 'Voraussetzung ist der Nachweis eines abgeschlossenen künstlerischen Bachelor- oder Diplomstudiums oder eines gleichwertig anerkannten künstlerischen Studiengangs mit Schwerpunktsetzung im Bereich Musikproduktion (z.B. Tonmeister, Soundengineering, Musikregie etc.). Im Sinne eines künstlerischen Abschlusses gilt auch ein Bachelorstudium im Studiengang Ton und Bild.' A completed ARTISTIC bachelor or diploma (or equivalent recognised artistic degree) WITH AN EMPHASIS IN MUSIC PRODUCTION is mandatory. Plus German B2 (Goethe), plus passing the concentration-specific Eignungsprüfung. Aptitude-test fee €50 for the first application, €10 for each additional application (confirmed).
acceptsNonMusic: No — this is a hard correction to the earlier 'Check'. The requirement is not merely 'a bachelor's degree': it must be an artistic bachelor/diploma with a music-production emphasis, and the examples given are Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's own Ton und Bild bachelor. A BSc in Software Engineering is neither artistic nor production-focused in the sense meant, so he is formally ineligible, before the audition is even considered.
portfolio: NOW EXACT (from the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page). Jazz/Pop major pre-selection: a portfolio of FOUR TO SIX already-realised works (or excerpts) in different styles from the jazz/popular-music production field; one audio file/track package per work sample; TOTAL DURATION 15–20 MINUTES; accepted formats stereo, 5.1/7.1 or Atmos; stereo mixes as stereo .wav, multichannel as clearly labelled mono .wav files (5.1/7.1) or as an ADM file (Atmos); each work sample accompanied by a short description of how it was made. PLUS unedited videos of the applicant's own artistic performance on instrument/voice (jazz/pop) with improvisation or ad-libs, tempi and styles varying, own composition allowed, max 20 minutes total — with an important alternative for keyboard/jazz piano: 'die Einreichung von bis zu drei Stücken mit Improvisation mit Hilfe von elektronischen Instrumenten wie Keyboards, Synthesizern, DAWs (z.B. Ableton live) mit deutlich erkennbarem spielerisch-handwerklichem Anteil sowie erkennbar eigener Soundgestaltung' (up to three pieces with improvisation using keyboards, synths or DAWs such as Ableton Live, with clearly recognisable playing craft and own sound design). PLUS a motivation letter referencing the chosen major and a CV with certificates. (Classical major differs: 5–6 works, 30–45 minutes, plus three works from different stylistic periods on video.)
audition: Yes — a substantial ON-SITE examination (Präsenzprüfung) in Düsseldorf, in four parts: (1) artistic presentation on instrument or voice with the same repertoire as the pre-selection, plus a prepared solo transcription (or a short a cappella piece for jazz/pop voice) AND sight-reading / sight-singing; six copies of the scores or lead sheets must be brought. (2) An UNPREPARED practical task in the chosen major, e.g. a mix or an edit, typically one to two hours. (3) Written examinations of both musical and technical hearing: musical ear (~40 min: dictations from piano and from recordings, intonation hearing, error detection, short aural analysis, instrumentation hearing) and technical ear (~40 min: listening examples including technical artefacts, level judgement, formant hearing). (4) A Fachgespräch with the selection panel, max 30 minutes. Fee €50.
deadline: 1 March, published as a standing annual deadline: 'Der Bewerbungsschluss zum Wintersemester ist der 1. März.' Aptitude tests for Künstlerische Musikproduktion are held for the WINTER SEMESTER ONLY ('Für die Masterstudiengänge Künstlerische Musikproduktion und Musikfilmregie ... gibt es Eignungsprüfungen ausschließlich zum Wintersemester'). So a September/October 2027 start means applying by 1 March 2027. The date is a standing rule rather than a prior-cycle artefact, but confirm it is unchanged when the 2027 links open. (The earlier note that entry is possible in winter OR summer was wrong for this programme.)
opens: Not published; the muvac application links are opened roughly one month before each deadline (as stated for the sister programme).
duration: 4 semesters (2 years). ECTS total not stated on the programme page or the Modulplan page — UNVERIFIED.
study: Two majors: Classical Acoustic Music Production, and Jazz and Pop Music Production. Three interwoven strands over four semesters: practical production work across genres and formats using the most recent production methods; instrumental/vocal tuition with ensemble performance; and technical methodology plus musical analysis including acoustics and ear training. Goal is artistically independent, methodically grounded professional production work. CONFIRMED on the official page — genuinely the most production-focused public master in this batch.
recommendation: Content-wise this is the best genuine music-production master in the batch — a real Jazz/Pop production track, Atmos-aware, with mixing and editing as examined craft. It is also the most firmly closed to him. The prerequisite is an artistic bachelor with a music-production emphasis (Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's Ton und Bild), which a software-engineering BSc is not; and even if that were waived, the on-site exam demands an instrumental/vocal performance with sight-reading, a live mixing task, and 80 minutes of written musical and technical ear tests, all in German at B2. Realistic only after a production-focused artistic bachelor plus years of instrument and ear training. Worth noting as a long-term aspiration and as a source of a training checklist — the Ableton/synth alternative for the keyboard performance shows what standard would eventually be expected — but not a 2027 target.

institution: SAE Institute Milano (SAE Italia S.R.L. International Technology College — SAE / Navitas global chain)
programme: Produzione Audio / Audio Production and Music Technologies — Diploma Accademico di Primo Livello
whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
qualification: Diploma Accademico di PRIMO livello — a first-level, bachelor-equivalent AFAM academic diploma, legally recognised by the Italian Ministry of University and Research. A genuine, official Italian qualification — but BACHELOR level, not a master. CONFIRMED: SAE Milano is authorised for first-level diplomas only and has NO 'Diploma Accademico di secondo livello' anywhere in its catalogue.
accreditation: OFFICIAL — CONFIRMED, and the only officially accredited programme in this batch. SAE Institute Milano appears BY NAME on MUR's official register of legally recognised AFAM institutes, listed under Lombardia as 'SAE Institute. Creative media education – Milano'. It is a non-state institution operating inside the national AFAM framework, ministerially authorised under Ministerial Decree 280 of 16 May 2017 pursuant to Art. 11 of DPR 212/2005. An AFAM first-level diploma is equated to a three-year laurea within the Italian higher-education qualifications framework. CRUCIAL CAVEAT, now firmly established: this official status covers the FIRST-LEVEL diploma only. Any SAE Italy course not on that ministerial list — including the Electronic Music Production and Urban Music Production short courses — is a purely private certificate with no legal academic value.
tuition: UNVERIFIED — no published figure for the three-year diploma anywhere on the official site. This is the single biggest information gap in this batch and stands in sharp contrast to SAE Amsterdam and Abbey Road, which publish every instalment total.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED — no enrolment, exam or materials fees published.
totalCost: UNVERIFIED — no tuition figure is published for any SAE Milano programme. Three years of unpublished fees plus Milan living costs, which are among the highest in Italy. He cannot budget for this without phoning the school directly.
scholarshipDetail: Genuinely valuable and unique in this batch, though amounts UNVERIFIED. Because SAE Milano is a recognised AFAM institution, its students can apply for Italian regional right-to-study grants (borse di studio per il diritto allo studio universitario); in Lombardy these are administered regionally and are generally open to non-EU students meeting income and merit criteria. No other private provider in this batch gives access to state right-to-study funding. Amounts and deadlines UNVERIFIED — confirm with the Lombardy regional authority, not the school. SAE Italy also runs occasional sponsored scholarships, e.g. the Billboard Italia 'Women in Music' bando covering 100% of tuition (not applicable to him).
entry: CONFIRMED. Domestic: minimum age 18; high school diploma or equivalent validated by the relevant authorities for Italy; aptitude interview, with possible additional skill assessments. International (his category): minimum age 18; certified translation of a qualification equivalent to the Italian high school diploma; certified Italian at minimum B2 CEFR; aptitude interview and possible additional assessments.
acceptsNonMusic: Not applicable in the way he needs. Entry is UNDERGRADUATE: the requirement is a high school diploma or foreign equivalent 'validated by the relevant authorities for Italy' — not a bachelor's. No music background is required, and no portfolio. His BSc would over-qualify him for a programme that sits BELOW his current level.
portfolio: No portfolio required — CONFIRMED. Admission is by aptitude interview and possible skills assessment only. Notable as the only programme in this batch with no portfolio gate.
audition: Aptitude interview ('colloquio attitudinale'), with the Academic Board reserving discretion to request additional assessments evaluating suitability.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — no application deadline published on the course page. Non-EU visa pre-enrolment deadlines are set nationally and are typically EARLIER than the school's own; both must be confirmed.
opens: UNVERIFIED — not published on the course page. Non-EU applicants must in practice work backwards from Italian national pre-enrolment (Universitaly) timelines, which typically run in spring/early summer preceding an October start.
duration: 3 years, 180 CFA (the AFAM credit unit, equivalent in weight to ECTS). CONFIRMED on the official course page.
englishTest: IELTS is NOT the relevant test and is not an entry route. The published language requirement for international students is certified ITALIAN at B2 CEFR. Even though teaching is bilingual English/Italian, no English test substitutes for the Italian certification.
study: Three years, 180 CFA. Foundational technical training in acoustics, recording, mixing and mastering, combined with contemporary applications: immersive systems, game audio, sound design and AI in music production. Delivery is explicitly project-based, 'replicating industry dynamics'. Internships and placements are organised during the programme. Career outcomes: recording engineer, music producer, sound designer, live sound engineer, audio programmer for games.
recommendation: Officially accredited, visa-viable, and still the wrong programme — the mismatch is level and language, not quality. This is the only programme in this batch verified at the ministry itself: SAE Institute Milano is named on MUR's official AFAM register, which means a real Italian qualification and, uniquely here, a plausible route to a study visa. But it is a three-year bachelor-equivalent he does not need, and international entry demands certified Italian at B2 — a requirement that bilingual English/Italian teaching does not waive, and which he cannot realistically reach and certify before an October 2027 start. Three things are worth carrying forward. First, it proves SAE can hold genuine accreditation where it seeks it, which throws its unaccredited Amsterdam certificates and any Spanish 'máster' claims into unflattering relief — always check the national register, never the school's own wording. Second, its AFAM status opens Italian REGIONAL right-to-study grants (borse di studio) to non-EU students, the only state funding identified anywhere in this batch; if Italy interests him at all, that mechanism is worth understanding, though he must confirm amounts and deadlines with the Lombardy regional authority rather than the school. Third, and decisively for planning: SAE Milano has NO second-level authorisation at all, so there is no Italian SAE master coming — do not wait for one. One practical warning if he ever reconsiders Italy: SAE publishes no fees anywhere, so he cannot budget without phoning 02 8912 0540, and non-EU Universitaly pre-enrolment deadlines typically fall well before the school's own.

programme: COVERAGE NOTE — negative and partial findings across the remaining Austrian list
whyChance: No explicit statement — ask admissions, but taught in German — language is the real gate

qualification: NONE CONFIRMED IN FIELD at these institutions.

tuition: AUSTRIAN THIRD-COUNTRY RATES OBSERVED IN THIS SWEEP: FH JOANNEUM Graz €727/semester (double the €363.36 EU rate), prepaid €1,454 for the first two semesters; USTP St. Pölten €1,500/semester. Austrian PUBLIC UNIVERSITIES (Mozarteum, ABPU is private) charge third-country nationals the statutory double rate of €726.72 per semester plus ÖH. So Austria's ceiling is roughly €1,450–3,000 per year — much cheaper than a private German diploma and comparable to Switzerland, but not free the way Berlin or Thuringia are.
otherFees: ÖH student union contribution €20.70–26.20 per semester at all Austrian institutions. Austrian student residence-permit fees and proof-of-funds requirement.

entry: n/a — no confirmed in-field master at these institutions.
languageReq: German B2 is the Austrian FH norm (confirmed at USTP St. Pölten). FH JOANNEUM Graz Sound Design is the exception: English B2 only, no German.
study: (1) ANTON BRUCKNER PRIVATUNIVERSITÄT LINZ — offers 13 bachelor and 12 master programmes, all awarding BA and MA, across classical instruments, voice, early music, jazz, composition, contemporary dance, theatre, music communication and elementary music pedagogy. It has a Computer Music Studio within the 'Institut für Komposition, Dirigieren und Computermusik' (Prof. Volkmar Klien, composition with a focus on electronic and computer music) and a professor of jazz saxophone AND MUSIC PRODUCTION (Fabian Rucker). BUT NO STANDALONE MUSIKPRODUKTION MASTER WAS IDENTIFIED — the computer-music strand sits under composition, which this brief excludes. The full master list could not be read from the site and this negative is UNVERIFIED; ABPU is the one Austrian institution worth a direct e-mail, because a production professor without a production degree usually means production teaching sits inside the jazz or composition master. (2) UNIVERSITÄT MOZARTEUM SALZBURG — masters found are Composition and Music Theory; recording, mixing and electroacoustic production appear as ACTIVITIES within those programmes, not as a degree. No Tonmeister or Musikproduktion master. Excluded on field grounds. (3) FH VORARLBERG (Dornbirn) — its 'InterMedia' master is interdisciplinary media design; no dedicated sound or music-production master was confirmed. UNVERIFIED. (4) SAE INSTITUTE VIENNA — private, same structure as SAE elsewhere: Audio Engineering Diploma then a bachelor, with masters delivered only through the UK/partner routes ('MA/MSc Professional Practice (Creative Media Industries)' with the University of Hertfordshire, and 'MA Professional Media Creation' with Folkwang in Germany). No Austrian-accredited SAE master. Fees not published. UNVERIFIED. (5) THE AUSTRIAN TRAP, RESTATED PLAINLY: several Austrian audio and music-production offerings are UNIVERSITÄTSLEHRGÄNGE — continuing-education courses, not second-cycle degrees. A Universitätslehrgang awards an MA/MSc-style title but is NOT an ordentliches Masterstudium, several of them require an ALREADY-COMPLETED master or equivalent professional standing to enter, and they generally do not support a student residence permit on the same footing. By contrast, the two Austrian programmes recorded in full here — FH JOANNEUM Graz (Master of Arts in Arts and Design) and USTP St. Pölten (Diplom-Ingenieur) — are BOTH ordentliche FH master's degrees, NOT Lehrgänge. That is why they are the ones worth pursuing.

DEPRIORITISE the Conservatorium van Amsterdam Master in Immersive Audio despite its NVAO accreditation: it demands a bachelor's in music or a related field AND professional-level audio engineering experience, and screens with a live Pro Tools mixing test on a 24-track session. He has neither the degree nor the experience today; applying for September 2027 would be a wasted application unless he spends the next year acquiring demonstrable professional mixing work. WHAT HE SHOULD ACTUALLY DO WITH THE NETHERLANDS IN THE MEANTIME: build the portfolio he does not have, to a published standard rather than a vague one. The CvA practical test tells him the benchmark precisely — a body of presentable recorded work plus the ability to deliver a clean 10-minute stereo mix from a 24-track Pro Tools session. Short courses in Amsterdam can be attended on an ordinary Schengen tourist visa and require no accreditation, and timing a visit around Amsterdam Dance Event in October adds scene contacts — but get every price in writing by email first, because none of the circulating figures survived verification. institution: Universitatea Națională de Muzică din București (UNMB) / National University of Music Bucharest
programme: Regie muzicală (Music Directing / Sound Direction) — studii postuniversitare. WARNING: THIS IS NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE.
whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
qualification: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. The award is a 'certificat de competență profesională' (professional competency certificate) for the occupation of music director, C.O.R. code 265228, issued jointly by the Ministry of Education and UNMB. It is officially inscribed in the National Registry of Postgraduate Programmes, so it is a real state-registered qualification and NOT a scam — but it is a postgraduate professional certificate, not a second-cycle (ciclul II) degree, and confers no master's.
accreditation: Genuine and state-registered (Registrul Național al Programelor Postuniversitare; Ministry-issued certificate), but categorically outside the Bologna second cycle. This is precisely the category the brief warns about: a real, reputable institution selling a real but non-degree postgraduate award whose name reads like a master's in exactly the field he is searching.
tuition: €1,600 for international participants, payable in three instalments — CONFIRMED VERBATIM on the official page. This is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national, and it is one of the very few places in this sweep where a distinct non-EU figure is actually published rather than inferred. It is cheap because the course is short and non-degree, not because it is good value for him.
otherFees: 100 RON registration fee (taxă de înscriere) plus 150 RON enrolment fee (taxă de înmatriculare) — CONFIRMED.
totalCost: €1,600 tuition plus 250 RON in fees, plus Bucharest living costs for the duration. Irrelevant in practice, since it confers no degree and supports no residence permit.
scholarshipDetail: None. Romanian Government/MFA and ARICE scholarships fund licență, masterat and doctorat cycles at accredited institutions. A 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a study cycle and would not be covered. Do not expect funding.
entry: A bachelor's degree or equivalent — CONFIRMED. No music degree is formally named, but the entrance exam assumes conservatoire-level aural training, which functions as a de facto music-degree requirement.
acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice — CONFIRMED. The formal condition is only a bachelor's degree in any field, but the entrance examination requires 16-bar melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, and aural timbre and instrument recognition. These are conservatoire skills. Without a music background he would fail the exam, and no amount of DAW proficiency substitutes.
portfolio: None specified — CONFIRMED. The gate is the aural-skills examination, not a portfolio. Which is worse for him, not better: a portfolio he could build in a year, an ear he cannot.
audition: DISQUALIFYING FOR THIS CANDIDATE — CONFIRMED IN SHARPER DETAIL THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Two components. (1) WRITTEN test: melodic dictation of up to 16 measures with a key signature of up to two sharps or flats, plus identification and notation of transposing instruments. (2) ORAL exam: identifying instrument timbres by ear and answering related questions. Taking a 16-bar melodic dictation in up to two accidentals is a skill built over years of formal solfège; identifying transposing instruments and their written-versus-sounding pitches is standard conservatoire theory. Someone with no music degree, no conservatoire training and one year of self-study will not pass this.
deadline: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask UNMB's Studii Postuniversitare office. Moot in practice, given everything below.
duration: CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 146 contact hours, 15 ECTS, in-person attendance. For scale, a genuine Romanian master's is 120 ECTS over two years — at 15 ECTS this is one-eighth of a master's. It is a short professional course.
languageReq: Not separately published — UNVERIFIED — but since teaching is in Romanian and the entrance exam is oral and written in Romanian, Romanian competence is required in practice. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant. UNMB does publish a non-EU admission methodology; ask its postgraduate office whether that route even applies to postuniversitare courses.
study: Music direction (regie muzicală), the classical Romanian tonmeister discipline. Detailed syllabus not published on the official page — UNVERIFIED. The entrance exam content is itself the clearest evidence of the discipline's nature: melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, timbral hearing and instrument recognition. This is built entirely on classical-music aural skill. There is nothing here about electronic production, DJing, DAWs or club music.
recommendation: CONFIRMED IN FULL, NO CORRECTIONS NEEDED — DO NOT PURSUE. I re-checked every figure against the official UNMB page and all of them are exact: 146 hours, 15 ECTS, Romanian instruction, 8,000 lei domestic and €1,600 international in three instalments, 100 RON registration plus 150 RON enrolment, certificate of professional competency C.O.R. 265228 registered in the National Registry of Postgraduate Programmes. This entry was accurate. AVOID stands. Searching 'music direction Romania master' or 'regie muzicală' leads straight here, at Romania's national music university, at an apparently affordable €1,600 for international students. It is not a master's degree. It is a 146-hour, 15-ECTS professional certificate — one-eighth the volume of a real second-cycle degree — it will not support a student residence permit, it is taught in Romanian, and its entrance exam is a conservatoire aural test (16-bar melodic dictation in up to two accidentals, transposing-instrument notation, timbral recognition) that he cannot pass without years of solfège. The low price signals what it is; it is not a bargain. Note also that UNMB's genuine master's portfolio contains NO sound-technology programme: the Faculty of Composition, Musicology and Music Pedagogy offers only Stil și limbaj compozițional, Sinteză muzicologică, Stilistică dirijorală, Jazz și culturi muzicale pop, Educație muzicală contemporană and Culturi muzicale religioase, and the Faculty of Musical Interpretation offers only performance-stylistics masters. UNMB is a dead end for him and should be closed off entirely — the Romanian opening is at UNATC, whose English-taught MAs need no Romanian and no conservatoire ear.

Compulsory health insurance for foreign students — cost still UNVERIFIED.
totalCost: Now largely computable. Tuition EUR 1,800 for the entire 60-ECTS degree. Plus institutional/administrative costs: 12,000 RSD exam fee + 5,500 RSD enrolment + 30,000 RSD (or EUR 260) recognition fee + 14,900 RSD administrative tax, i.e. roughly EUR 480–560 at ~117 RSD/EUR. So about EUR 2,300–2,400 in institution-side costs for the whole master, before living costs, visa fees, health insurance and Serbian-language tuition. Living costs in Novi Sad are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED. This remains among the cheapest genuinely accredited music-production masters in Europe.
scholarshipDetail: No programme-level or Academy-level scholarship for non-EU applicants is published on any official page — UNVERIFIED, unchanged after re-checking. Do not assume one exists. Realistic avenues to ask: (1) the Serbian Ministry of Education's bilateral scholarship offers, which are distributed through the applicant's home ministry — he should ask the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur whether Serbia offers Tunisia places in a given year; (2) the University of Novi Sad international office. Erasmus+ credit mobility is inbound-only for already-enrolled students and is not an admission route.
entry: THE DOCUMENTED CONTRADICTION IS REAL — I re-read both source documents and confirm it, but I now judge which one governs. (a) The 2026/27 konkurs, §2, programme-specific clause: 'Студијски програм – Музичка продукција: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању из уметничке области Музичка продукција, или сродан студијски програм (240 ЕСПБ)' — a four-year BA IN THE ARTISTIC FIELD of music production, or a cognate programme. (b) The informator, Opšti uslovi: 'Пријемни испит могу полагати лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)' — any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor. CORRECTION OF EMPHASIS: the konkurs is the legally binding enrolment act adopted on the University's template and issued on the basis of a Government decision; the informator is a summary of exam content. Where they differ the konkurs governs. Read that way, a BSc Software Engineering is NOT in the artistic field of music production and is unlikely to be accepted as 'srodan'. Second, the konkurs §2.2 general rule requires 'najmanje 240 ESPB' and lists the ONLY four exceptions permitted at 180 ECTS — Konzervacija i restauracija, the Guitar/Performing Arts joint programme, Kreiranje serija, and Pozorišni oblici modul Lutkarstvo. Muzička produkcija is NOT among them. A Tunisian three-year 180-ECTS licence is therefore ineligible, full stop. Foreign nationals additionally file the diploma-recognition decision, health-insurance proof and Serbian-language proof.
acceptsNonMusic: NO on the governing document — this is a correction of emphasis from the previous record, which left it 'ambiguous'. The konkurs restricts entry to a four-year bachelor in the artistic field of Music Production or a cognate programme. Software engineering is not cognate to music production in any ordinary reading. Even on the permissive informator reading he would still face a Serbian-language written subject test in music production, a written musical analysis, a commission interview and a portfolio. Unlike a conservatory master there is no instrumental audition, which is the one thing in his favour.
portfolio: CONFIRMED and EXPANDED — the previous record omitted two konkurs-level documents. Informator required documents: diploma or certificate of a completed four-year 240-ECTS bachelor; CV (biografija); motivation letter; MEDICAL CERTIFICATE WITH AN AUDIOGRAM (ophthalmologist, ENT specialist, psychologist); scanned/read ID; photo min. 1200x800 px JPG under 1 MB; proof of payment of the application fee. Separately, 'uz prijavu kandidati prilažu': (1) the medical certificate with audiogram, (2) a PORTFOLIO of works created in the 3 years preceding the date of the entrance exam. ADDITIONALLY required by konkurs §5 and omitted from the previous record: the completed PRIJAVNI LIST (application form, downloadable as Prijavni-list-za-master-studije-2026-2027.pdf) and the UVERENJE O POLOŽENIM ISPITIMA (official transcript of passed exams). Submission is 100% electronic, one e-mail per candidate to aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, all files under 12 MB total, every file named with the candidate's full name, study programme named in the subject line. His one-year portfolio plan does map onto the 'previous 3 years' rule.
audition: CONFIRMED verbatim. Two stages. PART ONE (pass/fail): written test in the professional-artistic field of Music Production; written analysis/evaluation of a musical work against subjective and objective criteria set by the commission; interview with the commission. Those who pass proceed to multi-day exercises and PART TWO: assessment of submitted works up to 30 points; practical work on the Academy's own material/equipment up to 20 points; oral examination of knowledge in the professional-artistic field of AUDIOVISUAL MEDIA (interview with the commission) up to 30 points. BA grade average scores separately, up to 20 points (10.00 = 20 pts; 6.49–6.00 = 4 pts; below 6.00 scores nothing). A candidate not exceeding 50 total points fails and is not ranked. Mobile phones and auxiliary devices are strictly banned from the exam rooms. Conducted in Serbian.
deadline: CORRECTED — the previous record missed the SECOND application round entirely, which materially improves his odds. 2026/27 cycle, Drama Department / Interdisciplinary studies (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for 2027/28). FIRST ROUND: electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07–13.10.2026; preliminary ranking 15.10.2026; final ranking 20.10.2026; enrolment 20.10.2026. SECOND ROUND (DRUGI KONKURSNI ROK): electronic application 21.10.2026; entrance exam 23–28.10.2026; preliminary ranking 30.10.2026; final ranking and enrolment 03.11.2026. Appeals to the Dean within 24 hours of the preliminary list. The timing trap stands: applications close in EARLY OCTOBER of the year of entry, not the preceding winter — but the diploma-recognition process, the audiogram/medical certificate and Serbian-language study must start many months earlier.
opens: 2026/27 cycle: konkurs text published 29 May 2026 (per the Drama Department admissions page), informators posted July 2026 (the Kreiranje serija informator appeared as late as August 2026). For a September/October 2027 entry, expect the 2027/28 konkurs around May–June 2027 and informators in July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note the informator itself states that the Drama Department's application and exam dates 'will be published on the Academy website', so the konkurs is the document to watch.
duration: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS. CONFIRMED from both the informator and the accredited curriculum sheet.
languageReq: Konkurs §9 (Upis stranih državljana): a foreign national enrols 'pod istim uslovima kao i domaći državljanin' and additionally files (a) rešenje o priznavanju strane diplome, (b) dokaz o zdravstvenom osiguranju, (c) 'dokaz o poznavanju srpskog jezika'. The required LEVEL and the accepted certificate are still NOT published — UNVERIFIED, confirmed by re-checking the University of Novi Sad's general rule, which only refers back to 'the University Statute and the Faculty Statute'. Ask: Služba za studije i studentska pitanja, 021/422-177 lok. 2 or 021/422-176 lok. 2, aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
englishTest: None. No IELTS/TOEFL appears anywhere in the konkurs or informator. Confirmed. His untaken IELTS is genuinely irrelevant here — the language barrier is Serbian, and it is a much harder one for him than IELTS would be.
study: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official accredited curriculum sheet (mas-muzicka-produkcija-2024.pdf). Compulsory: Muzička produkcija (2+2, both semesters); Zvuk i muzika na filmu (2+1); Savremene tendencije u muzičkoj produkciji 1 (1+2) and 2 (2+2); Muzika-događaj-publika (1+1, both semesters); Master rad – istraživanje (0+0+6); Master rad (0+0+5). Electives, 12 ECTS per semester block chosen from: Dramaturgija savremenog filma (2+1); Metode u muzičkom obrazovanju u digitalnom okruženju (2+0); Istorija elektroakustičke muzike (2+0); Istorija popularne muzike (2+0); Produkcija muzike za nove medije (1+2); Muzika u medijima (1+1). Hours are weekly, as (lectures)+(exercises)+(DON).
recommendation: Content-wise this is still the best-matched accredited music-production master in the Serbian state sector, and at roughly EUR 2,300 all-in it is extraordinarily cheap. But after re-reading the governing documents I am less optimistic than the previous assessment, which called it 'the single best find'. Three gates, and he currently fails all three. (1) THE 240-ECTS RULE IS ABSOLUTE. Konkurs §2.2 lists the only four programmes at the Academy that accept 180 ECTS, and Muzička produkcija is not one of them. If his SMU MedTech BSc is a three-year 180-ECTS licence he is ineligible regardless of talent, portfolio or motivation. Verify this FIRST. (2) THE FIELD RESTRICTION IS REAL. The binding konkurs requires a four-year bachelor 'iz umetničke oblasti Muzička produkcija, ili srodan studijski program'. The permissive informator wording is a summary, not the rule. A software-engineering degree is very unlikely to qualify as cognate. (3) SERBIAN. The entrance exam is a written subject test plus a written musical analysis plus two commission interviews, all in Serbian. Going from zero Slavic to exam-level Serbian in twelve months while also building a first audio portfolio and arranging an ENT audiogram in Tunisia is not a realistic 2027 plan. Everything is verified and correct in the record; what has changed is the honest read of his odds. Concrete next step, one e-mail to aofarts@uns.ac.rs copying aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs, asking: (a) can a 180-ECTS three-year foreign bachelor ever be accepted for MAS Muzička produkcija; (b) is a BSc in Software Engineering treated as a 'srodan studijski program' under the konkurs; (c) which Serbian-language certificate and level satisfies the requirement; (d) may foreign nationals compete for the 2 budget places.

whyChance: States it does not accept a non-music background
verdictWhy: Entry is a closed list of six conservatoire bachelor specialisations, none of which he can hold, and the programme is missing from both partner institutions' 2026/2027 handbooks. Taught in Bulgarian on top of that.
correction: Refines rather than overturns the record's negative finding: the AMTII specialty page is still live and still describes the programme as an active inter-university master's with NMA Sofia, so 'NOT OFFERED' should be softened to 'absent from both 2026/2027 handbooks; specialty page still live and not withdrawn'. Adds the fact that settles it independently of whether it runs — entry is restricted to six named conservatoire bachelor specialisations. Also corrects the gate: 'Exam/interview only' is right but underspecified — it is a single interview on four business topics, with no portfolio, no audition and no production task at all.
qualification: ОКС „магистър“ with the professional qualification „Магистър – музикален продуцент“ — a genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree WHEN IT RUNS. See accreditationStatus: it does not appear in either academy's 2026/2027 admission handbook.
accreditation: CORRECTED — MATERIAL CHANGE. The programme appeared in NMA's 2025/2026 candidate handbook as a ONE-YEAR ТКДФ master's. It does NOT appear anywhere in NMA's official 2026/2027 handbook (I searched the full extracted text: the string 'продуцентство' returns zero hits, and the specialty is absent from the list of ТКДФ master's programmes and from the exam-programme sections), and it does NOT appear anywhere in AMTII's official 2026/2027 candidate handbook either. AMTII's specialty web page for it is still live but is now unsupported by either admission handbook — treat it as a stale page. On the current official evidence the programme is not being admitted to for 2026/2027.
tuition: Would have been €8,500/year if administered by NMA Sofia, or €7,600/year if administered by AMTII Plovdiv. Which schedule governed is undocumented and now moot on two independent grounds — he is ineligible, and the programme is not in either 2026/2027 handbook.
otherFees: Would have been NMA's €100 / 195.58 BGN application fee plus recognition, legalisation and translation costs.
totalCost: Not applicable.
scholarshipDetail: None open to a Tunisian national. State-funded places closed to non-EU nationals; ПМС 103/1993, 228/1997 and 264/2024 all inapplicable.
entry: DISQUALIFYING, AND CONFIRMED VERBATIM ON BOTH SITES. Entry is restricted to graduates of six named specialties: „Звукорежисура, звуков и медиен дизайн“, „Хорово дирижиране“, „Композиция“ or „Оперно-симфонично дирижиране“ of the ТКДФ at NMA Sofia; OR „Дирижиране (хорово и оркестрово)“, „Композиция“ or „Тонрежисура“ of the Faculty of Music Pedagogy at AMTII Plovdiv. A BSc Software Engineering does not qualify, and neither would most foreign music degrees — the list names specialties at these two institutions specifically.
acceptsNonMusic: NO. Explicitly excluded by a closed list of six named music specialties at two named academies. The clearest 'no' in the sweep.
portfolio: None specified — irrelevant, he cannot meet the entry condition.
audition: Single-stage interview (събеседване) on one of the four industry topics. Documents were submitted to NMA Sofia.
deadline: None published. Do not plan around this programme.
opens: No 2026/2027 window is published by either academy. The 2025/2026 route was via NMA's ТКДФ calendar.
duration: One academic year when offered. Per NMA's handbook rule, a one-year master's carries a minimum of 60 credits.
languageReq: Would have been the NMA rule: a Bulgarian-language document from a Bulgarian HEI, or NMA's written and oral Bulgarian examinations, or a preparatory year (€5,500 at NMA, €4,600 at AMTII). IELTS/TOEFL irrelevant.
study: Per the syllabus published while it ran: creation and development of the music industry; record labels — types and specifics; the music industry and contemporary technologies; national and European copyright and neighbouring-rights legislation. Reading: Tommy Swindali 'Music Production 2024+ Edition', Howard Massey 'Behind the Glass', Bobby Owsinski 'The Music Producer's Handbook', Ari Herstand 'How To Make It In The New Music Business', and the Bulgarian Copyright Act. (Note: this is the syllabus the previous record wrongly attached to NMA's Мениджмънт на музикалните индустрии.)
recommendation: DO NOT APPLY — INELIGIBLE, AND ON CURRENT EVIDENCE NO LONGER RUNNING. The previous record was right to flag this as a trap: the title 'Music Production MA, one year, Bulgaria' is exactly what he will search for and exactly what will surface. Two independent reasons to cross it off permanently. First, the published entry rule limits admission to graduates of six named music specialties at NMA Sofia and AMTII Plovdiv — a Tunisian software-engineering graduate cannot qualify now or after any portfolio year. Second, and new: the programme is absent from BOTH academies' official 2026/2027 candidate handbooks, having been listed in NMA's 2025/2026 handbook as a one-year ТКДФ master's. Only AMTII's stale specialty web page still advertises it. If a directory site or aggregator shows it, that listing is out of date. The theoretical path in — complete AMTII's Тонрежисура first, then this — is now doubly closed, because Тонрежисура itself requires a music bachelor's he does not have.

The Danish state operates a scheme of tuition waivers and scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students distributed through institutions; whether RAMA has an allocation and whether it reaches this new Aalborg programme is UNVERIFIED. The non-EU/EEA applicants page (musikkons.dk/en/programmes/admission/applicants-from-non-eu-eea-countries/) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching and must be read manually. TREAT SCHOLARSHIP AVAILABILITY AS UNCONFIRMED.
entry: VERBATIM (section 2.1 Qualifying degrees): "To be admitted to a master’s programme at RAMA, applicants must have earned a relevant bachelor’s degree or earn such a degree before starting on the master’s programme. The following bachelor’s degrees are pre-approved: Bachelor’s degree from a music academy; Bachelor’s degree from another artistic programme approved by the Danish Ministry of Culture*; Bachelor’s degree from a university musicology programme*" with the footnote "*The applicant may have to pass an extended admission test to verify that he/she possesses the skills, knowledge, or qualifications that are acquired on music academy bachelor programmes but which the applicant may not have acquired on his/her qualifying BA programme. Examples include ear training, music theory, general music skills, minor instruments, or technical disciplines." Programme-specific: a Bachelor in jazz/pop or electronic music from a music academy or university, or a Bachelor in Sound Design.
acceptsNonMusic: NO on the pre-approved list, and this is the honest read. The three pre-approved categories are all music/artistic degrees: "Bachelor’s degree from a music academy", "Bachelor’s degree from another artistic programme approved by the Danish Ministry of Culture", "Bachelor’s degree from a university musicology programme". A BSc Software Engineering is none of these. The list says these are "pre-approved", implying other degrees may be individually assessed, but the PDF does not state a dispensation route. UNVERIFIED whether RAMA will individually assess a non-music BSc. NOTE the extended-admission-test footnote covers ear training and music theory for non-conservatoire entrants — a real risk for this candidate.
portfolio: EXACT: "15-20 minutes of audio featuring works produced by the applicant. Some of the works may have been created in cooperation with others; if so, the application must clearly state who did what. The applicant is encouraged to demonstrate artistic coherence and at the same time a degree of variation". Plus a "work description: A text that briefly (maximum of two A4 pages) explains the background of the music and how it was created. Information about production location, equipment used, and any other participants must be clear"; a "CV with a particular emphasis on the applicant’s music production experience"; and the "diploma for qualifying bachelor’s degree". Audio format not specified in the PDF (UNVERIFIED).
audition: THIS IS A PRACTICAL PRODUCTION TEST, NOT A PERFORMANCE AUDITION — the single most important distinction for this candidate, and RAMA is the clearest example of it in the region. VERBATIM: "No later than 8 days prior to the admission te[s]t, the applicants receive a production assignment. The completed assignment is presented during the admission test." Test structure: total maximum 30 minutes. "Presentation (10 minutes maximum): The completed assignment is played back, and the applicant gives a presentation accounting for e.g. production methods and artistic intentions." "Interview (20 minutes maximum)" covering artistic profile, technical and artistic aspects of the application and the production assignment, "the applicant’s work methods including use of software/hardware et cetera", music production and music industry experience, background and previous education, and ambitions for the programme. Graded on: "A) The submitted works B) The presentation C) Suitability for study based on the interview and the written material submitted". NO instrument required, NO ear-training test at the master admission test itself — but the qualifying-degree footnote warns an "extended admission test" covering ear training/music theory may be imposed on non-music-academy entrants. Admission tests are scheduled for January and February. Whether the test can be taken remotely is UNVERIFIED.
deadline: 1 December 2025 at 12.00 noon for the 2026/2027 study year — PRIOR CYCLE. This is an unusually EARLY deadline (a full nine months before the intake) and much earlier than Sweden or the other Danish conservatoires. For a September 2027 start expect 1 December 2026 at noon. Admission tests January and February.
opens: UNVERIFIED — apply via www.musikkons.dk / kum.studieoptag.dk; typically opens in the autumn before the December deadline.
duration: 120 ECTS / 2 years. NEW PROGRAMME — first intake August 2025.
languageReq: English in practice. Formal English test level for non-EU applicants UNVERIFIED (page blocked).
study: VERBATIM aims: the programme "is aimed at producers who want to: work professionally with electronic music production; work independently and creatively at a high artistic level based on electronic music production; be able to complete commercial and diverse professional electronic music production assignments". scholarshipDetail: The RMC tuition page lists only EXEMPTIONS, not scholarships: "an exception is made for students who participate in: An Erasmus Mundus programme, A Fulbright or DIS programme, Other bilateral agreements", plus exemptions for foreign students with permanent Danish residency and for those under the Afghan-assistance or Ukrainian-refugee acts. entry: VERBATIM: applicants must have "completed a Bachelor degree in music from RMC, a relevant Bachelor degree in music from another Danish music conservatory, or a relevant Bachelor degree in music from a foreign music conservatory", or "expect to have completed an eligible Bachelor degree by 1 July 2026 at the latest". acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY / DOUBTFUL on paper but the artistic bar is instrument-free. The qualifying-degree clause is music-only: "Based on a specific assessment, the conservatory may recognise other artistically based Bachelors degrees in music as qualifying" — note it still says "in music". HOWEVER RMC explicitly removes the performer barrier: "Applicants do not need to participate as a musician/singer in the music examples in their portfolio, and it is not a requirement to be able to play an instrument - the conservatory also accepts applicants who work exclusively on computers." A BSc Software Engineering would need a dispensation on the degree requirement — UNVERIFIED whether RMC grants this.
portfolio: EXACT (Round 1): "2-3 music examples" composed, arranged AND produced by the applicant, total duration "10 min.", mp3 format. Optional sheet music / graphic notation / text as pdf. HARD CONSTRAINT: "A minimum of one-third of the music submitted in your portfolio must be composed for and performed by others." Supplementary text: max 500 keystrokes per music example on the creation process, max 250 keystrokes per music example on roles. "All material must be composed, arranged and produced by you. Co-writes are not permitted." Round 1 scored out of 100; minimum 40/100 to advance. RMC selects two to three times as many applicants for round 2 as it admits.
audition: TWO ROUNDS. Round 1 is portfolio-only, no attendance. Round 2 is an IN-PERSON exam at RMC in Copenhagen, approx. 25 minutes: 10 min work presentation (live performance, recording, OR a combination — a recording alone is permitted, so no instrument is strictly needed), 5 min oral presentation of working methods, 10 min interview. Max 5 musicians including sound engineer if performing live. NOT a classical performance audition and NOT an ear-training test — it is a portfolio defence with an optional live element. CRITICAL LOGISTICS: "Exams cannot be conducted via video streaming unless explicitly stated for a specific programme" — so a Schengen visit visa and travel to Copenhagen is likely required for Round 2.

correction: Two significant corrections. (1) The record's gate 'Exam/interview only' misses that DKDM runs NO LIVE ENTRANCE EXAM AT ALL for master's — no ear test, no audition, no set task for tonmeisters. The gate is two submitted productions (one rhythmic, one classical, each at least 7 minutes) plus a production plan for non-EU applicants and a 20-minute discussion. Contrary to the Tonmeister stereotype, the assessment is not what closes this door. (2) The record omits the closed prerequisite that does close it — 'Bachelor of Music as tonemeister' — and omits the live 2027 deadline: 1 December 2026 for the autumn 2027 intake, which is the single most time-critical date found in this slice.
qualification: MMus (kandidat i musik)
tuition: EUR 11,100 per academic year for the Tonmeister/Sound Engineer MASTER (non-EU/EEA), paid in two instalments: 1 June (new students) and 1 September. Free for EU/EEA. For comparison the master fee table runs EUR 11,000-14,900 across specialisations.

entry: Bachelor as Tonemester from DKDM, or Bachelor as Tonemester or equivalent from a Danish music conservatory, or Bachelor as Tonemester or equivalent from a higher education institution abroad at a level corresponding to DKDM. RDAM's general prerequisites page states a "Bachelor's degree in music ... or equivalent from a higher education institution abroad at a level equivalent to RDAM".
acceptsNonMusic: NO. The published requirement is a Tonmeister bachelor or an equivalent conservatory-level music degree. A BSc Software Engineering does not meet this and no discretionary clause is offered on the pages read. This is the best-fitting curriculum in the whole slice and the hardest gate - he would need a music/audio bachelor or a documented equivalent first.
portfolio: Two musical production examples, EACH at least 7 minutes: one from the rhythmic genres (pop/rock/jazz) and one from classical music. Non-EU/EEA applicants must ADDITIONALLY submit a production plan documenting the creative process - timeline, equipment/software used, roles of participants and the recording context. (The certified audiogram, max 1 year old, is a Bachelor-level requirement, not master.)
audition: Principal-study audition of approximately 30 minutes including assessment, built around a roughly 20-minute discussion of the submitted works plus theoretical and practical questions on your "technical and musical standpoint". EU/EEA applicants audition IN PERSON; non-EU/EEA applicants audition ONLINE, with a possible additional interview covering piano, ear training/solfege and theory. Graded on the Danish 7-point scale; decision based on documentation of previous education plus evaluation of the submitted productions.
deadline: 1 December for both EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA applicants at Master level - PRIOR CYCLE date pattern, confirm the 2027-intake date. RDAM aims to answer non-EU/EEA Bachelor and Master applicants about six weeks after the deadline.
opens: UNVERIFIED (portal opening date not published on the pages read)

study: Principal study is music production and recording techniques, organised in close collaboration with the Danish Broadcasting Corporation (DR). Alongside: aural studies, basic piano, music theory and music history. Semester projects, set productions, studio recordings, CD recordings, film sound design and PA work for performances. Students can specialise by genre, sector, producer role or sound-technician role. "Well-equipped studios and plenty of mobile equipment." Study trips, masterclasses, company visits and listening tests.
recommendation: Content-wise this is the classic Nordic recording/production master - DR collaboration, real studios, both rhythmic and classical production, and non-EU applicants audition online so no travel cost. The deal-breaker is entry: it presumes a Tonmeister bachelor. Also note the portfolio demands a CLASSICAL production of 7+ minutes, which a DJ/electronic producer will not have. Realistic only after a bridging audio-engineering bachelor.

recommendation: A credible, well-established school and a fair 1,200 hours for the money — but the wrong programme for THIS candidate, and I would not put it ahead of the alternatives. The decisive issue is fit, not price: two of the five modules are compulsory instrumental performance with ensemble playing and classical harmony/notation, and he has no instrumental training whatsoever. This is a musician's production master, and he would spend a third of the year fighting a deficit rather than building the electronic-production and DJ craft he actually wants. Layered on top: CEV itself concedes the award has no equivalence in Spanish university education, publishes no ECTS, no entry requirements, no fees and no scholarship figures on its own site, and says nothing about visas. Its structural advantage — 1,200 in-person hours, which is the only programme here that plainly clears the 20-hours-a-week visa threshold — is real and worth noting, but it does not outweigh a fundamental content mismatch. accreditation: NOT NVAO-ACCREDITED. VERIFIED, in the school's own words: 'Alle opleidingen van Master The Mix Academy zijn officieel geregistreerd beroepsonderwijs, CRKBO-geregistreerd en gecertificeerd met het NRTO-keurmerk voor kwaliteit.' READ THAT CAREFULLY — 'officieel geregistreerd beroepsonderwijs' means officially REGISTERED vocational education, which is NOT the same as an accredited higher-education programme. CRKBO is a register for short vocational training that confers VAT exemption; NRTO is the quality mark of the private-training TRADE ASSOCIATION. Neither is NVAO accreditation and neither produces a recognised Dutch degree. The institution is private and 'niet-bekostigd'. NAMING CAUTION: 'Master The Mix Academy' will surface in any search for a 'master' in music production — it is not one, and the word 'officieel' in its own marketing makes the confusion worse.

The prior entry asserted that 'NO mestrado or pós-graduação in sound, audio, music production or music technology could be identified' and that Lusíada has no music presence whatsoever. That second half is FALSE and had to be corrected. Universidade Lusíada de Lisboa (DGES record estab=2410) runs (a) a LICENCIATURA EM JAZZ E MÚSICA MODERNA — a DGES-registered official first-cycle degree, 6 semestres / 180 ECTS, 31 vacancies in the 2026 national access competition, specialising in jazz or modern music (pop/rock), and (b) a MESTRADO EM MUSICOTERAPIA — an official 2-year / 120 ECTS second-cycle degree, described as the only music-therapy master's in Portugal, modelled on the American training model, still actively examining theses in July 2026. So Lusíada HAS a music department. What it does NOT have is any music-PRODUCTION, sound-engineering, studio or electronic-music programme. The conclusion for him is unchanged; the reasoning behind it is now correct.

It trains therapists who use music to treat patients (published theses cover music therapy for adults with cerebral palsy and for adults with disabilities in institutional settings). recommendation: RULE OUT — but for a corrected reason. The prior draft's claim that Lusíada has no music provision at all was wrong and would have been an embarrassing thing to tell him if he later found the jazz degree. The accurate position: Lusíada Lisboa HAS music — a Licenciatura em Jazz e Música Moderna (180 ECTS) and a Mestrado em Musicoterapia (120 ECTS) — but NOTHING in music production, sound engineering, studio work or electronic music. The Musicoterapia master is doubly closed to him: his software-engineering bachelor is outside the listed eligible fields, and the programme states it is 'essential' to have at least a year of music training plus instrumental practice, tested at interview. The jazz licenciatura is a bachelor's, which he already has at a different subject, and would require passing an instrumental aptitude test. THE PRACTICAL WARNING FROM THE PRIOR DRAFT STANDS AND IS REINFORCED: LUSÍADA and LUSÓFONA are different universities with confusingly similar names, and the confusion is now doubly dangerous because Lusíada genuinely does have music programmes — so a search that surfaces 'Lusíada' plus 'música' will look plausible. LUSÓFONA (Campo Grande, Lisbon) is the one with the sound department, the A3ES-accredited Mestrado em Produção e Tecnologias do Som (120 ECTS, Pro Tools / Max-MSP / Arduino), the pós-graduação in Produção e Tecnologia do Som, the Atmos room and the ReSound Erasmus Mundus master.
